measure_name: Free-roaming dogs surrounding Liziping Reserve
what_it_represents: Free-roaming domestic dogs as an opportunity for contact between domestic dogs and wildlife in and near giant panda reserves.
measurement_method: A comprehensive survey in six village groups surrounding Liziping Reserve.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive evidence summarized in this review; not used by this paper in a statistical analysis.
quantitative_result: 64% (212/334) of dogs were free-roaming.
evidence_quote: A comprehensive survey in six village groups surrounding Liziping Reserve found 64% (212/334) of dogs were free-roaming(11).

measure_name: Panda habitat within stray-dog roaming range
what_it_represents: Spatial overlap between panda habitat and the roaming range of stray domestic dogs.
measurement_method: Not stated in the supplied text.
metric_or_unit: 40% of panda habitat
role_in_analysis: Descriptive evidence summarized in this review; not used by this paper in a statistical analysis.
quantitative_result: 40% of panda habitat falls within the roaming range of stray dogs.
evidence_quote: Across all panda reserves, 40% of panda habitat falls within the roaming range of stray dogs.

measure_name: Frequency of reported infectious agents and parasites by domestic livestock and wild ruminants
what_it_represents: The frequency of infectious-agent and parasite reports/mentions, presented separately for domestic livestock and wild ruminants.
measurement_method: Compilation of peer-reviewed literature and WOAH-WAHIS database records, presented by taxon/functional group.
metric_or_unit: Total number of reports/mentions.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of reported infectious agents and parasites across domestic livestock and wild ruminants.
quantitative_result: Only six publications (3.0%) reported infectious agents in wildlife.
evidence_quote: Frequency of reported infectious agents and parasites in domestic livestock and wild ruminants in countries of interest from peer-reviewed literature and WOAH-WAHIS database, by taxon/functional group. Results are presented over a total number of reports/mentions, not over the number of studies or records.

measure_name: Bird origin category
what_it_represents: Whether the H10 AIV isolate originated from wild or domestic waterbirds, including wild and domestic mallards.
measurement_method: Virus isolates were classified by bird origin in Table 1 during sample collection.
metric_or_unit: Categorical (W, wild; D, domestic)
role_in_analysis: Used to distinguish wild- and domestic-origin mallard H10N7 isolates in the phylogenetic interpretation.
quantitative_result: Three wild-mallard H10N7 viruses were closely related to one domestic-mallard H10N7 strain.
evidence_quote: Interestingly, the HA genes of these three H10N7 viruses isolated from wild mallards in December 2005 and January 2006 were closely related to that of the H10N7 strain isolated from domestic mallards in July 2005.

measure_name: HA nucleotide identity
what_it_represents: Genetic relatedness of H10 HA sequences, including viruses from wild and domestic mallards.
measurement_method: Nucleotide sequence identity was analysed using BLAST results from GISAID.
metric_or_unit: Percent nucleotide identity
role_in_analysis: Supported phylogenetic comparison of virus isolates across wild and domestic mallard origins.
quantitative_result: The four H10N7 isolates, including the domestic-mallard isolate and three wild-mallard isolates, each had 98–99% nucleotide identity with A/H10N7 A/Shoveler/Egypt/09781-NAMRU3/2004.
evidence_quote: The other four H10N7 isolates, A/Mallard/Italy/166998/2005, A/Mallard/Italy/Eco-634/2005, A/Mallard/Italy/Eco-33/2006, and A/Mallard/Italy/Eco-7/2006 clustered together (Figure 2), and all of them showed the highest nucleotide identity with A/H10N7 A/Shoveler/Egypt/09781-NAMRU3/2004 (98–99%—BLAST result) (Table 2).

measure_name: Parasite prevalence by host species
what_it_represents: The proportion of each host population infected with at least one trematode egg, reported across wildlife, domestic animals, and humans sampled at forest–oil palm interface areas.
measurement_method: Microscopy of fecal samples; prevalence was calculated as the proportion infected with at least one trematode egg.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%) and infected/total samples.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of infection occurrence and prevalence among host species frequenting the interface.
quantitative_result: Leopard cats had 75% prevalence (3/4), Asian palm civets had 72.2% (13/18), domestic dogs had 60% (3/5), domestic cats had 100% (1/1), long-tailed macaques had 10% (1/10), and humans had 77.7% (7/9).
evidence_quote: Table 1. Prevalence and abundance of trematode eggs found in feces of wildlife, domestic animals and humans, as detected through microscopy

measure_name: Eggs per gram of feces (EPG) by host species
what_it_represents: Trematode egg output in feces from wildlife, domestic animals, and humans sampled in interface areas.
measurement_method: Calculated from the average of 5 replicate counts of observed trematode eggs under a McMaster chamber’s grid.
metric_or_unit: EPG (mean ± S.D.); reported ranges and means.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of parasite egg output among sampled host species.
quantitative_result: Domestic dogs had the highest reported mean EPG, 7126.7 ± 12 232.9, with a range of 55–21 252 EPG.
evidence_quote: Dogs had the highest parasite egg output in this study, suggesting that infected individuals can end up contributing significantly to parasite environmental pollution, and highlighting the importance of including domestic

measure_name: Host species/domain comparison of pathogen seroprevalence and incidence
what_it_represents: Comparison of infection or exposure patterns between domestic cattle and wild ruminants at the domestic–wild ruminant interface.
measurement_method: Serological testing for pestiviruses, BRSV, BoHV-1 and MTC, and SITT for MTC in cattle; proportions positive were compared between host species using chi-square or Fisher's tests.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence/incidence (%) and p-values
role_in_analysis: Tested differences in infection rates between domestic and wild host species.
quantitative_result: Respiratory-virus seroprevalence was higher in cattle than wild ruminants (p < .001); no difference in MTC was detected between domestic and wild ruminant species (p = .674).
evidence_quote: Statistically significant higher seroprevalence to respiratory viruses was detected in cattle (p < .001) compared to wild ruminants, showing a P-­value of 0.065 for pestiviruses and p < .001 for both BRSV and BoHV-­1. Among cattle, differences in seroprevalence to viral agents were not found between males and females (p = .141), but were higher in adult animals compared to the remaining age classes in the case of BRSV (p < .001) and BoHV-­1 (p = .003). Additionally, a positive correlation (p < .001) was found between BRSV and BoHV-­1 seropositivity. For MTC, no differences between domestic and wild ruminant species were detected (p = .674) nor between deer species themselves (p = .528).

measure_name: Pathogen transmission-route category
what_it_represents: Selected pathogens grouped by primarily close versus non-close direct-contact transmission routes in a domestic–wild ruminant setting.
measurement_method: Pestiviruses, BRSV and BoHV-1 were classified as mainly close-contact pathogens, and MTC as a non-close-contact pathogen, then evaluated in cattle and wild ruminant populations.
metric_or_unit: Categorical transmission route (close or non-close contact)
role_in_analysis: Structured the study hypothesis and pathogen evaluation at the interface.
quantitative_result: The paper found viral exposure in cattle but not wild ruminants, whereas MTC incidence in cattle and MTC seroprevalence in wild ruminants were similar.
evidence_quote: The wild ruminant population of DNP showed no seropositivity to the analysed respiratory viruses.

measure_name: Mesostigmatid mite prevalence by host group
what_it_represents: Occurrence of mesostigmatid mites in adult wild birds, wild bird broods, and laying hens at poultry farms.
measurement_method: Prevalence was calculated as the proportion of hosts infested; for nestlings, the brood was the study unit.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%)
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of mite occurrence across wild and domestic host groups.
quantitative_result: Adult wild birds had 30% prevalence, wild bird broods 45%, and laying hens 32%.
evidence_quote: Prevalence of mesostigmatid mites and identified species found on different host groups on poultry farms from central Argentina.

measure_name: 16S rRNA sequence comparison between poultry and wild-bird mites
what_it_represents: Genetic similarity of O. sylviarum collected from poultry and wild birds, relevant to potential cross-transmission between hosts.
measurement_method: Mitochondrial 16S rRNA gene sequences obtained from PCR products were compared.
metric_or_unit: Sequence identity (%)
role_in_analysis: Assessment of potential cross-transmission between wild birds and hens.
quantitative_result: Sequences from mites collected from wild birds and laying hens showed 99.7–100 % identity with the corresponding GenBank sequence, and the analysed fragment was identical between poultry and wild-bird samples.
evidence_quote: The fact that the sequences of the 16S rRNA gene fragment analysed were identical when comparing samples from poultry and samples from wild birds suggests a potential cross-transmission between passerines and hens.

measure_name: TB-positive status by combinations of red deer, wild boar, and cattle
what_it_represents: Municipal co-occurrence of TB-positive status across wild ungulates and cattle.
measurement_method: Municipalities were classified according to whether they were TB positive in red deer (RD), wild boar (WB), cattle (Bov), or combinations of these hosts in 2006 and 2007.
metric_or_unit: Number of municipalities; percentage of TB-infected regions with cases in more than one species.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive assessment of a potential multi-species interaction scenario; the paper states that host-variable interactions were not included in the final model.
quantitative_result: Many TB-infected regions presented TB cases in more than one species (44.19% in 2006 and 28.86% in 2007).
evidence_quote: Ciudad Real municipalities with this scenario are an exception (9 out of 113) and many TB-infected regions presented TB cases in more than one species (44.19% in 2006 and 28.86% in 2007) (Table 2).

measure_name: Guineafowl host category (domestic versus wild)
what_it_represents: The comparison between domestic guineafowls sampled in villages at the GMA periphery and wild guineafowls sampled at the Mulela plains-Ila forest interface.
measurement_method: Cross-sectional monthly sampling from November 2010 to October 2011, followed by comprehensive necropsy.
metric_or_unit: 148 domestic and 50 wild guineafowls
role_in_analysis: Grouping variable for comparisons of helminth infection measures between wild and domestic guineafowls.
quantitative_result: Domestic guineafowls had higher mean helminth species richness than wild guineafowls.
evidence_quote: Mean helminth species per host was 4.177 (SD: 1.654; Range: 1–7; CI: 3.91–4.44) for domestic fowls and 3.40 (SD: 1.107; Range: 1–5; CI: 2.92–3.88) for wild fowls. There was an overall difference in mean species richness between domestic and wild fowls (ANOVA F1,197 = 5.10, P = 0.025).

measure_name: Helminth species richness by domestic versus wild host group
what_it_represents: The number of helminth species discovered per host, compared across domestic and wild guineafowls.
measurement_method: “Parasite richness was determined by enumerating the number of helminth species discovered per host.”
metric_or_unit: Mean species per host; ANOVA F1,197; P value
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of parasite species richness between the domestic and wild host domains.
quantitative_result: Mean species richness was 4.177 in domestic fowls and 3.40 in wild fowls, with an overall difference (P = 0.025).
evidence_quote: Mean helminth species per host was 4.177 (SD: 1.654; Range: 1–7; CI: 3.91–4.44) for domestic fowls and 3.40 (SD: 1.107; Range: 1–5; CI: 2.92–3.88) for wild fowls. There was an overall difference in mean species richness between domestic and wild fowls (ANOVA F1,197 = 5.10, P = 0.025).

measure_name: Mean total nematode burden per bird by domestic versus wild host group
what_it_represents: The intensity of nematode infection in domestic and wild guineafowls.
measurement_method: Nematode helminths recovered from each gastrointestinal tract section were “identified and counted individually to get the actual worm burdens.”
metric_or_unit: Mean ± SD nematode burden; 95% confidence interval; ANOVA F1,197; P value
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of infection burden between domestic and wild fowls.
quantitative_result: There was no difference in mean total nematode burden per bird between domestic and wild fowls (P = 0.69).
evidence_quote: There was also no difference in mean total nematode burden per bird between domestic and wild fowls (ANOVA F1,197 = 0.16, P = 0.69, mean ± SD of overall domestic nematode burden 113.72 ± 91.32, CI: 98.9–128.6; mean ± SD of overall wild nematode burden 108.04 ± 75.40, CI: 76.6–139.5) and neither was there a difference in mean total nematode burden per bird between domestic and wild fowls.

measure_name: Proportion positive for individual helminth species by domestic versus wild host group
what_it_represents: Prevalence/proportion of guineafowls infested with each helminth species in domestic and wild groups.
measurement_method: Chi-square testing of the proportions of helminth-species positives between wild and domestic guineafowls.
metric_or_unit: Proportion positive; Chi-square test; P value
role_in_analysis: Tests differences in helminth-species positivity between the domestic and wild host groups.
quantitative_result: Significant differences in positive proportion were found for R. echinobothrida, R. cesticillus, A. galli, A. suctoria, G. ingluvicola and Heterakis spp.
evidence_quote: There were significant differences in positive proportion per helminth species between wild and domestic fowls with R. echinobothrida, R. cesticillus, A. galli, A. suctoria, G. ingluvicola and Heterakis spp.

measure_name: Proximity to livestock
what_it_represents: The distance of wildlife sampling sites from livestock-associated boundaries, representing wildlife-livestock proximity.
measurement_method: Sites within Serengeti NP, eastern MMNR and the Mara Triangle were categorised by distance from the boundary; NCA and Loliondo GCA sites were categorised as <10 km from livestock because they were multi-use areas.
metric_or_unit: <10 km or >10 km from the boundary
role_in_analysis: Used to explore the association between proximity to livestock and serological status.
evidence_quote: To explore the association between proximity to livestock and serological status, sites within Serengeti NP, eastern MMNR (defined as the part of the MMNR to the east of the Mara Triangle) and the Mara Triangle were categorised by their distance from the boundary (<10 km or >10 km from the boundary). All other sites in NCA and Loliondo GCA were multi-use areas and therefore categorised as <10 km from livestock.

measure_name: Free-roaming
what_it_represents: Dogs allowed to roam in streets and natural areas, representing opportunity for contact with wild carnivores.
measurement_method: Owner questionnaire; included as an explanatory variable in logistic regression.
role_in_analysis: Risk factor for CDV exposure in domestic dogs.
quantitative_result: Free-roaming was a significant risk factor for CDV exposure.
evidence_quote: Free-roaming was defined as dogs allowed to roam freely on the streets and natural area.

measure_name: Free-roaming dogs
what_it_represents: An ownership and movement category used as a risk factor for exposure to CDV.
measurement_method: Logistic regression model.
role_in_analysis: Predictive parameter in the logistic regression model estimating risk factors for CDV exposure.
quantitative_result: Free-roaming is a risk factor for CDV exposure.
evidence_quote: The logistic regression model (Table 3) revealed that free-roaming is a risk factor for CDV exposure (OR = 3.05, p < 0.05)

measure_name: Recognition of interactions between free-roaming dogs and wild carnivores
what_it_represents: Questionnaire-reported interactions between domestic dogs and wild carnivores across study towns.
measurement_method: Cross-sectional household questionnaire.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of recognition of interactions: 40%, 40%, 35%, and 25% by town.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of reported dog–wild-carnivore interactions among locations.
quantitative_result: PV and MV had the highest reported recognition of interactions (40% each).
evidence_quote: According to the questionnaire results, interactions between free-roaming dogs and wild carnivores were mentioned in all locations. PV and MV were the towns with the highest percentage of recognition of interactions (40% and 40%, respectively), followed by CJ (35%) and ESP (25%).

measure_name: Sample location: within the reserve versus outside the reserve
what_it_represents: Comparison of rabies positivity among domestic dogs in the wildlife reserve versus dogs sampled outside the reserve.
measurement_method: Rabies brain samples were tested for lyssavirus antigen using the direct fluorescent antibody test (FAT); dogs were classified by whether they were sampled within or outside the reserve.
metric_or_unit: Percentage positive; odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence interval; Chi-square test.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of dog rabies test positivity across reserve and non-reserve settings.
quantitative_result: Dogs inside the reserve had a higher positivity proportion than dogs outside it (65.3% versus 45.5%); OR = 2.26 (95% CI: 1.27–4.03).
evidence_quote: The odds of a dog sampled from within the reserve being positive for rabies was 2.26 times greater than for a dog sampled outside the reserve (95% confidence interval CI: 1.27–4.03).

measure_name: Distance to villages
what_it_represents: Spatial proximity of dogs detected in the wildlife reserve to villages bordering the reserve.
measurement_method: Distance in kilometers from each georeferenced dog record to the nearest village was calculated using the “Generate near table” tool in ArcMap; association with rabies test status was analysed by logistic regression.
metric_or_unit: Distance (km); odds ratio with 95% confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Spatial predictor in univariable and multivariable logistic regression of dog rabies test status in the reserve.
quantitative_result: Dogs were more likely to test positive if shot further from villages (OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.18–1.71).
evidence_quote: Dogs were more likely to test positive for rabies if they were shot further from villages (odds ratio 1.42, 95% CI 1.18–1.71) and closer to water points (0.41, 95% CI 0.21–0.81).

measure_name: Distance to water points
what_it_represents: Spatial proximity of dogs detected in the wildlife reserve to water points within the reserve.
measurement_method: Distance in kilometers from each georeferenced dog record to the nearest water point was calculated using the “Generate near table” tool in ArcMap; association with rabies test status was analysed by logistic regression.
metric_or_unit: Distance (km); odds ratio with 95% confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Spatial predictor in univariable and multivariable logistic regression of dog rabies test status in the reserve.
quantitative_result: Dogs were more likely to test positive when shot closer to water points (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21–0.81).
evidence_quote: Dogs were more likely to test positive for rabies if they were shot further from villages (odds ratio 1.42, 95% CI 1.18–1.71) and closer to water points (0.41, 95% CI 0.21–0.81).

measure_name: Reported contacts between cattle and wildlife
what_it_represents: Wildlife-cattle contact in grazing areas and at watering points in the CNP and OD interfaces.
measurement_method: A face-to-face farmer questionnaire, with contact defined as wildlife and cattle grazing together in an area the size of a football field.
metric_or_unit: Comparative proportions; P < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Compared reported contacts between the CNP and OD interfaces.
quantitative_result: Contacts with wildlife were reported more frequently in CNP than OD, both in grazing areas and at watering points.
evidence_quote: Contacts with wildlife were also mentioned more frequently in the CNP than in the OD interface, both in grazing areas and at watering points (Fig. 2).

measure_name: BTB prevalence by livestock/wildlife interface
what_it_represents: BTB reactor prevalence in cattle sampled at the OD and CNP interfaces.
measurement_method: Cattle were tested with the interferon-gamma assay (IFN-c) and apparent individual animal and herd prevalence were calculated.
metric_or_unit: Individual animal prevalence: 0.7% (3/449) in OD and 2.4% (9/369) in CNP; P < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Compared apparent individual animal and herd prevalence between cattle from the two interface study areas.
quantitative_result: Apparent individual animal prevalence and herd prevalence were both significantly higher in the CNP interface than in the OD interface.
evidence_quote: Apparent individual animal prevalence and herd prevalence were both significantly higher in the CNP interface than in the OD interface (P < 0.05).

measure_name: Apparent pestivirus seroprevalence by animal species and district
what_it_represents: The prevalence of pestivirus antibodies in domestic sheep and wild ruminants, including chamois, in the study districts.
measurement_method: Pestivirus-specific antibodies against the NS3 protein were investigated using a commercial blocking ELISA; apparent prevalence confidence intervals were estimated using a binomial exact distribution and prevalence was compared between species and districts using Fisher’s exact test.
metric_or_unit: Apparent seroprevalence (%), with 95% CI
role_in_analysis: Comparison of pestivirus antibody prevalence between wild and domestic species and among districts.
quantitative_result: Pestivirus seroprevalence in sheep was significantly higher for all districts in comparison with chamois (P < 0.0001).
evidence_quote: Pestivirus seroprevalence in sheep was significantly higher for all districts in comparison with chamois (P < 0.0001).

measure_name: Nucleotide identity of chamois and sheep pestivirus isolates
what_it_represents: Genetic similarity between a pestivirus strain isolated from chamois and one isolated from sheep in the same valley.
measurement_method: Phylogenetic analysis of the Npro genes and analysis of the 5′ UTR sequence.
metric_or_unit: Percent nucleotide identity in the 5′-UTR region
role_in_analysis: Evidence used to assess possible cross-contamination and infer interspecies transmission.
quantitative_result: The chamois RUPI-05 strain and sheep 10F03356 strain showed 92% nucleotide identity in the 5′-UTR region.
evidence_quote: They also showed 92% of nucleotides identity in the 5′-UTR region (data not shown).

measure_name: Distance from mink farm
what_it_represents: Proximity of free-ranging mink to mink farms.
measurement_method: For the large-scale analysis, distance was calculated between the mink’s township and the nearest township with a mink farm; for the Niagara small-scale analysis, it was the distance from the capture site to the mink farm.
metric_or_unit: km at the small scale; township-to-nearest-farm-township distance at the large scale.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in logistic-regression candidate models explaining AD seroprevalence.
quantitative_result: Seronegative mink were caught, on average, 10 km from the mink farm, whereas seropositive mink were caught an average of 4.5 km from the mink farm.
evidence_quote: Seronegative mink were caught, on average, 10 km (95% CI, 13.1 – 7.4 km) from the mink farm. Seropositive individuals were caught an average of 4.5 km (CI, 6.5 – 2.5 km) from the mink farm.

measure_name: Mink genotype (domestic, hybrid or wild)
what_it_represents: Genetic assignment of free-ranging mink to domestic, hybrid, or wild population clusters.
measurement_method: Mink were genotyped and assigned to population clusters using a minimum membership probability of q≥0.80; animals with q<0.80 for both groups were considered hybrids.
metric_or_unit: Three levels: 0 = wild, 1 = hybrid, and 2 = domestic.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in logistic regression of AD antibody status and comparison of AD prevalence among domestic, hybrid, and wild mink.
quantitative_result: Hybrid mink had 44% seroprevalence, free-ranging domestic mink had 38%, and wild mink had 28%; the trend was not statistically significant.
evidence_quote: Hybrid mink had the highest seroprevalence (44% or 10/23), followed by free-ranging domestic mink (38% or 8/21) and wild mink with the lowest seroprevalence AD (28% or 42/164); however, this trend was not statistically significant (x2 = 3.94, p = 0.142).

measure_name: Wildlife-dog interactions
what_it_represents: Household-reported contact between domestic dogs and wild animal species, represented by dogs fighting with wildlife.
measurement_method: A total of 202 households within the area were randomly selected and visited to collect information on wildlife abundance and habits, and for wildlife-domestic dog interactions.
metric_or_unit: Percent and number of households reporting fights; frequency of fights.
role_in_analysis: Used to assess the potential for dog-wildlife contact and interpret the frequency of contact between dogs and wild carnivores.
quantitative_result: Seventy-one percent (143 of 202) of households reported having heard or witnessed dogs fighting with wild animals, and 70% reported hearing fights at least weekly.
evidence_quote: Seventy-one percent (143 of 202) of the households reported having heard or witnessed dogs fighting with unspecified wild animal species; 70% reported having heard the fights at least weekly.

measure_name: Rabies fluorescent antibody test results by domestic and wild species
what_it_represents: Rabies-positive and rabies-negative specimens compared across domestic animal and wildlife species.
measurement_method: The collected head specimens from rabies-suspect animals and road-kills were placed in a polythene bag and stored in a freezer at the Kibwezi Divisional Veterinary Office before transportation, in transport kits provided by the WHO, to the Central Veterinary Laboratory in Kabete, Nairobi, for rabies diagnosis using the fluorescent antibody test (FAT) according to the method described by Kissling (1975);
metric_or_unit: Numbers of positive and negative specimens by species; percent of positive specimens from domestic dogs.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare rabies detection in domestic animals and wildlife and assess whether wildlife could be involved in rabies transmission.
quantitative_result: Twenty-two (39%) of the collected specimens were positive for rabies on FAT, of which 91% were from domestic dogs; none of the nine wildlife specimens were positive.
evidence_quote: Twenty-two (39%) of the collected specimens were positive for rabies on FAT out of which 91% were from domestic dogs (Table 2). None of the 9 wildlife specimens were positive for rabies.
section: 3.5. Rabies cases detected by active surveillance

measure_name: Proximity of soft-tick-containing rodent burrows to pig pens
what_it_represents: The spatial proximity of soft ticks to domestic pig pens.
measurement_method: Inspection of pig farms for soft ticks and observation of the location of rodent burrows containing ticks relative to pig pens.
metric_or_unit: 95% of cases; 25% at less than 10 m
role_in_analysis: Descriptive assessment of potential contact opportunities between soft ticks and domestic pigs.
quantitative_result: Soft ticks were in rodent burrows close to pig pens in 95% of cases, with 25% less than 10 m from pig pens.
evidence_quote: In 95% of cases, soft ticks were found inside rodent burrows situated close (25% at less than 10 m) to pig pens.

measure_name: Anti-O. moubata salival gland antibodies in bushpigs and domestic pigs
what_it_represents: Exposure of wild bushpigs and domestic pigs to O. moubata.
measurement_method: ELISA testing of bushpig and pig sera for antibodies against O. moubata salival glands.
metric_or_unit: 27 bushpig sera; 273 pig sera; 51% positive pig sera; 7% highly positive
role_in_analysis: Cross-host assessment of tick exposure relevant to the potential wild-host/tick/domestic-pig cycle.
quantitative_result: All 27 bushpig sera were negative, while 51% of 273 pig sera were positive and 7% were highly positive.
evidence_quote: The 27 bushpig sera were found negative for O. moubata salival gland antibodies. Out of the 273 pig sera tested against O. moubata salival gland antibodies, 51% were found positive, among which 7% were highly positive.

measure_name: Frequency distribution of spoligotypes shared across hosts
what_it_represents: The proportion of M. bovis spoligotypes detected in wild pigs that were also reported in cattle, domestic pigs, wildlife, or humans in Argentina.
measurement_method: MTC isolates from wild pigs were spoligotyped and compared with the online public database and the local database.
metric_or_unit: Percentage and count of 12 reported spoligotypes.
role_in_analysis: Used to support the interpretation that wild pigs may be reservoirs and spreaders of mTB among host species.
quantitative_result: 75% (9/12) were shared with cattle, 58% (7/12) with domestic pigs, 50% (6/12) with wildlife, and 42% (5/12) with human isolates.
evidence_quote: In this study, 75% (9/12) of the reported spoligotypes were shared with cattle, 58% (7/12) with domestic pigs, 50% (6/12) with wildlife, and 42% (5/12) with strains isolated from humans in Argentina (Table 2).

measure_name: mTB prevalence in wild pigs and cattle by sampled county
what_it_represents: Comparison of mTB prevalence between wild pigs sampled in each county and cattle in the same areas.
measurement_method: Wild-pig prevalence was estimated using Monte Carlo simulations; cattle prevalence was based on SENASA-reported detection of tuberculous-like lesions in slaughtered cattle.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence percentage, with standard deviation and 95% confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Used to assess whether mTB prevalence was correlated between wild pigs and cattle across sampled counties.
quantitative_result: mTB prevalence was not strongly correlated between wild pigs and cattle, and was significantly higher in wild pigs.
evidence_quote: In our study, mTB prevalence is not strongly correlated between wild pigs and cattle (Table 3), being the prevalence in wild pigs significantly higher than that reported for cattle.

measure_name: Occurrence estimates of E. coli serovars by host
what_it_represents: Frequency of isolation of E. coli serogroups in pastoral cattle and Kafue lechwe, which compares the wild and domestic hosts sharing the study setting.
measurement_method: Faecal samples from lechwe antelopes and pastoral cattle were cultured for E. coli, and isolates were serogrouped using commercially available E. coli antisera.
metric_or_unit: Frequency of isolation, n (%)
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of E. coli serogroup occurrence between pastoral cattle and Kafue lechwe.
quantitative_result: O125 was isolated from 4 (2.8) pastoral-cattle isolates and 6 (5.8) Kafue-lechwe isolates.
evidence_quote: Table 3. Occurrence estimates of Escherichia coli serovars from Kafue lechwe and pastoral cattle.

measure_name: Probability of contact between cattle and buffalo outside KNP (Pcoo)
what_it_represents: The probability that a buffalo and at least one animal in a cattle herd are in contact outside KNP.
measurement_method: Questionnaire of 113 cattle farmers adjacent to the KNP fence; contact was defined as buffalo and cattle in a common area of approximately 0.7 ha, then modelled using a Beta distribution and cattle-herd size.
metric_or_unit: Probability; mean 0.005, 90% confidence interval [0.001; 0.013].
role_in_analysis: Input modelling buffalo-cattle contact outside KNP and FMD transmission risk.
quantitative_result: Probability of contact between a buffalo and a susceptible cattle outside KNP(Pcoo ). 0.005 [0.001; 0.013]

what_it_represents: The probability that an individual from a cattle herd contacts at least one individual of a buffalo herd inside KNP.
measurement_method: Questionnaires of small-scale farmers recorded cattle entering KNP for drinking; fence-worker questionnaires recorded buffalo-cattle contacts and contact duration; the parameter was modelled with Beta distributions and buffalo-herd size.
metric_or_unit: Probability; mean 0.007, 90% confidence interval [0.04–0.03].
role_in_analysis: Input modelling buffalo-cattle contact inside KNP and FMD transmission risk.
quantitative_result: Probability of contact between a buffalo and a susceptible cattle inside KNP (Pcoi ). 0.007 [0.04–0.03]

measure_name: Annual probability of at least one cattle becoming infected at the KNP wildlife/livestock interface (P(Icbz ))
what_it_represents: Combined annual risk that at least one bovine becomes infected with FMDV through the buffalo-cattle transmission scenarios inside or outside KNP.
measurement_method: Stochastic model combining the probability of infection from buffalo escaping KNP and cattle entering KNP and contacting buffalo.
metric_or_unit: Probability; mean 0.18, 90% confidence interval [0.045; 0.47].
role_in_analysis: Final quantified model output comparing and combining wild-domestic transmission scenarios.

measure_name: Poultry-farm location inside or outside wild-waterfowl habitat isopleths concurrent with an HPAI outbreak
what_it_represents: Spatial overlap of a commercial poultry farm with the estimated habitat of Mallards, Spot-billed Ducks, or Common Teals during the same migration period as an HPAI outbreak.

measure_name: Poultry-farm location inside or outside wild-waterfowl habitat isopleths prior to an HPAI outbreak
what_it_represents: Spatial overlap of a commercial poultry farm with the estimated habitat of Mallards, Spot-billed Ducks, or Common Teals in the migration period before an HPAI outbreak.
measurement_method: Additional binary geographical-location predictors derived from species’ utilization-distribution isopleths; 0 = Out and 1 = In.
metric_or_unit: Inside/outside (0/1); migration period k − 1 prior to an outbreak.
role_in_analysis: Lagged habitat-overlap predictors in the multilevel logistic regression model.
quantitative_result: In the final model, farms within Common Teals’ and Mallards’ habitats during the prior period had odds ratios of 0.46 and 0.40, respectively.
evidence_quote: To assess a potential lag from the habitat use of wild waterfowl to HPAI outbreaks in poultry farms, the model included additional three binary predictors of whether a poultry farm i was located inside or outside of three species’ isopleths (X2, X4, and X6) at the migration period k − 1 prior to an HPAI outbreak (0 = Out /1 = In).

measure_name: Pigeon type / captive domestic versus free-living status
what_it_represents: A host-category comparison between captive domestic pigeons and free-living C. livia; free-living combined feral pigeons and undomesticated wild Rock Doves for statistical analyses.
measurement_method: The authors collated published prevalence studies and recorded pigeon-population type; they analysed prevalence with beta regression and included pigeon type as an explanatory variable.
metric_or_unit: Trichomonas prevalence, expressed as a proportion of infected birds; pigeon type was categorical.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in global model selection testing variation in Trichomonas prevalence among pigeon populations.
quantitative_result: Free-living pigeons had decreased prevalence of Trichomonas infection (estimate = -0.567 ± 0.26, P-value = 0.029).
evidence_quote: In Table 1, the best performing model suggested that variation in prevalence was primarily explained by pigeon type (free-living or not), with free-living pigeons having decreased prevalence of Trichomonas infection (estimate = -0.567 ± 0.26, P-value = 0.029).

measure_name: Hybrid score
what_it_represents: A proxy for individual introgression level between domestic/feral and Rock Dove forms.
measurement_method: Calculated from the absolute distance from the mean principal-component-1 value in a PCA of logged wing, bill and tarsus length, cere width and mass.
metric_or_unit: Individual absolute distance from mean PC1 value.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in a binomial GLM testing whether individual Trichomonas infection status was explained by sample location, sex, and hybrid score; also included in condition models.
quantitative_result: Hybrid score was not a significant predictor retained in the best model for infection status.
evidence_quote: Because we did not have whole genome sequences available from the particular individuals used in this study, we calculated a proxy for individual introgression level using individual principal component 1 scores from a principal component analysis (PCA) using the logged values of wing, bill and tarsus length, cere width and mass.

measure_name: Pestivirus antibody seroprevalence by wild and domestic ruminant host species
what_it_represents: A quantitative comparison of pestivirus exposure/infection patterns across sympatric wildlife and livestock hosts.
measurement_method: Sera were analysed for pestivirus antibodies by cELISA; positive sera were further tested by VNT.
metric_or_unit: Per cent seroprevalence and numbers of positive herds/flocks.
role_in_analysis: Compared seroprevalence between cattle, sheep and red deer using statistical tests.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was higher in cattle (59.4 per cent) than domestic small ruminants and wildlife; cattle seroprevalence was significantly higher than sheep and red deer (P<0.001).
evidence_quote: Results showed a higher seroprevalence in cattle (59.4 per cent, 13/13 of herds) than in domestic small ruminants (5.9 per cent sheep, 2/8 of flocks; 0 per cent goats of 4 flocks) and wildlife (10.8 per cent in red deer, 0 per cent in roe deer and 0 per cent in Cantabrian chamois).

measure_name: Pestiviral RNA detection across sympatric wild and domestic ruminants
what_it_represents: Evidence of active pestivirus infection across wildlife and livestock hosts in the shared study area.
measurement_method: All sera were analysed for pestiviral RNA using RT-PCR.
metric_or_unit: Number of RT-PCR-positive animals.
role_in_analysis: Used to identify active infection and interpret the likely domestic source of infection in wild ruminants.
quantitative_result: BVDV-1 RNA was detected in one cattle calf.
evidence_quote: BVDV-1 RNA was detected in one cattle calf by RT-PCR and sequencing.

measure_name: Host species categories and interspecies transmission rates
what_it_represents: The wild-domestic relationship as virus transmission between buffalo and cattle.
measurement_method: Ancestral character reconstruction using host species as a discrete trait, with an asymmetric Bayesian stochastic search variable selection matrix estimating non-zero transmission rates between host categories.
metric_or_unit: Bayes factor (BF) for transmission rates; BF > 3.0 considered significant.
role_in_analysis: Tested directional virus transmission between buffalo and cattle.
quantitative_result: Buffalo-to-cattle and cattle-to-buffalo transmission each had BF >1000.
evidence_quote: There was strong evidence supported by BSSVS analysis of transmission from buffalo to cattle, and from cattle to buffalo (Table 1).
section: RESULTS — Discrete Traits for Host Species and Location

measure_name: TFCA interface location assignment
what_it_represents: A spatial definition of whether a sampled outbreak location belonged to the corresponding Transfrontier conservation area interface.
measurement_method: Locations within at most 50 km of a TFCA limit were assigned to the corresponding TFCA interface; other locations were assigned to the country of the outbreak.
metric_or_unit: Distance threshold of at most 50 km from the limit of a TFCA.
role_in_analysis: Location was used as a discrete-trait partition to reconstruct phylogeny and estimate virus transmission between locations.
quantitative_result: Transmission from KAZA to GL TFCA was significant, whereas there was no statistical support for migration from GL TFCA to KAZA TFCA.
evidence_quote: If the given location was within at most 50 km from the limit of a TFCA, it was assigned to the corresponding TFCA interface. Otherwise, the location was assigned to the country where the outbreak occurred.

measure_name: Distance from ASF-infected wild boar case to index farm
what_it_represents: Geographical proximity between an ASF-infected wild boar case and the domestic-pig index farm.
measurement_method: Reported location-based distance between the detected wild boar case and the index farm.
role_in_analysis: Contextual epidemiological observation; not used in a reported statistical comparison or model.
quantitative_result: A wild-boar ASF case was detected 230 m from the index farm.
evidence_quote: Numerous cases of wild boars infected with ASF had been reported in Hwacheon County, including a case detected 230 m away from the index farm on 27 July 2020.

measure_name: Proximity of backyard farms to the Lerma marshes
what_it_represents: The spatially proximate setting of domestic pigs and poultry relative to the wild-duck marsh habitat.
measurement_method: Backyard farms were selected based on accessibility and proximity to the marshes; their location was reported relative to the marsh boundaries.
metric_or_unit: within a 6 Km radius
role_in_analysis: Sampling-frame criterion defining the wild-duck/backyard-livestock study setting.
quantitative_result: Nine backyard farms were located within a 6 Km radius of the Lerma marshes boundaries.
evidence_quote: Animals were sampled from ten different study units: wild ducks from the Lerma marshes, as well as pigs and poultry from nine backyard farms located within a 6 Km radius of the Lerma marshes boundaries (Figure 1).

measure_name: IAV detection frequency by wild versus domestic host group
what_it_represents: IAV occurrence in wild ducks and in domestic poultry and swine sampled in the same wildlife–livestock setting.
measurement_method: Biological samples from wild ducks, poultry, and swine were tested by qRT-PCR.
metric_or_unit: Number sampled (n) and IAV-positive frequency (%)
role_in_analysis: Host-group comparison of molecular IAV detection at the study interface.
quantitative_result: Twenty-two wild dabbling ducks (3.68%) tested positive for IAV, whereas all pig and poultry swabs tested negative.
evidence_quote: Twenty-two wild dabbling ducks (3.68%) tested positive for IAV (Table 1).

measure_name: Species (buffalo versus cattle) RVFV seroprevalence
what_it_represents: Comparison of RVFV neutralizing-antibody prevalence between wild buffalo and domestic cattle.
measurement_method: Sera were tested using virus neutralization test (VNT); prevalence was compared between species.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%), 95% confidence interval, and p value.
role_in_analysis: Species was evaluated in the total sample, including stratified analyses by region.
quantitative_result: The overall prevalence was significantly higher in buffalo (12.7%) than cattle (5.7%; p = 0.0016).
evidence_quote: The overall prevalence was significantly higher (p = 0.0016) for buffalo [12.7%, 95% CI (7.8–19.5%)] than for cattle [5.7%, 95% CI (4.3–7.5%)].

measure_name: Cattle sampling location (CNP interface versus OD periphery)
what_it_represents: A spatial comparison of cattle seroprevalence across the Chobe National Park interface and the Okavango Delta periphery.
measurement_method: Cattle were sampled at crush pens selected according to proximity to protected-area boundaries; seroprevalence was compared by location.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%), with p value.
role_in_analysis: Location was tested as a potential influence on observed seroprevalence in sampled cattle.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was higher in cattle sampled at the CNP interface (9.5%) than at the OD periphery (3.9%; p = 0.004).
evidence_quote: Seroprevalence was significantly higher in cattle sampled at the interface with CNP compared to cattle sampled at the OD periphery (p = 0.004, 9.5 vs. 3.9%; Table 1).

measure_name: Ardeidae landscape suitability (%)
what_it_represents: The landscape suitability of wild Ardeidae maintenance hosts.
measurement_method: An ensemble approach comprising boosted regression trees (BRT), random forests (RF) and generalised additive models (GAM) was used to estimate the landscape suitability of each of the 15 Ardeidae species; a composite measure was calculated from the mean of individual species suitability distributions.
metric_or_unit: Percent (%)
role_in_analysis: Covariate in the final inhomogeneous Poisson models of JEV outbreaks, jointly adjusted with domestic-host density and landscape features.
evidence_quote: JEV outbreaks were strongly associated with Ardeidae suitability (Table 1, Model 1—relative risk (RR) ¼ 2.77, 95% CI 1.15–6.69; Model 2—RR ¼ 2.44, 95% CI 1.02–5.86)

measure_name: Pig density (deciles)
what_it_represents: The landscape distribution of domestic pig amplification hosts.
measurement_method: Pig density data were obtained from the Gridded Livestock of the World (GLW).
metric_or_unit: Deciles
role_in_analysis: Covariate in the final inhomogeneous Poisson models of JEV outbreaks, jointly adjusted with wild Ardeidae suitability and other landscape features.
evidence_quote: JEV outbreaks were strongly associated with Ardeidae suitability (Table 1, Model 1—relative risk (RR) ¼ 2.77, 95% CI 1.15–6.69; Model 2—RR ¼ 2.44, 95% CI 1.02–5.86), pig density (Model 1—RR ¼ 1.30, 95% CI 1.22–1.39; Model 2—RR ¼ 1.29, 95% CI 1.20–1.38) and chicken density (Model 1—RR ¼ 1.09, 95% CI 1.03–1.15; Model 2—RR ¼ 1.09, 95% CI 1.03–1.16) whereby an increasing presence of each in the landscape was associated with increased risk.

measure_name: Chicken density (deciles)
what_it_represents: The landscape distribution of domestic chicken hosts.
measurement_method: Chicken density data were obtained from the Gridded Livestock of the World (GLW).
metric_or_unit: Deciles
role_in_analysis: Covariate in the final inhomogeneous Poisson models of JEV outbreaks, jointly adjusted with wild Ardeidae suitability and other landscape features.
evidence_quote: JEV outbreaks were strongly associated with Ardeidae suitability (Table 1, Model 1—relative risk (RR) ¼ 2.77, 95% CI 1.15–6.69; Model 2—RR ¼ 2.44, 95% CI 1.02–5.86), pig density (Model 1—RR ¼ 1.30, 95% CI 1.22–1.39; Model 2—RR ¼ 1.29, 95% CI 1.20–1.38) and chicken density (Model 1—RR ¼ 1.09, 95% CI 1.03–1.15; Model 2—RR ¼ 1.09, 95% CI 1.03–1.16) whereby an increasing presence of each in the landscape was associated with increased risk.

measure_name: Felid group/type
what_it_represents: Domestic and wild felid groups, with feral domestic cats further divided by human management/association.
measurement_method: Felids were grouped by species; feral domestic cats were classified as managed or unmanaged based on association with humans.
metric_or_unit: T. gondii infection seroprevalence and oocyst-shedding prevalence; odds ratios from logistic regression.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare infection and oocyst-shedding levels among domestic and wild felid groups and to estimate their relative contributions to terrestrial oocyst load.
quantitative_result: The odds of shedding T. gondii-like oocysts were more than seven times higher in unmanaged feral cats and bobcats than managed feral cats (P = 0.02; Table 2).
evidence_quote: The odds of shedding T. gondii-like oocysts were more than seven times higher in unmanaged feral cats and bobcats than managed feral cats (P = 0.02; Table 2).

measure_name: T. brucei s.l. prevalence in cattle around wilderness/protected areas
what_it_represents: Reported infection occurrence in livestock located around wildlife-protected areas, relevant to livestock involvement in transmission around wilderness areas.
measurement_method: PCR and loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP).
metric_or_unit: Percentage of cattle carrying T. brucei s.l.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative evidence synthesized by the review to discuss cattle importance in r-HAT transmission around wilderness areas; not a quantitative analysis performed by this review.
quantitative_result: Around Serengeti National Park, 6% by PCR and 30% by LAMP; around Luangwa Valley, 1% by PCR and 25% by LAMP.
evidence_quote: Around the Serengeti National Park, 6% of cattle carried T. brucei s.l. by PCR, and 30% by loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and around Luangwa Valley in Zambia 1% by PCR and 25% by LAMP were reported ([14,28,29] J. Mubanga, PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh, 2008) (Table 1).

measure_name: Livestock proportion of identified G. pallidipes feeds at mixed wildlife-livestock sites
what_it_represents: The share of tsetse feeds from livestock where wildlife and livestock were both present.
measurement_method: Identified G. pallidipes feeds.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of identified feeds.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative evidence reviewed to describe tsetse feeding patterns in settings containing both wildlife and livestock; the figures are attributed to Bett et al., not generated by this review.
quantitative_result: 16% of identified feeds at Nguruman and 58% at Nkineji came from livestock.
evidence_quote: At two sites in Kenya where both wildlife and livestock were present, Bett et al. reported that 16% of G. pallidipes feeds identified at Nguruman and 58% at Nkineji came from livestock, with the rest from wildlife [56] but the absence of data on the relative abundance of wildlife and livestock at these two sites makes it is difficult to draw more general conclusions about tsetse choice.

measure_name: Domestic aspect of disease versus diseases potentially shared with domestic animals
what_it_represents: Numbers of reviewed articles that mention the domestic side of disease compared with articles addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals.
measurement_method: Systematic review count of reviewed articles.
metric_or_unit: Number of articles (n).
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of representation of the domestic aspect among reviewed long-term wildlife-disease studies.
quantitative_result: There were 67 articles in which the domestic side of the disease was mentioned, compared with 454 addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals.
evidence_quote: Concerning the wildlife–domestic interfaces addressed in the publications reviewed, there are a relatively low number of articles (n = 67) in which the domestic side of the disease is mentioned (considering livestock and companion animals as ‘domestic animals’), compared with those addressing diseases potentially shared with domestic animals (n = 454).

measure_name: Wildlife–domestic interface category
what_it_represents: The wildlife and domestic host-group pairing addressed by the reviewed long-term studies.
measurement_method: Articles were classified by wildlife–domestic interface and counted.
metric_or_unit: Publications.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive ranking of the top four interface categories and pathogens involved.
quantitative_result: Ungulates-cattle had 32 publications, carnivores-cattle 19, carnivores-dog 12, and carnivores-cat 10.

measure_name: Gastrointestinal parasite prevalence by host group at the shared ecosystem
what_it_represents: A descriptive comparison of parasite prevalence between wild gaur and domestic cattle that shared a common ecosystem at the interface zones.
measurement_method: Faecal samples were collected from 30 wild gaur and 20 domestic cattle and examined by centrifugal sedimentation and/or floatation.
metric_or_unit: Percentage faecal positive
role_in_analysis: Descriptive prevalence comparison between the wild and domestic host groups.
quantitative_result: 63.3% in wild gaur and 80.0% in domestic cattle; overall prevalence 70.0%.
evidence_quote: The parasitic prevalence was 63.3% and 80.0% in wild gaur and domestic cattle respectively with overall prevalence of 70.0%.

measure_name: Parasite-category prevalence by host group
what_it_represents: Prevalence of trematodes, cestodes, GI nematodes, and Coccidia oocysts in wild gaur and domestic cattle in the Nilgiri hills.
measurement_method: Qualitative faecal examination using centrifugal sedimentation and/or floatation technique.
metric_or_unit: Number positive and percentage positive
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of parasite categories across wild gaur and domestic cattle.
quantitative_result: GI nematodes were detected in 43.3% of wild gaur and 75.0% of domestic cattle; trematodes in 13.3% and 5.0%, respectively.
evidence_quote: Table 2: Overall parasite prevalence in wild gaur and domestic cattle in the Nilgiri hills.

measure_name: Livestock–wildlife interaction level
what_it_represents: The degree of interaction between livestock and wildlife across study areas.
measurement_method: Study areas were classified as high, medium, low, or no interaction using human population density, settlements, physical barriers, regular interactions, and whether livestock or wildlife alone was present.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: high, medium, low, and no interaction.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare pathogen detection in wildlife between areas categorized by wildlife-livestock interaction.
quantitative_result: Campylobacter detection in wildlife was lower in MFNP northern sector than in areas with high wildlife-livestock interaction (v2 = 33.1, df = 3, p = 0.03).
evidence_quote: However, Campylobacter’s detection in wildlife samples was significantly lower in MFNP northern sector than in areas categorized with high wildlife-livestock interaction (v2 = 33.1, df = 3, p = 0.03).

measure_name: Host domain (livestock versus wildlife)
what_it_represents: Comparison of pathogen sample prevalence between domestic livestock and wildlife.
measurement_method: PCR testing of faecal samples collected from domestic and wild animals.
metric_or_unit: Sample prevalence (%), with 95% confidence intervals.
role_in_analysis: Compared Salmonella and Campylobacter detection between livestock and wildlife.
quantitative_result: Salmonella and Campylobacter sample prevalence was higher in livestock (5.1% and 23.5%) than wildlife (1.9% and 16.8%), although differences were not statistically significant.
evidence_quote: The sample prevalence was higher in livestock (Salmonella spp. 5.1%, CI95% 2.7–8.6; and Campylobacter spp. 23.5%, CI95% 18.5–29.2) compared with wildlife (Salmonella spp. 1.9%, CI95% 0.5–4.8; and Campylobacter spp. 16.8%, CI95% 12.0–22.5), but differences were not statistically significant.

measure_name: Location
what_it_represents: Cattle origin in an interface area versus a non-interface area.
measurement_method: Study areas and dip tanks were categorized as interface or non-interface; location was generated as a two-category variable.
metric_or_unit: Brucella seroprevalence (%) and logistic-regression odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Predictor variable in logistic regression of cattle Brucella-seropositive status.
quantitative_result: Interface versus non-interface: OR 1.6 (95% CI 0.8–3.0; P=0.3) in the overall analysis.
evidence_quote: The seroprevalence varied from 9.6% to 11.2% for cattle originating from the interface areas while it varied from 5% to 8.3% for those originating from the non-interface areas.

measure_name: History of grazing in Park
what_it_represents: Whether cattle from the interface had a history of grazing in the national park, representing movement into and exposure within a wildlife area.
measurement_method: Grazing history according to the owner (GNP or KNP) was collected for each cattle animal and categorized as grazing in Park or not grazing in Park.
metric_or_unit: Brucella seroprevalence (%) and logistic-regression odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Additional predictor of seropositivity in a logistic-regression model restricted to female cattle; descriptive statistics were restricted to cattle from the interface.
quantitative_result: History of grazing in Park versus no history of grazing: OR 3.3 (95% CI 1.8–6.1; P<0.01).
evidence_quote: The results showed a non-significant association between antibodies against Brucella spp. and an increasing age of female animals and also a higher prevalence for those sampled from the interface areas. However, the results demonstrated a strong association (P<0.001) between antibodies against Brucella spp. and a history of abortion (odds ratio (OR)=35.8; 19.0<OR<67.6; χ2 =56.8; P<0.01) and that of grazing in the park (OR=3.3; 1.8<OR<6.1; χ2 =4.9; P<0.01).

measure_name: Movement patterns and activity-time overlap of free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pigs
what_it_represents: Potential temporal and movement overlap between domestic and wild pigs across the wildlife-livestock interface.
measurement_method: GPS/GSM tracking collars were used to monitor movement patterns.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive preliminary assessment of pig movements and potential overlap; no statistical comparison or model is reported.
quantitative_result: There was an overlap between free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pig activity times.
evidence_quote: In addition tracking collars (GPS/GSM) were used to monitor the movement patterns of free-ranging domestic pigs and wild pigs. Domestic pigs were mostly active during the nights, early mornings and in the evening. The bush pigs were active from the evening and throughout the night wandering between game reserves and farmlands. There was an overlap between free-ranging domestic pigs and bush pig activity times and this might be a contributing factor to the ASFV disease epidemics.

measure_name: nHSM.C
what_it_represents: Number of fenced big game estates near a cattle farm, representing nearby managed wild-ungulate settings.
measurement_method: Counted within a 2-km radius around the farm and coded above versus below the median.
metric_or_unit: Number of fenced big game estates; binary above-median/below-median category.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in multilevel logistic regression models of cattle-farm TB occurrence, new infection, and persistence.
quantitative_result: OR 1.75 [1.15, 2.68] for TB occurrence and OR 1.79 [1.06, 3.03] for TB persistence.
evidence_quote: nHSM.C (Number of fenced big game estates within a 2-km radius around the farm. Coded as 1=above median, 0=below median) 1. 75 [1.15, 2.68]a 1.55 [0.97, 2.49]b 1.79 [1.06, 3.03]a

measure_name: nHSM.O
what_it_represents: Number of open big game estates near a cattle farm, representing nearby open wild-ungulate settings.
measurement_method: Standardised count in a 2-km buffer around the farm.
metric_or_unit: Standardised number of open big game estates.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in the multilevel logistic regression model of TB persistence.
quantitative_result: OR 0.62 [0.46, 0.85] for TB persistence.
evidence_quote: nHSM.O (Standardised number of open big game estates in a 2-km buffer around the farm) NA NA 0.62 [0.46, 0.85]a

measure_name: Deer.HS
what_it_represents: Deer abundance in hunting estates near cattle farms, using hunted deer as a proxy.
measurement_method: Standardised number of deer hunted per game estate within a 2-km radius around the farm.
metric_or_unit: Standardised number of deer hunted per game estate.

quantitative_result: OR 1.20 [0.97, 1.47] for new TB infection.

what_it_represents: Proximity of a cattle farm to open big game estates.
measurement_method: Minimum distance to open big game estates, dichotomised at the median.
metric_or_unit: Meters; binary above-median/below-median category.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in the multilevel logistic regression model of new TB infection.
quantitative_result: OR 1.45 [0.97, 2.16] for new TB infection.

measure_name: Calif
what_it_represents: Extensive cattle production systems, identified by the authors as settings in which cattle contact with wild reservoirs is more likely.
measurement_method: Farm production type coded as beef and bullfighting versus dairy.
metric_or_unit: Binary category: 1=beef and bullfighting; 0=dairy.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in multilevel logistic regression models of cattle-farm TB occurrence, new infection, and persistence.
quantitative_result: The authors report risks of 3.03, 3.01 and 3.69 times higher for TB occurrence, new infection and persistence, respectively, than dairy farms.
evidence_quote: The models also indicate that extensive production systems (i.e. beef and bullfighting cattle farms), in which contact between cattle and wild reservoirs is more likely, are at 3.03, 3.01 and 3.69 times higher risk of TB occurrence, new infection and persistence, respectively, than dairy farms.

measure_name: Presence of wild birds (WildBirds)
what_it_represents: The predicted presence/distribution of waterbirds, representing the wild-bird component of the backyard-poultry–wild-bird interface.
measurement_method: The potential distribution of 22 waterbird species was modelled with MaxEnt, and model outputs were averaged by raster cell to map wild bird assemblages.
metric_or_unit: MaxEnt output in raster cells; combined by averaging outputs for 22 species.
role_in_analysis: One of four MCDA risk factors used to calculate the spatial LPAIV risk index.
quantitative_result: WildBirds received 22.2% of the total factor weight; sensitivity analysis found the risk index was strongly influenced by predicted wild-bird distribution (β = 0.45; p < 0.001).
evidence_quote: Proximity to wetlands (ProxWet) and the number of families with backyard poultry (BackPoul) were the highest weighted risk factors, and received 27.6% and 25.9% of the total weight, respectively. Proximity to a rice field (ProxRice) received 24.3% of the weight, and the presence of wild birds (WildBirds) received the lowest weighting, with 22.2% of the total weight (Table 3).

measure_name: Number of families with backyard poultry (BackPoul)
what_it_represents: The spatial presence/number of families owning backyard poultry, representing the domestic-poultry component of the interface.
measurement_method: Estimated from WorldPop population data by simulating family sizes and randomly selecting families as poultry owners according to population-density-dependent probabilities.
metric_or_unit: Estimated number of families with backyard poultry per raster cell, ranging from 0 to 4.
role_in_analysis: One of four MCDA risk factors used to calculate the spatial LPAIV risk index.
quantitative_result: BackPoul received 25.9% of the total factor weight.
evidence_quote: According to our model, the number of families owning backyard poultry varied between 0 and 4, but in 99.9% of cells with backyard poultry only one or two families had birds.

measure_name: Spatial risk index for LPAIV occurrence at the backyard-poultry–wild-bird interface (R)
what_it_represents: A spatially explicit index of risk for LPAIV occurrence at the interface between backyard poultry and wild birds.
measurement_method: Estimated for each raster cell through a weighted linear combination of four risk factors: proximity to wetlands, proximity to rice-growing areas, wild-bird presence, and backyard-poultry presence.
metric_or_unit: Continuous risk index by raster cell, displayed from lowest to highest risk.
role_in_analysis: Primary model outcome; validated by permutation tests comparing mean risk in counties with and without reported LPAIV activity.
quantitative_result: All three permutation tests found higher mean risk in counties where LPAIV had been isolated than in counties without reported LPAIV activity (p < 0.05).
evidence_quote: All three permutation tests showed that the mean risk in counties where LPAIV has been isolated is higher (p < 0.05) than in counties without reported LPAIV activity.
section: 3.3 | Model validation, uncertainty and sensitivity analysis

measure_name: C. burnetii antibody seroprevalence by ruminant host species
what_it_represents: Exposure to C. burnetii in wild and domestic ruminant species within the study area.
measurement_method: Specific antibodies against C. burnetii phase I and phase II antigens were tested using a commercial indirect ELISA; prevalence estimates were calculated and species prevalences were compared with binomial tests.
metric_or_unit: Percentage prevalence with 95 % confidence intervals; p values for species comparisons.
role_in_analysis: Compared exposure prevalence across domestic and wild ruminant species to assess their relative importance in C. burnetii epidemiology.
quantitative_result: Domestic sheep prevalence was statistically higher than red deer prevalence (p = 0.01112), but was not statistically different from mouflon prevalence (p = 0.1865).
evidence_quote: Specific antibodies against C. burnetii phase I and phase II antigens were tested by a commercial indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) that detects IgG from ruminant species (Q-Fever Antibody Test Kit; IDEXX, Westbrook, Maine, USA).

measure_name: Host status (wild or domestic)
what_it_represents: The host-domain category distinguishing wild from domestic animals.
measurement_method: Host status was included as a sample characteristic in PERMANOVA of within-sample E. coli phylogroup composition.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: wild or domestic; estimated variation (%) and PERMANOVA P value.
role_in_analysis: Significant explanatory variable for variation in within-sample phylogroup composition.
quantitative_result: Host status explained 43.24% of total variation (PERMANOVA, P = 0.006).
evidence_quote: Permutational multivariate analyses of variance (PERMANOVA) of the differences between within-sample E. coli phylogroup composition and host and environmental factors identified host status (wild or domestic) and season (wet or dry) at the time of collection as significant variables, with host status having the largest effect, explaining 43.24% of the total variation (Table 1; PERMANOVA, P = 0.006).
section: RESULTS — Influence of host and environmental variables on within-sample phylogroup composition

measure_name: Relative abundance of phylogroup B2 in wild versus domestic herbivores
what_it_represents: Comparison of E. coli phylogroup B2 abundance between wild and domestic hosts restricted to herbivores.
measurement_method: Wilcoxon comparison of relative abundance.
metric_or_unit: Relative abundance; Wilcoxon P < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Test of phylogroup-abundance differences across wild and domestic herbivores.
quantitative_result: The relative abundance of phylogroup B2 was significantly higher in wild herbivores than in domestic herbivores.
evidence_quote: Additionally, the relative abundance of phylogroup B2 was significantly higher in wild herbivores than in domestic herbivores (Fig. S6c; Wilcoxon, P , 0.05).
section: RESULTS — Phylogroup diversity within and between individual hosts

measure_name: Poultry versus wild-bird NDV sequence groups
what_it_represents: NDV genomic sequences grouped by domestic poultry versus wild-bird host origin, used to compare codon usage across the two host domains.
measurement_method: Genome-wide codon-usage analysis using DAMBE v7.0.35, including relative synonymous codon usage (RSCU), effective number of codons (ENC), nucleotide composition, and codon adaptation index (CAI).
metric_or_unit: 45 poultry sequences; 35 wild-bird sequences; 80 total sequences from genotypes II, XIV, and XVII.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of poultry and wild-bird virus sequences for codon usage and host adaptation.
quantitative_result: For all of the sequences studied here, all codons were used similarly in the complete genome among the Nigerian poultry and wild-bird viruses, with a Pearson r coefficient of 0.9987.
evidence_quote: For all of the sequences studied here, all codons were used similarly in the complete genome among the Nigerian poultry and wild-bird viruses (Fig. 3), with a Pearson r coefficient of 0.9987 that was statistically

measure_name: BTV-4 strain homology
what_it_represents: Sequence homology between BTV-4 strains detected in Iberian ibex and strains isolated in livestock during the same period.
measurement_method: BLAST analysis of sequenced BTV-4 segments.
metric_or_unit: Percent homology (99.4%–100%).
role_in_analysis: Comparison of BTV-4 strains across wild and domestic ruminants.
quantitative_result: The sequenced strains detected in Iberian ibex had 99.4%–100% homology with strains isolated in livestock during the same period.
evidence_quote: BLAST analysis showed that all the segments of the sequenced BTV-4 strains detected in Iberian ibex had high homology (99.4%–100%) with the strains isolated in livestock during the same period, and also with other BTV isolates (≥98.9%) previously found in Spain and other Mediterranean Basin countries, such as France, Italy, Morocco and Tunisia.

measure_name: Chlamydia positive ratios by wild-bird and livestock host group
what_it_represents: The prevalence of Chlamydia among wild birds and livestock, including sheep, goats, and chickens, sampled in the same village area.
measurement_method: Molecular surveillance using real-time PCR screening for chlamydial DNA.
metric_or_unit: Percentage positive and number of specimens.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of Chlamydia prevalence across wild-bird and domestic-livestock host groups.
quantitative_result: The positive ratios were 24.1% in wild birds, 40.0% in sheep, 43.3% in goats, and 26.9% in chickens.
evidence_quote: Among 29 captured wild birds and 63 livestock, 5 sheep, 30 goats and 28 chickens, the positive ratios of Chlamydia were 24.1%, 40.0%, 43.3% and 26.9%, respectively.

measure_name: ompA VD2 phylogenetic clustering of C. pecorum across host species
what_it_represents: Whether C. pecorum samples from wild birds and livestock occurred in the same phylogenetic clusters and had identical partial VD2 ompA sequences.
measurement_method: Sequencing and phylogenetic analysis of the ompA variable domain 2 region.
metric_or_unit: Three C. pecorum clusters; host source of samples within clusters.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of pathogen genetic clustering across wild and domestic host species.
quantitative_result: Each cluster included samples from different animal species, including goat, sheep, chicken and wild birds.
evidence_quote: In this phylogenetic tree, three clusters of C. pecorum were identified in this narrow sampling area (Fig. 2). Each cluster included at least three samples from the different animal species sampled, goat, sheep, chicken and wild birds.

measure_name: Presence of waterfowl in backyards
what_it_represents: A backyard-level wild/domestic bird exposure condition.
measurement_method: Reported as the presence of waterfowl in backyards; the review attributes the association to reference [15].
role_in_analysis: Reported association with HPAI H5N1 virus detections.
quantitative_result: Associated with more HPAI H5N1 virus detections.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, the presence of waterfowl in backyards was associated with more HPAI H5N1 virus detections [15].
section: Spillover of AIV from wild to domestic birds

measure_name: Contact rates between wild and domestic birds
what_it_represents: The frequency of contact between wild and domestic birds in villages and surrounding agricultural fields.
measurement_method: Investigated inside villages and in surrounding agricultural fields as part of a cross-sectional study.
role_in_analysis: The reported study attempted to link contact rates to HPAI H5N1 virus presence in domestic birds, but detections were too low.
quantitative_result: Could not be linked to HPAI H5N1 virus presence in domestic birds because the number of detections was too low.
evidence_quote: Contact rates between wild and domestic birds in Egypt have been investigated inside villages and in surrounding agricultural fields as part of a cross-sectional study, but could not be linked to HPAI H5N1 virus presence in domestic birds as number of HPAI H5N1 virus detections were too low [52].
section: Spillover of AIV from wild to domestic birds

measure_name: C. burnetii seroprevalence by host species
what_it_represents: The frequency of present/previous C. burnetii exposure in wild and domestic host species sharing the study habitat.
measurement_method: Sera were tested for antibodies against C. burnetii using ELISA; positive, negative, and inconclusive results were classified using S/P% cut-offs.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence of exposure (frequency expressed in %)
role_in_analysis: Compared across host species using χ2 or Fisher’s exact tests.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was 33% in European wildcats, 24% in Spanish ibex, 19% in domestic sheep, and lower in the other tested species.
evidence_quote: Seroprevalence was 33% (95% CI 2·53–64·13) in European wildcats, 24% (95% CI 5·59–42·03) in Spanish ibex, 19% (95% CI 17·68–20·19) in domestic sheep, 1·6% (95% CI 0·21–2·98) in red deer, 1·4% (95% CI 0·00–3·02) in European mouﬂon, 0·2% (95% CI 0–0·727) in cattle, and 0·1% (95% CI 0–0·53) in fallow deer (Table 1).

measure_name: Odds ratio of C. burnetii exposure associated with host species
what_it_represents: Relative risk of C. burnetii exposure for different wild and domestic host species.
measurement_method: Odds ratios with 95% Corneﬁeld confidence intervals were calculated for host species.
metric_or_unit: Odds ratio (OR) with 95% CI
role_in_analysis: Estimated and tested differences in exposure risk associated with host species.
quantitative_result: The odds ratio of seropositivity was significantly higher in domestic sheep than in the other species.
evidence_quote: The odds ratio (OR) of seropositivity was signiﬁcantly higher in domestic sheep compared to the other species (P < 0·05) (Table 1).

measure_name: Host type categories and host-type transition rates
what_it_represents: Transmission between wild birds and domestic bird production types, including primary wild-bird-to-domestic incursions and domestic-to-domestic spread.
measurement_method: Host type was modelled as a discrete phylogenetic trait; transition rates between host types were estimated in BEAST using an asymmetric discrete-trait evolution model and BSSVS.
metric_or_unit: Rates of transition occurrence (the number of transitions per unit of time)
role_in_analysis: To identify significant host type-to-host type routes of transmission and compare wild-to-domestic with domestic-to-domestic transmission.
quantitative_result: “The highest rate of transmission between host types was estimated as being from wild birds to domestic turkeys, followed by the rate of wild birds to backyard premises.”
evidence_quote: “Rates of transition between geographical regions and between host types were estimated in BEAST by inferring models of discrete trait evolution using an asymmetric model that allows the rate of transition between any given pair of traits to differ depending on the direction”

measure_name: Phylogenetic distance threshold for inferred transmission type
what_it_represents: Whether domestic cases represented primary transmission from wild birds or secondary transmission between domestic premises.
measurement_method: Patristic distances between each domestic case and its phylogenetically closest domestic case recorded at an earlier date were calculated; a threshold was applied to infer wild or domestic host type at internal nodes.
metric_or_unit: Evolutionary distance threshold; selected threshold value 0.19
role_in_analysis: To classify branches and cases as wild bird to domestic, domestic to domestic, or within wild birds, while accounting for cryptic wild bird-mediated transmission.
quantitative_result: “A threshold value of 0.19 was found to provide a good level of accordance with existing methods, balancing sensitivity and precision and maximizing an F-score calculated with a beta value of 1.5 (Table S5), and was applied across the phylogeny.”
evidence_quote: “Domestic cases were classified as resulting from primary or secondary transmission, according to host type (wild or domestic) inferred at internal nodes using a range of threshold phylogenetic distances.”
section: 3.3 | Quantification of the role of wild birds in transmission between host types

measure_name: Transmission type and dispersal distance
what_it_represents: The association of wild-bird-mediated versus domestic-to-domestic transmission with geographic virus dispersal distance.
measurement_method: Reconstructed per-branch transmission types were compared with dispersal distances using a general linear model.
metric_or_unit: Dispersal distance in km; general linear model p-value
role_in_analysis: To test the role of wild-to-domestic and domestic-to-domestic transmission types in virus dispersal dynamics.
quantitative_result: “both intrawild bird (23 km) and wild bird to domestic transmission (23 km) tending to occur across greater distances than domestic to domestic transmission (4 km).”
evidence_quote: “Inferred transmission type explained significant variation in mean dispersal distance (general linear model, p < .005)”

measure_name: C. burnetii seroprevalence in domestic ruminants and wild ungulates
what_it_represents: Comparative exposure to C. burnetii across domestic ruminants and wild ungulates.
measurement_method: An indirect ELISA test was performed on animal sera; titers equal to or greater than 1:40 were considered positive.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%) and 95% confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of infection exposure between domestic and wild host domains, interpreted to identify the likely reservoir.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was higher in domestic ruminants than in wild ungulates; domestic-ruminant values were 8.4% in sheep, 18.4% in cattle, and 24.4% in goats, while the highest wildlife value was 8.43% in red deer.
evidence_quote: The results obtained in the current study showed that, in general, seroprevalence in domestic ruminants is higher compared to that observed in wild ungulates, suggesting that livestock, and particularly goats, may be the most important reservoir of infection in Asturias.

measure_name: Risk of domestic-to-wild avian influenza transmission
what_it_represents: Modeled transmission risk between wild waterfowl and domestic poultry in China during breeding and wintering seasons.
measurement_method: A model developed by Prosser et al. (32) and presented as Figure 6.
role_in_analysis: Used with other highlighted models and poultry-outbreak reports to assess whether transmission between the populations could be a risk in northeastern China.
quantitative_result: The model identifies broad areas in northeastern China in Jilin and Heilongjiang.
evidence_quote: In addition, transmission risk at this interface identifies broad areas in northeastern China in the same provinces of Jilin and Heilongjiang that were identified to be highly connected to South Korea (Figure 2) and that underwent rapid land use changes toward rice cropping (Figure 4).

measure_name: Risk of contact with pasture
