what_it_represents: Roe deer potential exposure to domestic sheep or cattle pasture through overlap of their potential home range with pasture.
measurement_method: For each roe deer fecal sample, the authors estimated a circular virtual home range and assessed whether it overlapped sheep or cattle pastures; roe deer were classified as high or low risk of contact.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: high versus low risk of contact with pasture.
role_in_analysis: Independent variable in linear models of roe deer nemabiome alpha and beta diversity.
quantitative_result: The selected beta-diversity model included an interaction between sampling period and risk of contact with sheep pasture; cattle-contact risk was not retained.
evidence_quote: The selected linear mixed model for beta diversity included the interaction between the sampling period and the risk of contact with sheep pasture (Supplementary Table S3, Table 4, Fig. 5) and had a conditional R2 of 0.20. The risk of contact with cattle was not retained in the selected model, neither for explaining alpha diversity nor for beta diversity (Table 4).
section: 3.3. Differences among the roe deer nemabiomes according to their proximity to pastures

measure_name: Host-species genetic differentiation of H. contortus populations
what_it_represents: Genetic structure and inferred parasite circulation between domestic sheep and wild roe deer host populations.
measurement_method: Partial nad4 mtDNA amplicons were sequenced and pairwise PhiST and AMOVA were used to assess differentiation between sheep and roe deer populations.
metric_or_unit: Pairwise PhiST; percentage of molecular variance.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative test of parasite circulation between domestic and wild host populations.
quantitative_result: All PhiST values between roe deer and sheep were below 0.047, and 98.20% of molecular variance was within H. contortus populations.
evidence_quote: All PhiST values were low (<0.10) and the PhiST between roe deer and sheep were all <0.047 (Table 2). The majority of molecular variance was explained by the variation within H. contortus populations (98.20%) (Table 3).
section: 3.2. Diversity of gastrointestinal nematodes in sheep and roe deer

measure_name: Annual and seasonal spatial overlap in home ranges and core-areas
what_it_represents: Coarse-scale spatial overlap between wild boar and cattle.
measurement_method: Area of overlap in 95% utilization-distribution home ranges (HR) or 50% utilization-distribution core-areas (CA), divided by the total HR or CA area for each focal species.
metric_or_unit: Percent overlap (%)
role_in_analysis: Estimated annual and seasonal overlap between the concurrently monitored species.
quantitative_result: Overall, > 60% of wild boar HR overlapped areas used by cattle, whereas ≤ 40% of the HR of cattle overlapped areas used by wild boar.
evidence_quote: Spatial overlap between wild boar and domestic cattle within the BR cattle management area (see Figure 1). Percent overlap was estimated using fixed-kernel density estimators for 95% (HR) and 50% (CA; in bold) utilization distribution.
section: Table 1: Seasonal and annual coarse-scale overlap

measure_name: Spatial interspecific interaction (SII) index
what_it_represents: Fine-scale predicted potential interaction between cattle and wild boar based on similarity in their relative probability of spatial use.
measurement_method: Derived from latent selection difference models: "SII = (1 – P) if P ≥ 0.5, and SII = P if P < 0.5."
metric_or_unit: Index from 0 = low interaction to 0.5 = maximum interaction
role_in_analysis: Mapped across DNP and compared among cattle management areas with high versus low TB incidence in cattle.
quantitative_result: In general, areas with a high probability of use by both species (high potential interaction) were mostly associated with the marsh-shrub ecotone and permanent water sources.
evidence_quote: Accordingly, we constructed a spatial interspecific interaction (SII) index for the whole of BR using the rule: SII = (1 – P) if P ≥ 0.5, and SII = P if P < 0.5.
section: Fine-scale spatial interaction between wild boar and cattle

measure_name: Distance to protected areas
what_it_represents: Proximity of cattle dip tanks to protected areas with known African buffalo populations, used as a proxy of FMD presence in buffalo.
measurement_method: Euclidian distance from dip tanks to the nearest protected areas was calculated using ArcGIS 10.2.
metric_or_unit: Distance (in km)
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in generalized linear models of FMD outbreaks, assessed across provinces and in the SEL and Matabeleland regions.
quantitative_result: The number of FMD outbreaks recorded over the study period at the dip tank level was significantly related with the distance to protected areas.
evidence_quote: Protected areas with known buf‑falo populations were selected and used as a proxy of FMD presence in the buffalo population [36] (Figure 1).
section: Distance to protected (conservation) areas on the variation in the probability of FMD outbreaks

measure_name: Argasid tick infestation by habitat
what_it_represents: Occurrence of argasid ticks in warthog burrows in the wildlife area compared with domestic pig pens.
measurement_method: Ticks were collected from 32 warthog burrows and 20 domestic pig pens; apparent infestation prevalence was calculated for each habitat.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of inspected burrows or pig pens containing argasid ticks, with 95% confidence intervals.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of tick occurrence across wild and domestic habitats.
quantitative_result: Infestation was 90.6% in burrows and ticks were found in 10% of pig pens.
evidence_quote: The apparent prevalence of infestation in the burrows (n = 32) was 90.6%, 95% CI (82.2–99.0), while argasid ticks were only found in 10% (2/20), 95% CI (3.1–23.1) of the pig pens inspected.

measure_name: ASFV DNA detection in ticks by habitat
what_it_represents: ASFV infection in soft ticks collected from wild-host burrows versus domestic pigsties.
measurement_method: Soft tick samples were screened for ASFV DNA by nested PCR.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of ticks and pooled samples positive for ASFV DNA, with 95% confidence intervals.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of ASFV detection between ticks from burrows and pigsties.
quantitative_result: ASFV DNA was detected in 72.4% of ticks from burrows and 15.4% of pooled specimens from pigsties.
evidence_quote: African swine fever virus DNA was detected by PCR in 72.4%, 95% CI (52.8–92.0) of the soft ticks collected in burrows (18.8%, 95% CI [14.4–23.1] of the 304 pooled samples) and 15.4%, 95% CI (1.53–29.3) of the 26 pooled soft tick specimens collected in pigsties using (Table 1).
section: 3.2 | Analysis of ASFV infection in collected soft ticks

measure_name: Distribution of ASFV genotype XXIV across domestic and sylvatic habitats
what_it_represents: Presence of the novel ASFV genotype in isolates from domestic pig pens and warthog burrows, representing potential linkage between domestic and sylvatic cycles.
measurement_method: p72 gene amplification and sequencing of virus isolates from ticks collected in the two habitats.
metric_or_unit: Number of isolates and their habitat of origin.
role_in_analysis: Phylogenetic comparison used to assess potential transmission between domestic and sylvatic cycles.
quantitative_result: Five genotype-XXIV isolates included two from domestic pig pens and three from warthog burrows.
evidence_quote: This new genotype included viruses from domestic pig pens (MOZ 18/2006 and MOZ 19/2006) as well as warthog burrows (MOZ 10/2006, MOZ11/2006 and MOZ 16/2006) (Figure 2), illustrating a potential transmission between the domestic and the sylvatic cycle.
section: 3.3 | p72 Gene relationships between ASFV from soft ticks in different habitats

measure_name: Surface of communal pastures
what_it_represents: Communal pastures shared by cattle, goats, and/or sheep, representing settings that facilitate inter-species contact.
measurement_method: Surface was available at Local Veterinary Unit (LVU) scale and was included as a predictor in generalized linear mixed models.
metric_or_unit: Surface of communal pastures at LVU scale; model coefficients.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in cattle, goat, and wild boar prevalence models.
quantitative_result: Communal pastures cattle + small ruminants had a coefficient of 0.0003 in the cattle individual TB prevalence model, 0.0005 for communal pastures cattle + goats in the goat model, and 0.0001 in the wild boar MTC infection prevalence model.
evidence_quote: The model for the prevalence of TB in cattle evidenced the explanatory capacity of the proportion of extensive (beef) cattle farms and of the surface of communal pastures, while that of goats had a negative effect. Wildlife was relevant, since variables such as the presence of fenced hunting estates, wild boar abundance and the prevalence of wild boar MTC infection were included in the model. The model for that of goats showed the relevance of pastures shared by herds of cattle and goat. Finally, the model for the prevalence of TB in wild boar included the abundance of wild boar and, again, the surface of communal pastures.
section: 3.3. The MTC maintenance host community in CyL

measure_name: Wild boar MTC infection prevalence
what_it_represents: Infection prevalence in a wildlife host, compared spatially with livestock TB prevalence.
measurement_method: Wild boar mandibular lymph nodes were systematically sampled for microbiological cultures; prevalence was used as an LVU-level predictor where more than 30 wild boar were sampled.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%); coefficient 0.2734 in the cattle individual TB prevalence model.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in the cattle TB-prevalence model and component of cross-host spatial association analysis.
quantitative_result: Wild boar MTC infection prevalence had a coefficient of 0.2734 (95% CR 0.2597–0.2871) in the cattle individual TB prevalence model.
evidence_quote: Wild boar MTC infection prevalence was considered as a predictor only for LVUs with n > 30 sampled wild boar (see below).

measure_name: Presence of fenced hunting estates
what_it_represents: Presence of fenced wild-ungulate populations, a wildlife-management setting associated with livestock TB risk.
measurement_method: Presence/absence at LVU level was included as a predictor in generalized linear mixed models.
metric_or_unit: Presence; coefficient 15.9715 in the cattle individual TB prevalence model.
role_in_analysis: Predictor in the cattle TB-prevalence model.
quantitative_result: Fenced estates (presence) had a coefficient of 15.9715 (95% CR 15.8466–16.0962) in the cattle individual TB prevalence model.
evidence_quote: The cattle model suggests that wild boar abundance, the prevalence of TB in wild boar, and the presence of fenced hunting estates all contribute to the risk of detecting skin-test reactors cattle (Table 3).

measure_name: Shared MTC spoligotype patterns between livestock and wildlife
what_it_represents: Molecular-pattern sharing between livestock and wildlife MTC isolates.
measurement_method: Spoligotype patterns of MTC isolates from wildlife and livestock were compared in municipalities with data for both.
metric_or_unit: 15 of 20 municipalities (75%); in 2014, five of six municipalities (83%).
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of MTC isolates across wild and domestic hosts.
quantitative_result: In 15 of 20 municipalities (75%) with livestock data, at least one spoligotype pattern was shared by livestock and wildlife MTC isolates.
evidence_quote: Of these 20, in 15 municipalities (75%) at least one spoligotype pattern was found to be shared by livestock and wildlife MTC isolates.
section: 3.3. The MTC maintenance host community in CyL

measure_name: incursion index
what_it_represents: Cattle exposure to FMD virus from frequenting the buffer, an area used by buffalo and other wild ungulates.
measurement_method: Ratio of GPS locations in the buffer zone to all GPS locations over 24 hours.
metric_or_unit: Ratio of GPS locations recorded in the buffer zone to total GPS locations recorded over 24 hrs.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in GLMMs of FMD serological incidence in cattle.
quantitative_result: Serological incidence was higher when incursions into the protected area were more frequent.
evidence_quote: The index is the ratio of the number of GPS locations recorded in the buffer zone to the total number of GPS locations recorded over 24 hrs.

measure_name: cattle–buffalo contact index
what_it_represents: Potentially infective spatio-temporal contacts between GPS-collared cattle and buffalo.
measurement_method: A contact occurred when cattle were within 300 m of a buffalo position recorded up to 15 days earlier; rates were contacts relative to cattle–buffalo position pairs and multiplied by 10^8.
metric_or_unit: Contacts relative to the number of cattle–buffalo position pairs, multiplied by 10^8.
role_in_analysis: Candidate explanatory variable in GLMMs of FMD serological incidence.
quantitative_result: The index was very low: 172 contacts, compared with 90,238 cattle and 72,601 buffalo positions.
evidence_quote: A potentially infective contact was considered to occur whenever a cattle’s position was recorded within 300 m of a buffalo’s position and 15 days after the buffalo’s position had been recorded.

measure_name: buffer incursion index
what_it_represents: Daily use of the buffer by cattle and buffalo, used to assess synchrony or avoidance across the two species.
measurement_method: Daily buffer-incursion frequency time series analysed using cross-correlation functions.
metric_or_unit: Incursion index per day: loc buffer/total locs.
role_in_analysis: Cross-correlation analysis of cattle and buffalo buffer-incursion frequencies.
quantitative_result: Cattle did not use the buffer when buffalo had used it frequently up to 2 months before, and buffalo did not use it when cattle had used it up to 1 month before.
evidence_quote: The cross-­correlogram between buffalo and cattle (i.e., correlation of cattle incursion frequency at day 0 with buffalo incursion frequency at varying lags) showed negative correlations from a negative lag of 50 days to a positive lag of 40 days (Figure 7a).

measure_name: Distance to human settlements (urban distance)
what_it_represents: Anthropization and proximity of wild carnivores to settlements, used as a proxy for domestic dog populations.
measurement_method: Distance was calculated from each wild-carnivore capture location to the closest settlement using settlement spatial data from satellite images, then grouped into four distance categories.
metric_or_unit: Distance categories: < 5, 5–10, 10–15, and > 15 km.
role_in_analysis: Fixed effect in binomial GLMMs assessing CPV seropositivity and PCR positivity in wild carnivores.
quantitative_result: PCR prevalence had a significant negative relationship with distance to human settlements; relative to <5 km, the 5–10 km category had an estimate of -2.01 (SE 0.98), Z = -2.05, P = 0.04.
evidence_quote: GLMM analysis showed that there was a significant negative relationship between the distance to human settlements and PCR prevalence in wild carnivores from the JBR (Table 3).

measure_name: CPV haplotype sharing among carnivores including dogs
what_it_represents: Genetic sharing of CPV across wild carnivores and domestic dogs.
measurement_method: A median-joining haplotype network based on VP2 gene sequences was used to evaluate relationships among CPV haplotypes, taking host species into account.
metric_or_unit: Six different haplotypes.
role_in_analysis: Phylogenetic/genetic-diversity analysis used to assess evidence consistent with cross-species and bidirectional viral transmission.
quantitative_result: One haplotype was shared by all carnivores including dogs.
evidence_quote: The haplotype network showed a total of six different haplotypes circulating in JBR: kit foxes harbored the greatest diversity with three unique haplotypes, followed by striped skunks with two. One haplotype shared by all carnivores including dogs was central to the network.

measure_name: Wildlife presence versus wildlife exclusion on ranches
what_it_represents: Contrasting wildlife-livestock ranch settings: a ranch with high wildlife densities and a ranch from which wildlife was excluded.
measurement_method: Cost comparison of two ranches in the same agro-ecological zone, comparing relative annual acaricide cost per head of cattle.
metric_or_unit: $ per year per head of cattle
role_in_analysis: Comparison of disease-control costs associated with ranches differing in wildlife presence.
quantitative_result: The ranch with high wildlife densities applied acaricide weekly at $ 6.7 per year per head of cattle, whereas the wildlife-excluded ranch applied it monthly or twice monthly at $ 2.3.
evidence_quote: The former ranch had to apply acaricide on a weekly basis, costing $ 6.7 per year per head of cattle, while the latter ranch applied acaricide monthly or twice per month at an average cost of $ 2.3.
section: THE RELATIVE IMPORTANCE OF DISEASE IN MIXED WILDLIFE AND LIVESTOCK RANCHING

measure_name: Standard tick counts by host domain
what_it_represents: The relative contribution of cattle and wildlife to maintenance of the total tick population on a mixed wildlife/cattle ranch.
measurement_method: Female ticks were collected and measured over four years from animals harvested for meat; counts used the concept of engorging female 'standard ticks' dropping fully engorged in the next 24 hours.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of total tick population
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of tick-population maintenance by cattle versus wildlife.
quantitative_result: Cattle maintained approximately 75% and wildlife 25% of the total tick population on the farm.
evidence_quote: Based on standard tick counts, it was concluded that the cattle on this ranch maintained approximately 75% of the total tick population on the farm in comparison to 25% being maintained by the wildlife.
section: Wild Bovidae as maintenance hosts for ticks

measure_name: Daily output of standard female Rhipicephalus pulchellus ticks by animal species
what_it_represents: The daily tick contribution of livestock and individual wildlife host species on a mixed wildlife/cattle ranch.
measurement_method: Standard tick counts, calculated from approximate animal numbers and mean number of standard female ticks.
metric_or_unit: daily output of standard female ticks
role_in_analysis: Species-level quantification used to compare host contributions to tick populations on the ground.
quantitative_result: The table estimates daily output as 30,000 for cattle, 1,000 for sheep, and 11,210 combined for the listed wildlife species with data.
evidence_quote: Table 1. Estimation of the contribution per animal species to the daily population of RhiPicephalus pulchellus ticks on a mixed wildlife/cattle ranch in Kenya.
section: Wild Bovidae as maintenance hosts for ticks

measure_name: lion-to-dog transmission parameter
what_it_represents: Cross-species CDV transmission from lions to domestic dogs.
measurement_method: Bayesian state–space model; forecast comparison with and without lion-to-dog transmission.
role_in_analysis: Used to evaluate the impact of lion-to-dog transmission on annual probability of infection.
quantitative_result: Transmission from lions to dogs was negligible.
evidence_quote: This finding is consistent with the estimated lion-to-dog transmission parameter value [ω4 = 0.032 (0.00–0.20)] (SI Appendix, Table S5).

measure_name: dog-to-lion transmission parameter
what_it_represents: Cross-species CDV transmission from domestic dogs to lions.
measurement_method: Bayesian state–space model; forecast comparison with and without dog-to-lion transmission.
role_in_analysis: Used to evaluate the impact of dog-to-lion transmission on annual probability of infection.
quantitative_result: The estimated effect size was 10 times larger than lion-to-dog transmission, indicating strongly asymmetric cross-species transmission.
evidence_quote: However, the effect size of the parameter governing dog-to-lion transmission [β4 = 0.283 (0.08–2.48)] was 10 times larger than that of lion-to-dog transmission, indicating strongly asymmetric cross-species transmission.

measure_name: Wildlife-livestock overlap category
what_it_represents: The degree of spatial/ecological overlap between wildlife and livestock at sheep sampling locations.
measurement_method: Sheep were sampled at MRC, described as having considerable wildlife-livestock overlap, and Lekiji, described as having significantly less wildlife-livestock overlap.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: considerable versus significantly less wildlife-livestock overlap.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare TBH profiles and assess whether identical parasite genotypes were more likely to be shared under greater host overlap.
quantitative_result: The shared Anaplasma genotype AnGa + Sh5 occurred in 9% of sheep from Lekiji and none from MRC.
evidence_quote: Finally, AnGa + Sh5 sequences were isolated from both Grant’s gazelle and sheep. 25% of successfully sequenced gazelle samples in 2009 and 14% in 2011 were infected with the AnGa + Sh5 genotype, compared with 9% of sheep from Lekiji and none from MRC.

measure_name: Level of interaction with wild ungulates
what_it_represents: Village-level wild-ungulate/domestic-ruminant interaction category.
measurement_method: The three selected villages were classified as having medium, higher, or low interaction with wild ungulates.
metric_or_unit: Categorical level: medium, higher, or low interaction.
role_in_analysis: Used in descriptive comparison of sheep brucellosis seroprevalence across villages with differing interaction levels.
quantitative_result: Higher sheep brucellosis prevalence was reported in Misigiyo, followed by Endulen, which had a low level of interaction between wild ungulates and domestic animals.
evidence_quote: Despite few blood samples obtained, brucellosis seroprevalence in sheep, as reflected by both tests, indicated that the higher prevalence was recorded among sheep in Misigiyo followed by Endulen in which there is a low level of interaction between wild ungulates and domestic animals.

measure_name: Main driver of transmission between species: overlap of livestock and wildlife habitat, home range, or shared pasture
what_it_represents: Spatial or resource-sharing opportunities for disease transmission between livestock and wildlife in the reviewed models.
measurement_method: Data extraction and frequency synthesis across included models, with drivers recorded in Supplementary Table S3.
metric_or_unit: 18 models
role_in_analysis: Descriptive review analysis of the predominant drivers of interspecies disease transmission.
quantitative_result: Disease transmission was predominately driven through overlap or shared pasture in 18 models.
evidence_quote: Disease transmission was predominately driven through the overlap of livestock and wildlife habitat, home range, or shared pasture (18) (Supplementary Table S3).
section: Drivers of disease transmission, representations of host interaction processes, and model calibration

measure_name: Direction of transmission between wildlife and livestock
what_it_represents: Whether modeled disease transmission was unidirectional from wildlife to livestock or bidirectional between wildlife and livestock.
measurement_method: Extracted direction of transmission from included models and counted models by direction.
metric_or_unit: Number of models
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of modeled interspecies transmission directions.
quantitative_result: Unidirectional transmission from wildlife to livestock occurred in 26 models and bidirectional transmission occurred in 25 models.
evidence_quote: The models in this review examined transmission in all directions, with unidirectional transmission from wildlife to livestock (26) or bidirectional transmission between wildlife and livestock (25) being most frequent (Supplementary Table S3).
section: Drivers of disease transmission, representations of host interaction processes, and model calibration

measure_name: Transmission rate, contact probability, and contact rate
what_it_represents: Functional representations of the interaction process between host populations; transmission rate may reflect direct or indirect transmission and can be defined using contact rate and transmission probability.
measurement_method: Review of functional interaction-process representations in the included models.
metric_or_unit: Average number of new infections produced by one infectious unit per unit of time
role_in_analysis: Parameters governing the force of infection; in some studies, contact rate and transmission probability were disentangled to evaluate external factors' impacts on transmission mechanisms.
quantitative_result: A few studies disentangled contact rate and transmission probability to evaluate the relative impact of external factors on transmission mechanisms.
evidence_quote: The transmission rate can also be defined as the product of the contact rate and the transmission probability whenever a contact occurs with an infectious unit. A few studies disentangled these two parameters to evaluate the relative impact of external factors on the different mechanisms of transmission (15, 29, 53, 61).
section: Drivers of disease transmission, representations of host interaction processes, and model calibration

measure_name: direct deer-cattle interactions (deer within 5 m of cattle)
what_it_represents: Direct spatial proximity between deer and cattle.
measurement_method: A cited study of deer-cattle interactions within the TB-endemic zone of Michigan.
metric_or_unit: deer within 5 m of cattle
role_in_analysis: Reported descriptive comparison of direct deer-cattle proximity versus deer use of cattle feed-storage areas; this review did not itself conduct the study.
quantitative_result: Direct deer-cattle interactions were "exceedingly rare"; deer were commonly observed in feed storage areas, hay racks, and feeding troughs.
evidence_quote: One study on deer-cattle interactions, within the TB-endemic zone of Michigan, found direct deer-cattle interactions (deer within 5 m of cattle) to be exceedingly rare; however, deer were commonly seen in feed storage areas eating out of hay racks and feeding troughs [50].

measure_name: Prevalence of TBL in fallow deer and presence of cattle TBL
what_it_represents: An interspecific wild-domestic comparison of tuberculosis-like lesions in fallow deer and cattle.
measurement_method: Fallow-deer annual prevalence of TBL was used as an explanatory variable and cattle TBL presence as the response.
metric_or_unit: TBL prevalence (%) in fallow deer; presence of cattle TBL; F1,37 and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tested as an interspecific relationship in the analysis of factors determining TBL presence.
quantitative_result: The association was positive and significant (F1,37 = 1.16, p = 0.01).
evidence_quote: Regarding interspecific relationships, the prevalence of TBL in fallow deer was significantly (as explanatory) positively associated with the presence of cattle TBL (as response) (F1,37 = 1.16, p = 0.01; Figure 6).
section: 2.2. Factors Determining the Presence of Tuberculosis-Like Lesions (TBL)

measure_name: Type of wildlife/livestock interface
what_it_represents: The degree and physical form of separation or potential interaction between wild ungulates/buffalo and domestic cattle.
measurement_method: Study sites were classified according to wild-ungulate absence, an ungulate-proof fence, or no/damaged fence.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: no interface, fenced interface, unfenced interface.
role_in_analysis: Cattle infection prevalence and detection results were compared and summarized according to interface type.
quantitative_result: Theileria antibodies were detected in unfenced cattle populations, while no antibody was detected in the fenced and no-interface areas.
evidence_quote: Cattle in Pesvi had a signiﬁcantly higher prevalence compared to all of the other cattle populations (Fisher’s test, P < 0·001 except for Malipati, P = 0·002). No antibody was detected in the fenced and no interface areas.

measure_name: Relative risk of exposure for the domestic population (Pwd)
what_it_represents: The relative risk of exposure for domestic poultry, calculated from the density of exposed wild resident birds relative to poultry density.
measurement_method: WRexp was converted into density using buffer surfaces calculated from lakes’ satellite images; Pwd was calculated as WRexp divided by density of poultry.
metric_or_unit: Pwd; relative risk of exposure
role_in_analysis: Used in the quantitative exposure assessment to compare Lake Awassa and Lake Ziway.
quantitative_result: The mean Pwd was 1.1E-04 for Awassa Lake and 3.5E-05 for Ziway Lake.
evidence_quote: Finally, the density of WRexp over the density of poultry gave an estimation of the relative risk of exposure for the domestic population (Pwd): Pwd ¼ WRexp/density of poultry.

measure_name: Potential exposure between wild and domestic birds in a 5-km buffer zone
what_it_represents: A spatially delimited wild-domestic exposure setting around each lake.
measurement_method: A 5-km buffer around each lake; buffer surfaces were calculated on satellite images using ArcView software.
metric_or_unit: 5 km buffer; 297 km2 (Awassa) and 579 km2 (Ziway)
role_in_analysis: Spatial basis for estimating densities and comparing the two lakes in the exposure assessment.
quantitative_result: The Awassa Lake buffer area was 297 km2 and the Ziway Lake buffer area was 579 km2.
evidence_quote: We decided to focus on the potential exposure between wild and domestic birds in a buffer zone of 5 km around each lake,

measure_name: Detection/prevalence of Theileria sp. (buffalo) in buffalo and cattle
what_it_represents: Occurrence of a buffalo-associated Theileria parasite in both wildlife (buffalo) and domestic cattle, representing a cross-host wild-domestic infection pattern.
measurement_method: RLB-PCR followed by sequencing analysis of positive amplicons.
metric_or_unit: Percent and number of positive animals.
role_in_analysis: Used to assess whether a buffalo-associated parasite was also present in cattle and to interpret infection at the wildlife-livestock relationship.
quantitative_result: Theileria sp. (buffalo) was detected in cattle at 0.4% (1/232), while it was present in buffalo at 49.1% (26/53).
evidence_quote: The presence of Theileria sp. (buffalo) (49.1%; 26 of 53) and Theileria sp. (bougasvlei) (18.9%; 10 of 53) in buffalo (Table 4) is of diagnostic importance as it affects the accurate detection of T. parva in mixed infections when performing hybridization PCR assay [33]. In addition to buffalo, Theileria sp. (buffalo) was also detected in the cattle population (0.4%; 1 of 232).

measure_name: Detection of T. parva ASV15 in buffalo and cattle
what_it_represents: A shared parasite sequence variant across buffalo and domestic cattle, interpreted as possible spillover from wildlife to cattle.
measurement_method: Deep amplicon sequencing of the 18S rRNA V4 hyper-variable region and ASV analysis.
metric_or_unit: ASV detection in individual cattle sample Na032.
role_in_analysis: Used to infer possible wildlife-to-cattle spillover.
quantitative_result: T. parva ASV15 was detected in cattle sample Na032.
evidence_quote: Indeed, T. parva ASV15 was detected in cattle (Na032), suggesting possible spillover of T. parva from buffalo to domestic cattle.

measure_name: NTM species isolated from different hosts in the same municipality
what_it_represents: Geographical co-occurrence of NTM species across wild boar and other wild or domestic host species at municipality level.
measurement_method: The species and hosts were tabulated by region and municipality.
metric_or_unit: Municipality-level host co-occurrence.
role_in_analysis: Used to identify and interpret geographical association of NTM across wild and domestic hosts.
quantitative_result: Maa, Mah, M. nonchromogenicum and M. lentiflavum were found in different hosts within the same municipality, with wild boar involved in every listed association.
evidence_quote:
Maa, Mah, M. nonchromogenicum and M. lentiflavum were isolated
from different hosts within the same municipality, being wild boar
always one of the implicated hosts (see Table 3).

measure_name: Host as a discrete trait
what_it_represents: FFV host state in domestic cats and pumas, used to assess movement between the domestic-cat and puma host domains.
measurement_method: Time-calibrated phylogenies in BEAST with a symmetric trait substitution model and Bayesian stochastic search variable selection to estimate host transition rates.
metric_or_unit: Bayes Factor (BF) and posterior probability
role_in_analysis: Estimated and tested cross-species host-transition rates, including directionality between domestic cats and pumas.
quantitative_result: The asymmetrical model supported domestic cat to puma transmission (BF = 8,155, posterior probability = 1) and puma to domestic cat transmission (BF = 20, posterior probability = 0.99).
evidence_quote: Further, analysis of host transmission using an asymmetrical model of discrete trait transition (Supplementary Fig. S3) shows two supported trends of FFV transmission: puma to domestic cat (BF ¼ 20, posterior probability ¼ 0.99) and domestic cat to puma (BF ¼ 8,155, posterior probability ¼ 1).
section: 3.4 Substitution rates and Bayesian ancestral reconstruction of location and host state

measure_name: Host origin of parental FFV sequences in recombination events
what_it_represents: Whether inferred parental FFV sequences in recombination events originated from domestic cats, pumas, or both species.
measurement_method: Recombination analyses of pol and env gene sequences from domestic cats and pumas.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of recombination events
role_in_analysis: Characterized recombination involving FFV originating from both host species.
quantitative_result: Parental FFVs originating from both species occurred in 9/12 (75%) pol events and 8/11 (approximately 72%) env events.
evidence_quote: Recombination events with inferred parental FFVs originating from both species were identified in 9/12 (75%) events in pol and 8/11 (􏰀72%) events in env (Fig. 4A and B and Supplementary Data S2).

measure_name: Vector-borne pathogen prevalence in wild versus domestic carnivores
what_it_represents: Comparison of vector-borne pathogen infection prevalence across wild and domestic carnivore host groups.
measurement_method: Real-time PCR detection of Anaplasmataceae, Rickettsia sp., Bartonella sp., Coxiella burnetii, and Piroplasmida in mammal samples; differences were tested with χ2 or Fisher’s exact test.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%); 22% in wild carnivores versus 4% in domestic carnivores.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of prevalence between wild and domestic species.
quantitative_result: Prevalence of VBP was higher in wild than in domestic carnivores (22% vs 4%; Fisher’s p = 0.0027).
evidence_quote: Prevalence of VBP was higher in wild than in domestic carnivores (22% vs 4%; Fisher’s p = 0.0027).
section: 3.1. Prevalence and molecular identification in mammals

measure_name: Chicken MID50 by virus origin
what_it_represents: The infectious dose required to infect half of chickens, compared between LPAI viruses of wild-bird origin and poultry origin as an indicator of adaptation to chickens.
measurement_method: Experimental determination of the minimal infectious dose 50 (MID50) in chickens.
metric_or_unit: log10 EID50
role_in_analysis: Comparison of wild-bird-origin and poultry-origin virus adaptation to chickens.
quantitative_result: Wild-bird-origin LPAI viruses generally had chicken MID50 values greater than 10^6 EID50, whereas most poultry-origin LPAI virus MID50s ranged from 10^2.8 to 10^4.2.
evidence_quote: For the wild-bird origin LPAI viruses, the chicken MID50 was greater than 106 EID50 with one exception (A/Mallard/Ohio/338/1986 at a MID50 of 104.4). For LPAI viruses of poultry origin, most of the MID50s were in the range of 102.8–104.2. This difference in the infectious dose clearly highlights that wild-bird origin viruses are generally not well adapted to chickens.

measure_name: High- versus low-risk area for wildlife contact
what_it_represents: Cattle exposure setting defined by proximity to Gonarezhou National Park and expected wildlife contact.
measurement_method: Sentinel cattle were monitored at one dip tank in each area; the HRA was 3 km from the GNP boundary and the LRA was more than 10 km from the park borders, where little or no wildlife occurs.
metric_or_unit: Distance from GNP boundary (3 km versus more than 10 km); seroprevalence (%) of cattle with antibody titre ≥1.6.
role_in_analysis: Groups defined by interface risk were compared for seroprevalence using Fisher’s exact test.
quantitative_result: At 4 months, antibodies to one or more SAT types were detected in 31% in the LRA and 26% in the HRA (P = 0.57).
evidence_quote: Indeed, at 4 months, antibodies to one or more of the 3 SAT types were detected in 28% of the monitored animals (31% in the LRA and 26% in the HRA; P = 0.57).
section: Serological status of the sentinel cattle

measure_name: MAC prevalence in wildlife, goats and cattle
what_it_represents: The prevalence of Mycobacterium avium complex in wild and domestic animal hosts sharing the study area.
measurement_method: Wildlife MAC positivity was determined on culture; cattle and goats were classified as MAC positive from comparative intradermal skin testing.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%)
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of MAC prevalence across wildlife and livestock host domains.
quantitative_result: Although MAC prevalence was relatively high in wildlife (4.2%), it was lower in livestock (0.8% in goats and 2.5% in cattle).
evidence_quote: Two MAC strains were isolated from intestinal lymph nodes of Grant’s gazelle. Although MAC prevalence was relatively high in wildlife (4.2%), it was lower in livestock (0.8% in goats and 2.5% in cattle).

measure_name: Type of interface
what_it_represents: Study areas categorized as interface or non-interface based on wildlife-livestock-human overlap and interactions.
measurement_method: Sites were selected as porous interface sites adjacent to protected wildlife areas with known wildlife-livestock interactions, or non-interface sites distant from protected areas with no known direct or indirect interactions.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: interface (0) or non-interface (1)
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in Chi-squared and odds-ratio comparisons of respondents reporting anthrax outbreaks.
quantitative_result: Respondents from non-interface sites had significantly higher odds of reporting anthrax outbreaks than respondents from interface sites (χ2 = 23.2, OR = 3.5, 2.1<OR<5.8, p<0.001).
evidence_quote: The non-interface sites were associated with respondents having a significantly higher odds (χ2 = 23.2, OR = 3.5, 2.1<OR<5.8, p<0.001) to report anthrax outbreaks than their counterparts from the interface sites.
section: Results—Respondents reporting presence of anthrax in their areas

measure_name: Site type: shared versus non-shared sites
what_it_represents: Whether sheep and guanaco co-occurred in a site (shared) or whether sites contained only one of the two host species (non-shared).
measurement_method: Six study sites were classified based on the presence of sheep and guanaco.
metric_or_unit: Categorical site treatment: “shared” or “non-shared”
role_in_analysis: Ecological context used to compare MAP prevalence and shedding, and included as a predictor in linear-model formulations.
quantitative_result: Sheep MAP prevalence in shared sites was highest in summer at 79.5%, while guanaco prevalence in shared sites rose from 5.0% in autumn to 44.7% in summer.
evidence_quote: Sheep and guanaco are present in Ranches 3 and 4, representing the “shared” sites treatment. Ranches 1 and 2 have only sheep, while in PNPA and PNTP only guanaco are present, representing the “non-shared” sites.

measure_name: MAP prevalence and pathogen shedding by host species and site type
what_it_represents: Infection prevalence and amount of MAP shed by domestic sheep and wild guanaco across shared and non-shared ecological contexts.
measurement_method: Prevalence was estimated from faecal samples positive and negative to pathogen culture; shedding was estimated from MAP DNA concentration in qPCR products.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence percentage; Log10 DNA copies/2 g faecal material
role_in_analysis: Prevalence differences among site types and species were compared using confidence-interval overlap; shedding was assessed by species, season, and site type using three-way ANOVA.
quantitative_result: Overall pathogen shedding was significantly higher in sheep (mean ± SD: 3.76 ± 0.86 Log10 DNA copies/2 g faecal material) than in guanaco (3.26 ± 0.65 Log10 DNA copies/2 g faecal material; t = −4.69, df = 199, p < .001).
evidence_quote: Differences in prevalence among site types and species were compared by the overlap of confidence intervals among sites and seasons (Cumming, 2009).

measure_name: RatesInt — direct wildlife–­cattle interaction rate
what_it_represents: The standardised number of direct interactions between a wildlife host species and cattle per month for each species pair.
measurement_method: Calculated from reported number of interactions, sampling effort, and study period; calculated separately for direct interactions.
metric_or_unit: interactions/month per species pair
role_in_analysis: Used to compare the overall frequency of direct versus indirect wildlife–­cattle interactions; direct-interaction occurrence was also analysed as presence/absence in binomial models.
quantitative_result: The overall mean of direct RatesInt was 0.03 interactions/month [range: 0.00–­ 0.12] per species pair.
evidence_quote: The overall mean of direct RatesInt was 0.03 interactions/month [range: 0.00–­ 0.12] per species pair, while indirect RatesInt was 4.63 interactions/month [range: 0.16–­ 30.00] per species pair, representing 154 times more than the mean of direct interactions (Fig. 4).

measure_name: RatesInt — indirect wildlife–­cattle interaction rate
what_it_represents: The standardised number of indirect interactions between a wildlife host species and cattle per month for each species pair, including interactions through shared environmental settings.
measurement_method: Calculated from reported number of interactions, sampling effort, and study period; calculated separately for indirect interactions.
metric_or_unit: interactions/month per species pair
role_in_analysis: Response variable in Gaussian models testing factors influencing indirect interaction rates and compared with direct interaction rates.
quantitative_result: The overall mean of indirect RatesInt was 4.63 interactions/month [range: 0.16–­ 30.00] per species pair, 154 times the mean direct-interaction rate.
evidence_quote: For indirect interactions, the response variable was RatesInt and models were fitted with a Gaussian family (function lme, R package ‘nlme’; Pinheiro et al. 2018).
section: materials and methods — Statistical analyses of factors influencing patterns of interaction rates

measure_name: Spoligotype patterns agreement between wildlife and indigenous-cattle M. bovis isolates
what_it_represents: Genetic similarity of M. bovis isolates across wildlife and cattle host domains.
measurement_method: Spoligotyping; comparison of isolates from wildlife with two novel strains from indigenous cattle.
metric_or_unit: Spoligo patterns agreement (%)
role_in_analysis: Used to assess whether infections in wildlife and indigenous cattle were genetically related.
quantitative_result: 96.8% agreement for SB2290 and 45.2% for SB2289.
evidence_quote: Comparison of M. bovis isolated from wildlife with the two novel strains (SB2290 and SB2289) found in indigenous cattle had a spoligo patterns agreement of 96.8% and 45.2%, respectively. This indicates that at least some infections due to bovine tuberculosis (bTB) in the wildlife and indigenous cattle were genetically related.

measure_name: Poultry and egg facility density
what_it_represents: The spatial density of domestic poultry facilities, used to situate wild-bird surveillance and infected domestic premises in the poultry domain.
measurement_method: Poultry and egg facility counts were extracted from the Statistics Canada 2021 Census of Agriculture at the census consolidated subdivision level, and facility density was calculated.
metric_or_unit: number of poultry and egg facilities per square kilometre, categorized into quantiles
role_in_analysis: Used as the population metric in purely spatial discrete Poisson scans of wild-bird surveillance intensity and mapped alongside HPAIV-infected domestic premises and wild-bird surveillance data.
quantitative_result: The spatial scan detected six clusters with increased live and harvest surveillance intensity; half were centred around areas of high poultry facility density.
evidence_quote: Using poultry production density as the population metric, the spatial scan detected six spatial clusters with increased live and harvest wild bird surveillance intensity (Table 2; Fig. 2D). All but one high cluster consisted of a single CCS, with half of the clusters centred around areas of high poultry facility density (PD3, PD4, PD8; Fig. 2D).

measure_name: Wild mallard abundance
what_it_represents: A spatial and seasonal proxy for the wild-bird domain in relation to poultry-facility detections.
measurement_method: Weekly eBird relative-abundance estimates for mallards were obtained for 26.7 × 26.7 km grid cells and averaged by season.
metric_or_unit: relative abundance estimates; 26.7 × 26.7 km grid cells
role_in_analysis: Used as a population metric in spatial scans and to map domestic-premises detections in relation to seasonal wild-bird abundance.
quantitative_result: Poultry facility detections occurred in locations and during time periods when wild birds were in high abundance, although some high-abundance areas had no poultry-facility detections.
evidence_quote: Additionally, there were poultry facility detections in areas with high human population density and in locations and during time periods when wild birds were in high abundance (Figs. 4A and 6A), including near the GTA and Ottawa. However, conversely, there were areas with high wild mallard abundance and no poultry facility detections (Fig. 6A).
section: 3.5. H5 HPAIV-infected premises and wild bird detections

measure_name: Observed cattle-wildlife contact
what_it_represents: The occurrence, frequency, and duration of cattle contact with elephant, buffalo, and impala in grazing areas outside and within the KNP.
measurement_method: A semi-structured questionnaire was administered to randomly chosen cattle owners; contact was defined as cattle and wildlife grazing together within approximately 7000 m2.
metric_or_unit: Proportion of 113 farmers reporting contact; duration categories of 0–60 min, 1–6 h, and >6 h.
role_in_analysis: Used to estimate the extent of contact and assess potential cross-species transmission.
quantitative_result: Sixteen percent of farmers (18/113) reported contact between cattle and buffalo, 9.7% (11/113) reported contact with impala, and one farmer reported contact with elephant.
evidence_quote: Sixteen percent of the farmers (18/113) reported observations of contact between cattle and buffalo, 9.7% (11/113) observed contacts with impala and only one farmer reported contacts with elephant.

measure_name: Probability of observing cattle-wildlife contact conditional on wildlife observation
what_it_represents: The estimated probability that observed buffalo, impala, or elephant outside the KNP fence would associate with cattle.
measurement_method: Calculated as the ratio of the proportion of farmers observing contact to the proportion observing that wildlife species.
metric_or_unit: Probability (Pr).
role_in_analysis: Compared estimated contact probabilities among wildlife species.
quantitative_result: The estimated probability was 0.6 for buffalo, 0.46 for impala, and 0.04 for elephant.
evidence_quote: The probability of a farmer observing contact between livestock and a particular wildlife species, given that the species was observed outside the KNP fence, was therefore much higher for buffalo (Pr = 0.6) and impala (Pr = 0.46), than for elephant (Pr = 0.04).

measure_name: Cryptosporidium occurrence by wild and domestic host species at the interface
what_it_represents: Cryptosporidium-positive proportions and identified species in elephant, impala, African buffalo, and domestic calves sampled at the wildlife/livestock interface.
measurement_method: Nested PCR at the 18S rRNA locus, followed by RFLP analysis and sequencing of wildlife samples.
metric_or_unit: Number tested and Cryptosporidium-positive percentage.
role_in_analysis: Characterized Cryptosporidium across wildlife and domestic calves at the wildlife/livestock interface.
quantitative_result: Impala and African buffalo were each 2/71 (2.8%) positive, while domestic calves were 4/51 (8%) positive.
evidence_quote:
Table 3
Cryptosporidium species identified from impala, African buffalo and domestic calves at the wildlife/livestock interface of the Kruger National Park.

measure_name: Between-deme effective reproduction number (Re)
what_it_represents: Cross-species and cross-country virus transmission, including farm-to-wild bird and wild bird-to-farm transmission.
measurement_method: Estimated with a multi-type birth–death (MTBD) phylodynamic model from HA genome sequences structured by host type and geographical location.
metric_or_unit: Re; posterior median and 95 per cent HPD.
role_in_analysis: Quantified transmission between poultry-farm and wild-bird demes.
quantitative_result: Values representing wild bird-to-farm transmission were extremely low (median within the range of 10−3–10−2), whereas farm-to-wild bird transmission had medians of 0.1–0.4; the Czech Republic farm-to-wild bird estimate had a median of 4.6 (95 per cent HPD: 0.9–9.2).
evidence_quote: Overall, the between-deme Re estimates were much lower than the within-deme Re estimates, with extremely low values (median within the range of 10−3 –10−2 ) for those representing farm-to-farm across countries and wild bird-to-farm transmission (Fig. 4B, SI Appendix Table S3). Slightly higher values were found for those representing farm-to-wild bird transmission (median of 0.1–0.4). One exception was found for the between-deme Re estimate representing farm-to-wild bird transmission in the Czech Republic, with a median of 4.6 (95 per cent HPD: 0.9–9.2).

measure_name: Number of wild bird-to-farm transmission events
what_it_represents: Imported H5N8 infections in poultry-farm demes from the wild-bird deme.
measurement_method: Inferred from simulated epidemic trajectories generated from posterior phylogenetic trees and MTBD model parameters.
metric_or_unit: Median number of events and 95 per cent HPD.
role_in_analysis: Compared local transmission with importation and identified the dominant transmission source for each country.
quantitative_result: In the Czech Republic, wild bird-to-farm transmission dominated, with a median of 116 events (95 per cent HPD: 55–218).
evidence_quote: In the Czech Republic, the epidemic was dominated by wild bird-to-farm transmission events (median: 116, 95 per cent HPD: 55–218).

measure_name: Cross-host recent-vicinity submodels
what_it_represents: Potential transmission between wild boar and domestic pigs, represented by a sample from one host occurring near a recent PCR-positive sample from the other host.
measurement_method: Weekly 2 × 2 km grid-cell surveillance data were restricted to samples occurring within 5 km of a PCR-positive sample from the other host population during the preceding 4 weeks.
metric_or_unit: Within 5 km; last 4 weeks; binary presence of positive samples within grid cell k in week t.
role_in_analysis: Separate boosted-regression-tree response variables used to test factors driving transmission between host populations.
quantitative_result: In the DP week submodel, WB-related variables were important predictors of DP detection; the number of WB harvested was the most important risk factor.
evidence_quote: In the DP week submodel, which limited the data only to DP samples that occurred within 5 km of a PCR+ sample in WB in the last 4 weeks, the number of WB harvested (a proxy for WB density) was the most important risk factor, followed by distance to the closest DP-positive sample, recent neighborhood prevalence in WB, sample size, and season (Figure 5B).
section: Results, 3.4. Risk factors involving WB were important for predicting ASF detection in the DP

measure_name: Cross-host surveillance proximity and positivity comparison
what_it_represents: The availability of surveillance from the opposite host sector near positive wild boar or domestic-pig grid-cell-week observations, and the relative frequency of cross-host positive samples nearby.
measurement_method: For grid-cell-week data points positive in one host, the authors counted surveillance samples from the other host within 5 km during the previous 4 weeks and calculated the percentage that were positive.
metric_or_unit: Within 5 km; last 4 weeks; 21.8%, 41.9%, 25%, 0.52%; 48 times as likely.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison used to assess directional relative transmission risk and the effects of surveillance design.
quantitative_result: The rate of positive WB samples near a positive DP sample was 48 times the rate of positive DP samples near a positive WB sample.
evidence_quote: Thus, the surveillance design afforded twice as much opportunity to find DP-positive samples in the recent vicinity of WB-positive samples compared to the opposite (compare 41.9 to 21.8%), yet the reverse occurred – the rate of positive WB samples in the recent vicinity of a positive DP sample was 48 times as likely than the rate of positive DP samples in the recent vicinity of a positive WB sample (divide 25% for WB-positive samples collected in the recent vicinity of a DP positive by 0.52% of the DP-positive samples collected in the recent vicinity of a WB-positive sample).
section: Results, 3.1. Spatial and temporal trends in cases

measure_name: Anti-Brucella antibody seroprevalence by host species
what_it_represents: The prevalence of anti-Brucella antibodies across human, livestock, and wildlife host species in the Katavi-Rukwa ecosystem.
measurement_method: Serological testing, with c-ELISA reported for cattle and goats and Rivanol Precipitation Test reported for humans and buffaloes.
metric_or_unit: Percent seroprevalence with 95 % confidence intervals.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of Brucella antibody prevalence across host species representing the human, livestock, and wildlife interface.
quantitative_result: Anti-Brucella antibodies were detected in humans at 0.6 %, cattle at 6.8 %, goats at 1.6 %, and buffaloes at 7.9 %.
evidence_quote: Anti-Brucella antibodies were detected in humans at 0.6 % (95 % CI: 0.1, 2.1 %); cattle at 6.8 % (95 % CI: 5.4, 8.5 %), goats at 1.6 % (95 % CI: 0.4, 4.1 %) and buffaloes at 7.9 % (95 % CI: 1.7, 21.4 %).

measure_name: Host-domain-specific tick PCR sampling and rickettsial infection detection
what_it_represents: Ticks associated with wild animals, dogs, and humans were tested to characterize the potential movement of spotted fever rickettsia from wild reservoirs through domesticated animals to humans.
measurement_method: Nested PCR detection of the 17 kDa antigen gene in a sub-sample of ticks collected from wild animals, dogs, and humans.
metric_or_unit: 80 ticks tested: 50 from wild animals, 20 from dogs, and 10 from humans; PCR-positive ticks (number and percentage).
role_in_analysis: The host-domain categories defined the tick sub-samples used to analyse the presence of spotted fever rickettsial infections.
quantitative_result: Four of 80 ticks (5%) were positive; the positives included three Amblyomma ticks from wild animals and Rhipicephalus sanguineus from a dog.
evidence_quote: Out of 80 ethidium-bromide stained gel electrophoreses with PCR products (208 bp), only four ticks (5%) were positive for spotted fever infections (Appendix 1). These include three Amblyomma species: Amblyomma testudinairum taken from a wild boar (Sus cristatus cristatus), Amblyomma clypeolatum from a star tortoise, and Amblyomma javanense from a pangolin and Rhipicephalus sanguineus from a dog.

measure_name: Posterior probability of pathogen transition between host species
what_it_represents: Support for direct M. bovis pathogen transition between pairs of elk, deer, and cattle host states.
measurement_method: Host species were modelled as a discrete trait using Discrete Ancestral Trait Mapping (DATM) in BEAST 2.
metric_or_unit: Posterior probability (PP)
role_in_analysis: Used to estimate and test support for pathogen transition rates between pairs of host species.
quantitative_result: State transitions between deer and cattle, and deer and elk were shown to have strong support (PP=0.996 and 0.989, Table 1), but the transition between cattle and elk was poorly supported (PP=0.391, Table 1).
evidence_quote: State transitions between deer and cattle, and deer and elk were shown to have strong support (PP=0.996 and 0.989, Table 1), but the transition between cattle and elk was poorly supported (PP=0.391, Table 1).

measure_name: Wildlife component
what_it_represents: Whether an OIE-reportable livestock disease present in the United States has a potential wildlife component associated with pathogen transmission, maintenance, or life cycle.
measurement_method: Systematic review of pathogens/diseases reportable to the OIE and present in the United States.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of pathogens: 42 (79%) of 53.
role_in_analysis: Review outcome used to characterize the extent of wildlife involvement among livestock diseases in the United States.
quantitative_result: 42 (79%) of the 53 diseases listed as present had a potential wildlife component.
evidence_quote: Our review of these pathogens identified 42 (79%) which have a potential wildlife component associated with the transmission, maintenance, or life cycle of the pathogen, and 21 (40%) are known to be zoonotic (Tables 1 and 2 ).
section: 2. Status of diseases at the livestock–wildlife interface in the United States

measure_name: Wildlife component among cattle diseases
what_it_represents: The number of OIE-reportable cattle diseases present in the United States that have a wildlife component.
measurement_method: Review classification of OIE-reportable diseases affecting cattle.
metric_or_unit: 6 out of 8 diseases.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of wildlife-component occurrence within the cattle disease category.
quantitative_result: 6 out of 8 cattle diseases present in the United States had a wildlife component.
evidence_quote: Of the OIE reportable diseases affecting cattle, 6 out of 8 are present in the United States and have a wildlife component; 3 have zoonotic potential.
section: 2. Status of diseases at the livestock–wildlife interface in the United States

measure_name: Pairwise genetic distance (SNPs) by host species
what_it_represents: Genetic distance among M. bovis strains within cattle, red deer, and wild boar host groups.
measurement_method: The distribution of pairwise SNP distance was obtained by applying the Hamming distance.
metric_or_unit: SNPs
role_in_analysis: Used to group and compare genetic distances by host species.
quantitative_result: 382 SNPs within cattle; 397 SNPs within red deer; and 398 within wild boar.
evidence_quote: Grouping by host species revealed that the mean genetic distance within each group is similar (382 SNPs within cattle; 397 SNPs within red deer; and 398 within wild boar)

measure_name: Zero SNP differences between host species
what_it_represents: Genetically indistinguishable M. bovis isolates occurring within and between host species, used to indicate possible intra- and inter-specific transmission events.
measurement_method: Pairwise comparison of absolute SNP distances between strains.
metric_or_unit: 0 SNP differences
role_in_analysis: Used to identify possible intra- and inter-specific transmission events.
quantitative_result: Zero-SNP links occurred between red deer and wild boar.
evidence_quote: Links with zero SNP differences were identified within the same host species (cattle– cattle and wild boar–wild boar) and between different host species (red deer–wild boar), suggesting intra- and inter-specific transmission events.

measure_name: Interface WB / PF transmission direction
what_it_represents: Whether ASF transmission between wild boar and pig farms was represented as wild-boar-to-pig-farm transmission only or in both directions.
measurement_method: Team model transmission assumptions, summarised in Table 1 and described for each team.
metric_or_unit: Categorical direction: "WB to PF" or "Both directions".
role_in_analysis: A model component used to evaluate the effects of pig-farm control measures on epidemic spread among wild boar.
quantitative_result: Alternative control measures in pig farms had relative differences in detected wild boar cases of at most about 10% compared with baseline.
evidence_quote: All teams (including Massey and INRAE teams that modelled transmission from pig farms to wild boar) concluded that the alternative control measures in pig farms had little or no effect on the spread of the epidemic among wild boar compared to the baseline scenario, with relative differences in detected cases of at most about 10% (Fig. 11A).

measure_name: Force of infection between wild boar and pig farms
what_it_represents: Cross-host ASF transmission from wild boar to pig farms and, for some teams, from pig farms to wild boar.
measurement_method: Teams modelled a force of infection between host populations; the CIRAD team instead modelled pig-farm risk using smoothed wild-boar case data.
metric_or_unit: Model force of infection; no numerical unit reported.
role_in_analysis: Used in team models to represent transmission across host populations.
quantitative_result: The UK and WUR teams modelled wild-boar-to-pig-farm force of infection but not pig-farm-to-wild-boar transmission, whereas INRAE and Massey modelled both directions.
evidence_quote: the UK (Dankwa et al., 2022) and the WUR teams modelled the force of infection from wild boar to pig farms but not from pig farms to wild boar as they found no strong evidence, based on the synthetic data provided, of transmission from pig farms to wild boar; finally, the INRAE (Beaunée et al., 2022) and Massey (Han and Vignes, 2022) teams defined a force of infection in both directions, from wild boar to pig farms and from pig farms to wild boar.
section: 3.1. Qualitative comparison of the teams’ approaches

measure_name: Species-specific HEV seroprevalence
what_it_represents: Comparison of HEV antibody prevalence across domestic pigs and sympatric wild ungulate species.
measurement_method: Specific antibodies against HEV were determined using a commercial double-antigen multispecies sandwich HEV ELISA 4.0®; seroprevalence was calculated as the coefficient of positive samples to total animals analysed.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%), positives/total, and P value.
role_in_analysis: Species was an explanatory variable, and seroprevalence in fattening pigs was statistically compared with wildlife.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was 97.0% in fattening pigs and 12.6% in wild ungulates; fattening pigs had significantly higher seroprevalence than wildlife (P<0.001).
evidence_quote: A total of 49 (12.6 %; 95 %CI: 9.3–15.9) of the 390 wild ungulates tested showed seropositivity to HEV (Table S1). Significantly higher seroprevalence was found in fattening pigs than in wildlife (P<0.001).

measure_name: Montanera-fattening production phase
what_it_represents: The outdoor fattening period during which pigs are in contact with sympatric wild boar and red deer.
measurement_method: Pigs were sampled longitudinally at the end of production phases, including fattening; sympatric wild boar and red deer were collected during the same study periods.
metric_or_unit: Pig seroprevalence (%), positives/total, relative risk, and P value.
role_in_analysis: Production phase, including montanera-fattening phase, was analysed as an explanatory variable for HEV seropositivity.
quantitative_result: Fattening-phase pig seroprevalence was 97.0% (514/530) and was statistically higher than at rearing phase (RR = 1.9; P < 0.001).
evidence_quote: In addition, the frequency of seropositivity at fattening phase was statistically higher than that observed at rearing phase (RR = 1.9; P < 0.001).

measure_name: True prevalence of M bovis infection in domestic cattle
what_it_represents: The estimated prevalence of M bovis infection in cattle within the wildlife-livestock interface area.
measurement_method: True prevalence was estimated from apparent prevalence adjusted for the sensitivity and specificity of serial CFT-CCT tests, using HMC, PCR assay, or both as the gold standard.
metric_or_unit: 0.86% (95% confidence interval, 0.24% to 1.49%)
role_in_analysis: Quantified infection in the domestic host population for comparison with the WR population and interpretation of potential transmission.
quantitative_result: M bovis infection was confirmed in 31 of 24,400 cattle.
evidence_quote: In our study, none of the 142 inspected WRs were identified as M bovis positive; however, M bovis infection was confirmed in 31 of 24,400 cattle.

measure_name: Apparent prevalence of M bovis infection in WRs
what_it_represents: The detected prevalence of M bovis infection in wild ruminants within the wildlife-livestock interface area.
measurement_method: WR carcass samples suspicious for M bovis infection were processed by HMC; because none were positive via HMC, PCR was not performed.
metric_or_unit: 0.00%; 95% confidence interval, 0.00% to 2.3%; statistical power, 11.4%
role_in_analysis: Assessed infection in the wild host population and the study's ability to detect infection, informing the conclusion regarding cattle-to-WR transmission.
quantitative_result: None of 142 WRs were identified as infected with M bovis.
evidence_quote: The apparent prevalence of M bovis in WRs from the WLIA was calculated as 0.00%; a posteriori assessment indicated that the statistical power value was inadequate (11.4%) to detect M bovis–infected WR for this population.

measure_name: Gorongosa National Park Buffer Zone (GNPBZ) versus rest of district (ROD)
what_it_represents: Farm-village proximity to the Gorongosa National Park and, implicitly, differing opportunity for contact between warthogs and domestic pigs.
measurement_method: Villages were grouped by distance from the GNP boundary: six edge villages less than 10 km away versus 12 villages at an average of 15 km from the boundary.
metric_or_unit: Distance to GNP boundary (<10 km versus average 15 km); ASFV sero-prevalence (%) and odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Geographic interface category used to compare ASFV sero-prevalence in domestic pigs.
quantitative_result: ASFV sero-prevalence was 12.5% in GNPBZ pigs and 7.8% in ROD pigs (OR = 0.59, P = 0.05).
evidence_quote: The ASFV sero-prevalence in pigs from GNPBZ was 12.5%, 95% CI [7.4–17.6] and in pigs from the ROD was 7.8%, 95% CI [5.4–10.3] (Table 2). However, these differences were only marginally significant (OR = 0.59, P = 0.05).
section: Results — Detection of antibodies against ASFV — Domestic pigs

measure_name: Antibodies to tick salivary proteins (rOmTSGP1) in domestic pigs
what_it_represents: Recent exposure of domestic pigs to soft-tick bites, a vector-mediated connection between wildlife-associated ticks and domestic pigs.
measurement_method: ELISA for antibodies to the recombinant salivary lipocalin protein (rOmTSGP1) of the Ornithodoros moubata complex.
metric_or_unit: Sero-prevalence (%) in pigs and farms; odds ratio and P value comparing GNPBZ and ROD.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare domestic-pig soft-tick exposure between the wildlife-proximate GNPBZ and the ROD.
quantitative_result: Approximately 45% of GNPBZ pigs were sero-positive compared with 28.9% of ROD pigs; the difference was significant (OR = 0.48, P = 0002).
evidence_quote: Approximately 45% of pigs (64/140 sera) in the GNPBZ were sero-positive to tick salivary proteins (95% CI [37.3–54.3]), compared to 28.9%, 95% CI [24.8–33.4] of pigs (129/445) in the ROD.
section: Results — Detection of antibodies against tick salivary protein — Domestic pigs

measure_name: Swamp Deer-livestock interaction level by study site
what_it_represents: Contrasting exposure settings: high Swamp Deer-livestock interaction at JJ and minimal interaction at JT.
measurement_method: Sites were selected based on varying levels of livestock interaction; JJ had reported daily livestock use, while JT was assumed to have minimal interaction.
metric_or_unit: Categorical site setting (high interaction versus minimal interaction); JJCR use reported as more than 1,300 livestock daily.
role_in_analysis: Study-site interaction setting under which Swamp Deer parasitic loads were compared using a Mann-Whitney U test.
quantitative_result: The overall mean Swamp Deer EPG was 487.5±46.30 at JJ and 363.64±49.97 at JT, with a significant difference between sites (p<0.01).
evidence_quote: The load of different parasitic ova in the Swamp Deer population at both sites revealed an overall mean EPG of 487.5±46.30 at JJ and 363.64±49.97 at JT. There was a significant difference in parasitic load between the two study sites (p<0.01, Mann–Whitney U test).

measure_name: Parasite prevalence in Swamp Deer and livestock at JJ and JT
what_it_represents: Quantitative comparison of parasitic-ova prevalence across the wild host (Swamp Deer) and domestic host (livestock) in the two interaction settings.
measurement_method: Coprological screening; prevalence calculated as the number of infected individuals divided by total individuals sampled, multiplied by 100.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence percentage.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive cross-host and cross-site comparison of parasite infection.
quantitative_result: Swamp Deer prevalence was 15.38% at JJ and 12.69% at JT; livestock prevalence was 95.41% at JJ and 60% at JT.
evidence_quote: Of the total samples collected and screened for parasitic ova, the overall prevalence of parasitic ova in the Swamp Deer population at JJ and JT were 15.38% and 12.69%, respectively, whereas the overall parasitic prevalence in livestock population at JJ and JT were 95.41 % and 60%, respectively.

measure_name: Relative spatial risk of AI incursion into poultry via wild birds
what_it_represents: The relative spatial risk that poultry flocks become infected with AI via wild birds in each 10 × 10 km grid cell.
measurement_method: A risk map derived from the classical epidemiological risk equation, combining the transmission parameter, susceptible poultry flocks, and infected wild birds; infected wild birds are represented as relative wild-bird abundance multiplied by AI prevalence.
metric_or_unit: Relative risk on a 10 × 10 km Ordnance Survey grid; visualised using six quantiles.
role_in_analysis: Primary model outcome used to map, compare, and target surveillance according to spatial incursion risk.
quantitative_result: The top two quantiles (relative risk > log10–3.36) contains almost 81% of total GB risk.
evidence_quote: It was not possible to estimate absolute risk due to a lack of knowledge regarding the amount of contact between wild birds and poultry; hence we measured relative spatial risk on a 10 × 10 km Ordnance Survey (OS) grid10.

measure_name: Poultry production type and outdoor-production exposure classification
what_it_represents: Poultry husbandry/production categories, including whether holdings are indoor or outdoor; outdoor or mixed husbandry was treated as increased exposure to wild birds.
measurement_method: Poultry demographic database information on poultry species, usual stock numbers, and an indoor/outdoor indicator; holdings reporting mixed systems were classified as outdoor.
metric_or_unit: Categorical production type j, with production-type-specific transmission parameter β(j) and risk ratio (RR).
role_in_analysis: Used to assign production-type-specific transmission parameters in the spatial risk model.
quantitative_result: Outdoor duck had a risk ratio of 24.5 and β(j) of 2.90 × 10−3.
evidence_quote: Many farms indicate both indoor and outdoor production; we assumed that any indication of outdoor production increased the risk of exposure to wild birds, and so all farms with mixed husbandry systems were categorised as having outdoor production.
section: Methods — Parameter estimation — Poultry flock density

measure_name: Host species
what_it_represents: Comparison of pathogen exposure among domestic cats and the two wild felid species (bobcats and puma).
measurement_method: Host species was included as a predictor in a Bayesian hierarchical logistic regression of pathogen exposure.
metric_or_unit: Probability of pathogen exposure; regression coefficient and 95% CI.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether exposure differed across wild and domestic host species.
quantitative_result: Exposure increased from domestic cat to bobcat to puma (coefficient and 95% CI: 0.606, 0.061–1.111).
evidence_quote: As predicted, the probability of pathogen exposure differed among host species (Table 2, Fig. 2). Exposure increased from domestic cat to bobcat to puma (coefficient and 95% CI: 0.606, 0.061–1.111).
section: Effects of host species and pathogen mode of transmission

measure_name: Distance to urban edge / proximity to the wildland–urban interface
what_it_represents: Spatial proximity of felid capture locations to urban boundaries, used as an operationalisation of proximity to the wildland–urban interface.
measurement_method: Euclidean distance from each georeferenced capture location to the nearest urban edge.
metric_or_unit: Euclidean distance; used as a landscape predictor of probability of pathogen exposure.
role_in_analysis: Included with land-cover predictors in Bayesian hierarchical logistic regression models of pathogen exposure within each host species.
quantitative_result: Proximity to the wildland–urban interface did not generally increase the probability of disease exposure in wild or domestic felids.
evidence_quote: In addition to land cover surrounding capture locations, we also calculated Euclidean distance of capture location to the nearest urban edge, as determined using the Urban Areas polygon layer from the US Census Bureau (Tiger/Line Shapefiles) and the Near tool in ArcGIS (v9.3.1; ESRI, Redlands, California, USA).

measure_name: PCR detection and pooled prevalence of MG and Starling mycoplasma in wild and domestic bird compartments
what_it_represents: Comparison of Mycoplasma detection between wild birds around poultry farms and domestic poultry sampled in the same area, including ducks described as in close contact with positive starlings.
measurement_method: Real-time PCR screening of pooled oropharyngeal, cloacal, or faecal samples targeting MG 16S rRNA, mgc2, and the Starling-mycoplasma mgc2-like gene; pooled prevalence was estimated from the PCR results.
metric_or_unit: Number of positive pools over number tested; estimated pooled prevalence (%) with 95% confidence intervals; PCR cycle threshold (Ct).
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of pathogen detection and prevalence across wild and domestic compartments to assess possible infectious contacts and spillover to poultry.
quantitative_result: The Starling mycoplasma was confirmed in 17 of 19 starling cloacal pools from 2016–2017 (32% estimated pooled prevalence), three starling cloacal pools from 2019–2020 (24%), and one wagtail cloacal pool (1.5%), whereas backyard-chicken pools positive for MG 16S rRNA had no Starling-mycoplasma detection.
evidence_quote: In wild birds that were positive for MG 16S rRNA, the presence of the Starling mycoplasma DNA was confirmed in 17 out of the 19 cloacal pools of 2016–2017 starlings (32% [95% CI: 18–50], mean Ct 34.1), in the three cloacal pools of 2019–2020 starlings (24% [95% CI: 4–64], mean Ct 39.9) and in the cloacal pool of wagtails (1.5% [95% CI: 0–7.9], Ct 39.1) (Table 3 and Figure 3).
section: 3.3 Distribution of the novel Mycoplasma sp. at the wild–domestic bird interface

measure_name: Close-contact exposure of free-range ducks to positive starlings
what_it_represents: A shared, close wild-domestic setting in which free-range ducks were exposed to starlings positive for the new mycoplasma.
measurement_method: PCR screening of free-range ducks and comparison with PCR-positive starlings sampled around the duck farm.
metric_or_unit: 80 free-range ducks screened; detection/non-detection of the new Starling mycoplasma.
role_in_analysis: Assessment of whether the novel mycoplasma detected in starlings was also detected in poultry living in close conditions.
quantitative_result: The new Starling mycoplasma was not detected in 80 free-range ducks in close contact with positive starlings.
evidence_quote: As the new Starling mycoplasma was not detected in free-range ducks (n = 80) in close contact with positive starlings, nor in backyard (n = 320) and free-range commercial (n = 720) chickens of the area, it might not infect poultry.

measure_name: Species
what_it_represents: Domestic cattle and wild ungulate host species, used to compare BTV and SBV exposure across the wild-domestic host community.
measurement_method: Animals were classified by species and seroprevalence was calculated as the proportion positive for viral antibodies; species was evaluated as an explanatory variable in bivariate tests and GLMMs.
metric_or_unit: Number positive/number analysed (%) seroprevalence; GLMM estimate and 95%CI.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory variable in bivariate association testing and generalized linear mixed models of BTV and SBV seroprevalence.
quantitative_result: For SBV, seroprevalence was 37.0% in cattle, 23.5% in fallow deer, 16.8% in red deer and 2.0% in wild boar; the species association had p < .001.
evidence_quote: With respect to SBV, a statistically significant pattern of decreasing seroprevalence was observed for the species tested: cattle > fallow deer > red deer > wild boar.

measure_name: Direct contact rates between buffaloes and cattle
what_it_represents: Risk of direct contact between buffaloes and cattle across space and time.
measurement_method: Spatially explicit multi-agent model maps contact risk; direct contact is defined as buffalo and cattle agents occupying the same cell at the same time.
metric_or_unit: Direct contact rates; contacts in space and time.
role_in_analysis: Primary model output used to analyse spatial factors influencing contact risk.
quantitative_result: The model simulations showed that contacts occurred up to 6 km from the fence.
evidence_quote: The model was developed to create risk maps of direct contact rates between buffaloes and cattle in space and time. The broader objective was to analyse and describe spatial factors inﬂuencing contact risk by examining the inﬂuence of the landscape.

measure_name: Number of buffalo–cattle contacts
