what_it_represents: The number of direct contacts between buffaloes and cattle simulated by the model.
measurement_method: Contacts were modelled as the presence of buffalo and cattle agents in the same cell at the same time; output variation was assessed in sensitivity analyses.
metric_or_unit: Number of contacts; percentage of output variation per percent of input variation.
role_in_analysis: Model output in one-at-a-time and Plackett–Burman sensitivity analyses.
quantitative_result: A 1% variation in buffalo movement input gave a 0.94% variation in contacts, and a 1% variation in cattle movement input gave a 1.07% variation in contacts.
evidence_quote: The outputs were the number of buffaloes outside the park and the number of buffalo–cattle con- tacts.

measure_name: Overlap between serotypes in companion animals and wildlife
what_it_represents: The number and proportion of dog and cat isolates with a serotype also isolated in wild birds, wild reptiles, or wild mammals.
measurement_method: Comparison of serotypes isolated from companion animals with serotypes isolated from wildlife, reported in Table 2.
metric_or_unit: Number of serotypes (n) and proportion (%) of isolates.
role_in_analysis: Examined overlap at the companion animal-wildlife interface.
quantitative_result: The highest similarity was seen between wild birds and cats, with 81% of isolates in cats being of a serotype that was also isolated from wild birds.
evidence_quote: There were 268 and 133 isolates from dogs and cats, respectively, that were of a serotype that was also isolated from wildlife. The highest similarity was seen between wild birds and cats, with 81% of isolates in cats being of a serotype that was also isolated from wild birds.

measure_name: Exposure to cattle / overlap of elk with cattle
what_it_represents: A binary categorisation of elk herds according to their contact or overlap with cattle.
measurement_method: Five herds in high-cattle-density areas were classified as “exposed” and five herds with no or limited contact with cattle as “non-exposed”; overlap was analysed as a binary variable.
metric_or_unit: Binary variable (exposed/non-exposed).
role_in_analysis: Tested for association with individual coproscopic results using a χ2 test.
quantitative_result: The five elk herds exposed to cattle had lower coproscopy prevalence than non-exposed herds (χ2 = 259; p<0.001).
evidence_quote: The five elk herds exposed to cattle had lower prevalence by coproscopy than the non-exposed herds (χ2 = 259; p<0.001) (Table 3).
section: Results—Effect of cattle density and elk migration

measure_name: Cattle density
what_it_represents: The density of beef cattle within elk or herd home ranges.
measurement_method: Area-weighted average of beef-cattle density in districts overlapping the home range, based on census data.
metric_or_unit: beef cow /km2
role_in_analysis: Included as a predictor in logistic and multivariable regression models of F. magna coproscopy prevalence and serological results.
quantitative_result: Herd prevalence was negatively associated with cattle density (OR = 0.26, 95% CI [0.2, 0.34]).
evidence_quote: The herd prevalence was negatively associated with cattle density (OR = 0.26, 95% CI [0.2, 0.34]) and with the proportion of migratory individuals (OR = 0.46, 95% CI [0.41, 0.52] for a 10% increase) (Fig 2).
section: Results—Effect of cattle density and elk migration

measure_name: Bird groups
what_it_represents: Wild and domestic bird categories used to display AIV serological distribution.
measurement_method: Serum samples were evaluated by c-ELISA, and randomly selected reactive samples were tested by haemagglutination inhibition (HI).
metric_or_unit: Frequency numbers and percentages of HA sero-subtypes by bird group.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of AIV serological distribution across migratory birds, resident wild birds, and domestic bird groups.
quantitative_result: The frequency of H5 was 65.9% (27/41) in migratory birds, 66.7% (24/36) in resident wild birds, 76.3% (29/38) in nomadic ducks, 61.7% (29/47) in household ducks, and 71.4% (5/7) in household chickens.
evidence_quote: In migratory birds, the frequency of the H5 serotype was found to be the most prevalent (65.9%; 27/41) followed by H9 (56%; 23/41), H1 (41.5%; 17/41), H12 (41.5%; 17/41) and H2 (34.2%; 14/41). In resident wild birds, the distribution of HA serotypes was 66.7% (24/36) H5, 30.6% (11/36) H9 and 25% (9/36) H2. In domestic birds, the HA serotype frequencies were 61.7% for H5 (29/47) and 38.3% for H9 (18/47) in household ducks, 76.3% for H5 (29/38), 55.3% for H2 (21/38) and 36.8% for H9 (14/38) in nomadic ducks, and 71.4% for H5 (5/7) and 28.5% for H9 (2/7) in household chickens (Table 1).

measure_name: Rincp
what_it_represents: Introduction risk of influenza virus by wild birds for each “Consejo Popular” (cp).
measurement_method: A weighted sum of the density of rice fields, important wild waterfowl areas, and permanent wetlands at the “Consejo Popular” level.
metric_or_unit: Normalized introduction-risk value; areas with ECDF values ≥0.85 were classified as high risk.
role_in_analysis: Input to the wild-bird-to-domestic-animal transmission model.
quantitative_result: The risk of an AIV introduction was high for 227 (15%) of the 1512 “Consejo Popular” in Cuba.
evidence_quote: The risk of an AIV introduction (Figure 3) was high for 227 (15%) of the 1512 “Consejo Popular” in Cuba.

measure_name: Rsp,cp
what_it_represents: Probability of AIV transmission from wild birds to domestic livestock or poultry, by species and production type, in each “Consejo Popular”.
measurement_method: The normalized wild-bird introduction-risk value was multiplied by normalized livestock or poultry density, stratified by commercial chickens, backyard chickens, commercial ducks, commercial swine, and backyard swine.
metric_or_unit: Normalized relative risk; “Consejo Popular” with ECDF values ≥0.98 were classified as high risk.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative estimation and spatial comparison of high-risk areas for transmission from wild birds to domestic animals.
quantitative_result: There were 21 (1.4%) higher-risk “Consejo Popular” for commercial ducks, 46 (3.0%) for commercial and backyard poultry and 35 (2.3%) for commercial and backyard swine.
evidence_quote: The high-risk “Consejo Popular” for AIV transmission from wild birds to livestock varied depending on the species (Figure 5). There were 21 (1.4%) higher-risk “Consejo Popular” for commercial ducks, 46 (3.0%) for commercial and backyard poultry and 35 (2.3%) for commercial and backyard swine.

measure_name: African buffalo perceived as a risk for disease transmission to cattle
what_it_represents: Respondents' perception of buffalo as a source of disease transmission to cattle.
measurement_method: Semi-structured questionnaire administered through in-person interview.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of respondents.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive assessment of farmers' knowledge of FMD epidemiology at the interface.
quantitative_result: A majority of respondents (92%) reported African buffalo as a risk for disease transmission to cattle.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, the African buﬀalo was reported by the majority of respondents (92%) as representing a risk for disease transmission to cattle.

measure_name: Wild/domestic birds group versus wild birds group
what_it_represents: Phylogenetically defined host-composition groups: one containing both domestic and wild bird isolates and one exclusively containing wild bird isolates.
measurement_method: Phylogenetic analyses of the internal genes of Jiangxi H5N6 viruses.
metric_or_unit: Group type (wild/domestic bird group; wild bird group) and estimated tMRCA.
role_in_analysis: Groups were compared to infer independent evolutionary processes and differences in median divergence time.
quantitative_result: The median divergence time of viruses in the wild/domestic birds group was between March 2009 and November 2011, whereas the divergence time in the wild birds group was approximately 1–3 years later in most internal genes.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, the median estimates of tMRCA suggested two independent evolutionary processes of Jiangxi H5N6 viruses in each group. It is estimated that the median divergence time of viruses in the wild/domestic birds group was between March 2009 and November 2011. By contrast, the divergence time of viruses in the wild birds group was approximately 1–3 years later in most internal genes (except for the PB2 gene) (Table 1, Fig. S11−16).
section: Evolutionary analysis of internal genes of Jiangxi H5N6 viruses from wild birds

measure_name: AIV isolation rate by host domain
what_it_represents: The proportion of sampled wild birds and domestic birds from which AIVs were isolated.
measurement_method: Surveillance sampling and virus isolation from wild birds and domestic ducks and chickens.
metric_or_unit: Percent and isolates/samples: 2.87 % (14/488) for wild birds; 11.58 % (157/1356) for domestic birds.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of AIV surveillance results across wild and domestic bird hosts.
quantitative_result: AIV isolation rates were 2.87 % in wild birds and 11.58 % in domestic birds.
evidence_quote: The isolation rates for AIVs were 2.87 % (14/488) for wild birds and 11.58 % (157/1356) for domestic birds (Fig. 1).

measure_name: FMD percentage sero-positivity (PS) in cattle and buffalo
what_it_represents: Serotype-specific FMDV antibody positivity in domestic cattle and wild buffalo sampled in livestock-wildlife interface areas.
measurement_method: SPCE serotyping of 3ABC-NSP ELISA-positive serum samples, with PS calculated as serotype-specific SPCE-positive samples divided by NSPE-positive samples.
metric_or_unit: Percentage sero-positivity (%)
role_in_analysis: Descriptive and comparative analysis of PS variation for FMDV types O, A and O&A between cattle and buffalo, using chi-square and independent t-tests.
quantitative_result: Cattle had higher overall seropositivity than buffalo: type A, 53.9% versus 30.1%; type O, 66.9% versus 54.8%; and mixed type A&O, 36.4% versus 24.7%.
evidence_quote: Similarly, out of 154 NSPE positive cattle samples analyzed 53.9% (83) of CI (69 – 98), 66.9% (103) of CI (88 – 118) and 36.4% (56) of CI (44 – 70) had FMDV antibodies specific to type A, O and mixed sero-reactions respectively.

measure_name: Livestock seroprevalence (%)
what_it_represents: CCHFV seroprevalence in livestock at the household level, used to assess the association between human and livestock exposure.
measurement_method: Estimated at the household level and merged with the human data.
role_in_analysis: Independent variable in mixed effects multivariable logistic regression analysis of human CCHFV seropositivity.
quantitative_result: >30% livestock seroprevalence was associated with higher odds of human exposure (OR 2.36, 95% CI: 1.06–5.23; P-value 0.041).

measure_name: Wild bird counts around poultry farms by wetland location
what_it_represents: Wild-bird presence around poultry farms and its relationship to whether farms are located in wetlands.
measurement_method: A study targeted HPAI H5 host species or species groups and counted wild birds around infected poultry farms in the Netherlands.
metric_or_unit: Counts; farms located in wetlands versus farms not located in wetlands.
role_in_analysis: Reported as evidence that wild-bird presence and wetland vicinity were associated with HPAI H5 GsGd virus introductions into poultry farms.
quantitative_result: Increased wild bird counts around poultry farms were much more pronounced for farms located in wetlands than farms not located in wetlands.
evidence_quote: Increased wild bird (i.e., Eurasian wigeon, tufted duck, Anatidae, Laridae) counts around poultry farms were much more pronounced for farms located in wetlands than farms not located in wetlands [166], which confirmed earlier findings on distance to open water as a risk factor for HPAI GsGd H5 introduction [167,168].
section: 3.5. HPAI H5 Virus Introductions into Poultry Farms by Wild Birds

measure_name: Timing of peak wild-duck densities around HPAI H5-infected poultry farms
what_it_represents: Seasonal overlap between wild-duck density around infected poultry farms and HPAI H5N8 poultry outbreaks.
measurement_method: A study targeting HPAI H5 host species or species groups assessed timing of peak densities around infected poultry farms in the Netherlands.
metric_or_unit: November–February peak densities; outbreaks between late November and late December 2016.
role_in_analysis: Reported as evidence of seasonal variation in wild-duck presence associated with poultry-farm introductions.
quantitative_result: The peak densities coincided with the timing of the HPAI H5N8 outbreaks in poultry.
evidence_quote: A study targeting HPAI H5 host species or species groups (Eurasian wigeon, tufted duck, Anatidae, Laridae) showed that the timing of peak densities of Eurasian wigeons and other Anatidae around HPAI H5 infected poultry farms in the Netherlands (i.e., November–February) coincided with the timing of the HPAI H5N8 outbreaks in poultry, between late November and late December 2016 [166].
section: 3.5. HPAI H5 Virus Introductions into Poultry Farms by Wild Birds

measure_name: Host-origin comparison of MLVA genotypes

measure_name: M. conjunctivae apparent prevalence by host species
what_it_represents: Detection and prevalence of M. conjunctivae in wild chamois, domestic sheep, and mouflon, enabling comparison of infection patterns across wild and domestic hosts.

evidence_quote: Mycoplasma conjunctivae was confirmed in three out of four sheep flocks sampled with an overall prevalence of 17.0% (95% CI 11.1–25.0%) and a within-flock prevalence that ranged from 6.9% (95% CI 1.9–22.0%) to 33.3% (95% CI 19.2–51.2%).

measure_name: Wildlife-livestock contact

quantitative_result: Wildlife-livestock contact was included among the constraints identified in the study area.

measure_name: Group interface classification
what_it_represents: The primary group of interest: wildlife, humans, or livestock animals.
measurement_method: Retained papers were categorized by group interface.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of publications in interface categories.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive classification of the 226 retained publications by the wild, human, and livestock disease interfaces they addressed.
quantitative_result: 163 publications addressed diseases exclusively in wild animals; 12 dealt with the wildlife-human interface; 25 addressed transmission and prevalence at the wildlife-livestock interface; and 26 pertained to all interfaces.
evidence_quote: A total of 163 publications addressed diseases that occurred exclusively in wild animals, conducted research solely with wild animals or took samples only from wildlife. In contrast, 12 papers dealt with diseases at the wildlife-human interface, and all of these diseases were zoonotic. In these 12 studies, humans and animals were sampled or results reported in humans and animals were discussed. Moreover, 25 publications addressed transmission and prevalence of diseases at the wildlife-livestock interface. Last but not least, 26 publications pertained to all interfaces, i.e., between wild animals, domesticated animals, and humans (see Figure 13).

measure_name: Disease distribution by host domain and TFCA
what_it_represents: Whether each disease may infect wildlife, domestic animals and humans, and its reported/likely presence in each transfrontier conservation area.
measurement_method: A categorical tabulation of diseases across TFCAs using host-domain and occurrence-status codes.
metric_or_unit: W, D and H host-domain codes; +, − and ? occurrence-status codes.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive representation of diseases shared across wildlife, domestic-animal and human domains; not used in a reported statistical analysis.
quantitative_result: The Great Limpopo TFCA is marked as having foot and mouth disease, bovine tuberculosis, brucellosis, canine distemper virus, African trypanosomiasis, malignant catarrhal fever, Rift Valley fever, anthrax, rabies, African swine fever, African horse sickness, heartwater, theileriosis and echinococcosis and cysticercosis present or likely present.
evidence_quote: Important diseases of wildlife, domestic animals and humans and their distribution in the transfrontier conservation areas (TFCAs) being developed in southern Africa (revised from Cumming and Atkinson, 2012).

measure_name: Seroprevalence of FMDV at the wildlife-cattle interface
what_it_represents: A comparison of FMDV antibody positivity between wildlife and cattle sampled in the study area.
measurement_method: Serum samples were screened for antibodies to the FMDV nonstructural polypeptide 3ABC using ELISA; samples with PI ≥50% were positive.
metric_or_unit: Number positive (%) and chi-square, P value, odds ratio, and 95% CI.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of overall FMDV seroprevalence between wildlife and cattle at the wildlife-cattle interface.
evidence_quote: Comparison of the overall seroprevalences of FMDV at the wildlife-cattle interface (Table 2) showed that detectable antibodies to FMDV were significantly higher (P < 0.05) in cattle 65.67% than in wildlife 24.0%.

measure_name: Seroprevalence of antibodies to Anaplasma spp. by wildlife and domestic species
what_it_represents: The proportion of sampled wildlife and domestic animals with antibodies to Anaplasma spp. at the wildlife/livestock interface.
measurement_method: Serum samples were analyzed by competitive inhibition enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (CI-ELISA).
metric_or_unit: Number positive/number tested and percentage positive
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of Anaplasma antibody prevalence across wildlife and domestic species at the wildlife/livestock interface.
quantitative_result: Overall prevalences in bovines, sheep and goats were 97 %, 90 % and 85 %, respectively.
evidence_quote: High seroprevalence was also found in bovines, sheep and goats, with overall prevalences of 97 %, 90 % and 85 %, respectively (Table 1).

measure_name: Host animal category-specific C. burnetii prevalence in tick pools
what_it_represents: Comparison of C. burnetii-positive tick pools collected from domestic small ruminants (goats and sheep) and wild Indian long-eared hedgehogs.
measurement_method: Ticks of identical species from a single animal were combined into one tube, and pooled tick samples were screened for C. burnetii by real-time PCR.
metric_or_unit: number and percentage of C. burnetii positive tick pools (n[%])
role_in_analysis: Host-associated prevalence was compared statistically; Table 3 reports P-values for goat, sheep, and hedgehog host categories.
quantitative_result: Ticks collected from sheep and goats had positivity of 40% and 38%, respectively, compared to 2% for Indian long-eared hedgehogs.
evidence_quote: Ticks collected from sheep and goats were more likely infested with C. burnetii (40% and 38%, respectively) compared to Indian long-eared hedgehogs (2%).

measure_name: Phylogenetic genotype grouping of cattle outbreak viruses and wildlife samples
what_it_represents: Genetic relatedness of SAT2 viruses sampled from cattle and wildlife.
measurement_method: Partial VP1 sequencing and phylogenetic analysis.
metric_or_unit: Genotype grouping and nucleotide identity (nt id).
role_in_analysis: Used to compare genetic relationships between cattle outbreak viruses and wildlife samples.
quantitative_result: The majority of cattle outbreak viruses grouped in distinct genotypes separate from wildlife samples, while some wildlife and cattle viruses grouped together in genotypes A and E.
evidence_quote: In addition, the majority of these cattle outbreak viruses grouped in distinct genotypes separate from the wildlife samples from the KNP and Greater KNP Area.
section: 3.2 | Genetic relatedness of SAT2 outbreak viruses

measure_name: Nucleotide identity between the 2013/2014 cattle outbreak viruses and wildlife isolates
what_it_represents: Genetic similarity between the cattle outbreak viruses and viruses isolated from impala and buffalo in the Greater KNP/KNP area.
measurement_method: Pairwise comparison of partial VP1 nucleotide sequence data.
metric_or_unit: Percentage nucleotide identity (nt id).
role_in_analysis: Used to assess whether outbreak viruses had a genetic relationship to wildlife viruses.
quantitative_result: A historic impala isolate had an average 82.5% nt id with the 2013/2014 outbreak viruses; a 2015 impala virus had 80.3%–80.7% nt id.
evidence_quote: A historic impala isolate (KNP/51/93) showed the closest genetic relationship (average 82.5% nt id) with the SAT2 2013/2014 outbreak viruses.
section: 3.2 | Genetic relatedness of SAT2 outbreak viruses

measure_name: Comparative morphometric host-species grouping of F. hepatica adults
what_it_represents: Phenotypic comparison of liver flukes from the wild host (wild boar) and domestic hosts (sheep and cattle) from Galicia.
measurement_method: Standardized adult-fluke measurements analyzed using multivariate analyses, including principal component analysis.
metric_or_unit: Principal component contributions: PC1 91.0% and PC2 3.5% of overall variations.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of F. hepatica phenotypic variation among wild boar, sheep, and cattle host groups.
quantitative_result: The liver fluke population from wild boars presents an intermediate size between sheep and cattle populations (Fig. 4).
evidence_quote: The size and shape of liver-ﬂuke bodies were studied by multivariate analyses. A scatter plot of the ﬁrst two principal components (PC) is shown in Fig. 4.

measure_name: Host origin (wild or domestic)
what_it_represents: The wild-versus-domestic origin of hosts in the phylogenetic reconstruction.
measurement_method: Host origin was reconstructed as a discrete character across the refined phylogenetic tree using augur-traits.
metric_or_unit: Discrete categorical character: wild or domestic.
role_in_analysis: Used in phylogenetic analysis to reconstruct host origin across tree nodes and depict branch colour.
quantitative_result: The domestic-poultry virus was previously detected in a wild Blue-Winged Teal in Manitoba, Canada.
evidence_quote: The host status (live or dead) and origin (wild or domestic) were reconstructed as discrete characters across the refined tree using augur-traits from the Augur bioinformatics toolkit.

measure_name: AIV RT-PCR results across wild dabbling ducks and premise mallards
what_it_represents: Viral presence in wild ducks sampled within 100 km of the infected premises compared with captive premise mallards maintained on wetlands on the domestic premises.
measurement_method: Pooled oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs were tested by RT-PCR targeting the influenza A virus matrix gene, with additional H5 and H7 tests for non-negative samples.
metric_or_unit: Number and proportion RT-PCR positive or suspicious.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive cross-sector comparison of viral presence and exposure.
quantitative_result: Of the 140 wild birds swabbed, 77 (55 %, 95 % CI: 0.46–0.63) tested positive on RT-PCR for the matrix AIV gene; of 250 premise mallards swabbed on Day 12, 60 (24 %; 95 % CI: 0.19–0.30) tested positive for the matrix gene.
evidence_quote: Specifically, we describe: (1) AIV RT-PCR results from sick and dead birds and mammals within a 100 km radius of the IP, (2) AIV RT-PCR results from samples collected during live wild bird surveillance conducted within a 100 km radius of the IP, (3) AIV RT-PCR and serological results from samples collected from a captive flock of Mallards (Anas platyrhynchos) maintained in wetlands on the domestic premises, and (4) AIV targeted genomic sequencing results from water and sediment samples collected from wetlands on the domestic premises.

measure_name: Genetic similarity of pond H5 fragments to poultry and wildlife sequences
what_it_represents: The relationship of H5 genomic material in wetlands on the infected premises to sequences from domestic poultry and local wildlife.
measurement_method: Fragmentary H5 sequences from ponds were aligned to HA segment sequences from poultry on the infected premises and HPAI-positive local wildlife; best matches were assessed by number and strength of alignments.
metric_or_unit: Number of fragments with best matches and alignment strength; HP H5 as percentage of HA genomic fragments.
role_in_analysis: Assessed the likely origin of environmental H5 fragments across domestic poultry, wildlife, and premise wetlands.
quantitative_result: Within specimens where HP H5 was detected, it constituted only 1.4 % to 6.7 % of genomic fragments originating from HA segments.
evidence_quote: To assess their origin, the fragmentary H5 sequences recovered from the ponds were aligned to HA segment sequences recovered from the poultry involved in the IP and HPAI-positive local wildlife (Table 3, Fig. 4). This indicated that the poultry were the most likely source of the H5 fragments, based on the number of fragments having their best match to these bird-origin sequences as well as the strength of those alignments.

measure_name: Relative risk map for CoVs at the wild pig-domestic pig-human interface
what_it_represents: County-level relative risk combining pathogen availability in wild pigs, domestic pigs, and humans with interface-connectivity risk factors.
measurement_method: Risk factors were normalized from 0 to 1 and combined multiplicatively with equal weights.
metric_or_unit: Relative risk score, normalized 0 to 1 for each risk factor; county-level map.
role_in_analysis: Spatial risk assessment and mapping to triage surveillance resources.
quantitative_result: The paper presents a relative risk map and distribution of percentage risk values across counties.
evidence_quote: Each risk factor, Өr, is normalized from 0 to 1 using minimum-maximum normalization (i.e., with county values being relative to one another such that the highest score would be 1 and reflect the county with the highest risk factor score) to allow each risk factor to be considered equally.

measure_name: Backyard pig density
what_it_represents: Potential direct and indirect contact, and resulting transmission risk, between wild pigs and domestic pigs.
measurement_method: County-level backyard pig density data layer.
metric_or_unit: County.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity component (Cw-d) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as a data layer in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Backyard operations often have low biosecurity allowing direct and indirect contact with wild pigs thus areas with higher backyard pig densities would have higher risk of contact transmission among wild and domestic pigs

measure_name: Agricultural workers and county fairs
what_it_represents: Human-domestic pig interaction and contact opportunity.
measurement_method: State-level agricultural-worker data and county-level county-fair data.
metric_or_unit: State for agricultural workers; county for county fairs.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity components (Cd-h) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as interface-connectivity data layers in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Agricultural workers (including animal caretakers and slaughterhouse workers) have the highest contact rates with domestic pigs

measure_name: Wild pig hunters and control personnel
what_it_represents: Human-wild pig contact opportunity.
measurement_method: State-level hunting and wild-pig-control data.
metric_or_unit: State.
role_in_analysis: Interface-connectivity components (Cw-h) of the relative risk framework and map.
quantitative_result: Included as interface-connectivity data layers in the relative risk mapping.
evidence_quote: Areas with more hunting have more wild pig-human contact

measure_name: Bat species density
what_it_represents: Opportunity for contact and spillover of coronaviruses between bats and wild pigs.
measurement_method: County-level bat species density data.
metric_or_unit: County.
role_in_analysis: Wild pig-bat interface-connectivity component (Cw-b) of the relative risk framework.
quantitative_result: Included once in the overall relative-risk map.
evidence_quote: Higher bat species densities present a higher spillover risk for CoVs into pigs that could act as intermediate hosts for further evolution or transmission to humans

measure_name: Regional Ardeidae richness
what_it_represents: A proxy for the regional species pool of wild ardeid bird hosts, derived from summed individual species habitat suitability distributions.
measurement_method: Habitat suitability of each of 14 ardeid species was modelled using an ensemble of random forest, boosted regression trees, and generalised additive models; individual suitability distributions were summed.
metric_or_unit: Ardeidae richness; number of species from the regional pool capable of colonising suitable patches.
role_in_analysis: Covariate in simple and multiple inhomogeneous Poisson models of JEV outbreaks in piggeries.
quantitative_result: JEV outbreaks were associated with ardeid richness (RR = 2.51; 95% C.I. 1.003–6.284).
evidence_quote: The model with the best fit and performance (Table 1; Supplementary Table S4) demonstrated strong associations between JEV outbreaks and ardeid richness (RR = 2.51; 95% C.I. 1.003–6.284), temporary surface water presence (RR = 1.08; 95% C.I. 1.023–1.135), proximity to waterways (RR = 0.91; 95% C.I. 0.844–0.977), increasing amount of cultivated land (RR = 1.03; 95% C.I. 1.017–1.039), increasing mean grassland RCC (RR = 7.57; 95% C.I. 1.786–32.11), and hydrological flow accumulation (RR = 1.001; 95% C.I. 1.0001–1.003).

measure_name: Feral pig habitat suitability
what_it_represents: Modeled suitability of landscapes for feral pigs, compared with JEV outbreaks in domestic-pig piggeries.
measurement_method: Feral pig observations recorded from 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2020 were obtained from GBIF to model feral pig habitat suitability.
metric_or_unit: Habitat suitability; unit not stated.
role_in_analysis: Assessed in crude associations with JEV outbreaks using a simple inhomogeneous Poisson model; not included in final full models.
quantitative_result: Feral pig habitat suitability was negatively associated with JEV outbreaks and was not included in the full models.
evidence_quote: Feral pig habitat suitability was not positively associated with JEV outbreaks, although it was negatively associated with outbreaks.
section: Statistical analysis – Outbreak point process modelling

measure_name: Direct and indirect inter-species contacts
what_it_represents: Observed direct and indirect interactions between macaques and people, goats, cattle, and dogs across sampling locations.
measurement_method: Field observations at sampling sites; direct contact was inter-species touching/contact, biting, or scratching, and indirect contact was a macaque remaining within 20 meters of another species for at least 15 min.
metric_or_unit: Number of contacts over 8 h.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of inter-species interactions among locations.
quantitative_result: The highest number of human-macaque contacts was in Gendaria, Dhaka, with 40 direct and 204 indirect contacts.
evidence_quote: We observed the highest number of human-macaque contacts in Gendaria, Dhaka, with 40 observations of direct contact and 204 observations of indirect contact.

measure_name: Inter-species contact rate by habitat
what_it_represents: Rates of direct and indirect contact between macaques and humans or domestic animals in urban, peri-urban, and rural habitats.
measurement_method: Observed interactions were expressed as direct and indirect contacts per hour by habitat and inter-species interaction.
metric_or_unit: Contacts per hour.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive habitat comparison of the wild-domestic and human-macaque relationship.
quantitative_result: Human-macaque direct and indirect contact rates were 3 and 22 contacts per hour, respectively, in urban habitat; goat-macaque direct contact was 4 contacts per hour in rural habitat.
evidence_quote: The contact rate between macaques and people was high in urban habitats for both direct contacts per hour (3) and indirect contacts per hour (22) (Table 7).

measure_name: Localization (inside LNP/outside LNP)
what_it_represents: Cattle residence within versus outside Limpopo National Park, representing their location relative to the park and its wildlife domain.
measurement_method: Cattle were classified by whether they lived inside the LNP or belonged to villages outside the park; BTB status was assessed by SICCT and prevalence was compared by location using a chi-squared test.
metric_or_unit: SICCT positive cattle: 18/1337 (1.3%) inside LNP and 6/1108 (0.5%) outside LNP.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of BTB prevalence by location.
quantitative_result: There was no significant difference in BTB prevalence between cattle resident inside and outside the LNP.
evidence_quote: The comparison of the proportion of positive cattle in the different villages showed no statistical significant differences between them (P > 0.05), and the same result was obtained when the proportion of positive cattle resident inside the LNP was compared with the proportion of positive cattle living outside the park (Table 3).

measure_name: Wildlife-livestock interaction zone
what_it_represents: A three-level spatial categorisation of cattle-rearing locations by intensity of wildlife-livestock interactions: intensive/high (zone 1), moderate (zone 2), and low (zone 3).
measurement_method: Five villages were purposively selected: two in each of the intensive and moderate interaction areas and one in a low-interaction location.
metric_or_unit: Categorical zone: zone 1, zone 2, or zone 3.
role_in_analysis: Independent categorical factor used to compare co-exposure distributions and as a predictor in Bayesian models.
quantitative_result: Cattle raised in moderate (zone 2) and high interface areas (zone 1) had a higher probability of FMDV and Leptospira spp. co-exposure than cattle in low interface areas.
evidence_quote: Cattle raised in moderate (zone 2) and high interface areas (zone 1) also had a higher probability of co-exposure to these pathogens than those in low interface areas.

measure_name: TB prevalence in wild boar
what_it_represents: Disease status of wild boar relative to cattle TB dynamics.
measurement_method: Estimated as the proportion of wild boars testing positive in the NWHSP relative to the total tested.
metric_or_unit: Proportion / prevalence (%) at county-year resolution.
role_in_analysis: Fixed predictor in risk-factor models of cattle prevalence, incidence, maintenance, and persistence.
quantitative_result: It was retained in the maintenance and persistence models, with odds ratios of 1.82 and 1.73, respectively.
evidence_quote: TB prevalence in wild boar was also included, estimated as the proportion of wild boars that tested positive in the NWHSP with respect to the total number of wild boar tested.

measure_name: Wild boar relative abundance (Wild boar ab.)
what_it_represents: Relative abundance of a main wild TB reservoir in Spain.
measurement_method: Wild boar hunting yield obtained as a 10 × 10 km grid and aggregated to county level using the average of intersecting grid cells.
metric_or_unit: Wild boar hunting yield; 10 × 10 km grid, aggregated at county level.
role_in_analysis: Fixed effect grouped within the wild-ungulates factor for cattle TB risk-factor modelling and variation partitioning.
quantitative_result: Wild boar relative abundance was retained together with wild boar TB prevalence in the models.
evidence_quote: We consequently included the wild boar hunting yield (ENETWILD-­consortium et al., 2020) and red deer environmental favorability (Ace­vedo et al., 2010) as proxies of relative abundance of these two species (Imperio et al., 2010), which are considered the main wild reservoirs of TB in Spain (Gortazar et al., 2012).

measure_name: Red deer relative abundance (Red deer ab.)
what_it_represents: Relative abundance of a main wild TB reservoir in Spain.
measurement_method: Red deer habitat favorability was aggregated from municipality to county using area-weighted mean values of intersecting municipalities.
metric_or_unit: Red deer habitat favorability; municipality data aggregated at county level.
role_in_analysis: Fixed effect grouped within the wild-ungulates factor for cattle TB risk-factor modelling and variation partitioning.
quantitative_result: The wild ungulates factor explained most of the variation in the incidence model.
evidence_quote: The wild ungulates factor explained most of the variation in the incidence model (see Fig. 5)

measure_name: Source of samples / avian population category
what_it_represents: Resident bird husbandry and rearing settings spanning backyard poultry, commercial broiler farms, weekly live bird markets, and wild bird/hobby flocks.
measurement_method: Cloacal swabs were collected and the sampled avian population was classified by husbandry practices and rearing intent; H9N2-positive proportions were compared across categories.
metric_or_unit: Number screened, number positive isolates, and proportion of H9N2-positive samples; p > 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of the proportion of H9N2-positive samples across domestic, market, and wild bird/hobby flock categories.
quantitative_result: No significant difference in H9N2-positive proportions was found between the four categories (p > 0.05).
evidence_quote: There is no significant difference in the proportion of AIVs H9N2 positive samples between the backyard poultry, commercial broiler farm, weekly live bird market, and wild bird/hobby flock (p > 0.05) (Table 1).
section: 3.1. Prevalence of H9N2 viruses in resident birds

measure_name: elephant–livestock interface
what_it_represents: The number of livestock in a space adjusted by the probability that the space is suitable elephant habitat.
measurement_method: A raster metric produced by weighting livestock density in each 1 km2 space by an E. maximus ecological niche estimated with a separate Maxent model using GBIF observations.
metric_or_unit: Weighted metric raster; livestock density per 1 km2 space weighted by elephant niche probability.
role_in_analysis: Environmental covariate in the Maxent model of anthrax suitability; ranked by permutation importance and evaluated in sensitivity analyses.
quantitative_result: It was the dominant feature delineating anthrax suitability, with permutation importance of 67.7%.
evidence_quote: The elephant– livestock interface was the dominant feature delineating anthrax suitability (permutation importance (PI) ¼ 67.7%).

measure_name: Known and novel bacteria shared by wildlife reservoirs and livestock species
what_it_represents: The number of bacterial species known to occur in each wildlife reservoir that were either known in, or predicted to be novel for, each focal livestock species.
measurement_method: The authors identified the top ten wildlife reservoir species for each livestock species from their prediction dataset and tabulated novel, known, and total shared bacteria.
metric_or_unit: Number of bacterial species (Novel, Known, Total)
role_in_analysis: Used to identify and rank wildlife reservoir species associated with bacterial species of cattle, sheep, and domestic swine.
quantitative_result: For Bos taurus, Ovis canadensis had 8 novel and 25 known bacteria, totaling 33; for Ovis aries, Ovis canadensis had 11 novel and 28 known bacteria, totaling 39; and for Sus scrofa domesticus, Procyon lotor had 18 novel and 14 known bacteria, totaling 32.
evidence_quote: Top Ten Wildlife Reservoirs of Known and Novel Bacteria Predicted to be Associated with Livestock Species, Ordered in Decreasing Order of Total Shared Bacteria Known to be Found in Each Wildlife Reservoir.

measure_name: Number of wildlife hosts associated with predicted novel or known livestock bacteria
what_it_represents: The breadth of wild mammal species that are known hosts of predicted novel bacteria or known bacterial species of the three focal livestock species.
measurement_method: Counts were derived from the dataset of predicted associations and known host-bacteria associations.
metric_or_unit: Number of wild mammal species
role_in_analysis: Quantifies potential wildlife reservoirs and supports the interpretation of potential transboundary disease transmission at the wildlife–livestock interface.
quantitative_result: 266 wild mammals hosted at least one predicted novel bacterium of the three livestock species, and 378 hosted at least one known livestock bacterial species.
evidence_quote: In addition to the top-ranked reservoir species, 266 wild mammals are known to host at least one predicted novel bacteria of the three livestock species and 378 wild mammal species are known to host at least one known livestock bacterial species.

measure_name: Studies classified as public health or livestock–wildlife interface research themes
what_it_represents: The number of reviewed dynamic, spatial wildlife disease-model studies addressing public health or the livestock–wildlife interface.
measurement_method: The authors classified each reviewed article by research thematic focus, including livestock–wildlife interface and public health, and counted the studies in those themes.
metric_or_unit: 33 studies; 33/168 studies
role_in_analysis: Descriptive synthesis used to identify the relative lack of reviewed studies addressing public health or livestock–wildlife interface topics.
quantitative_result: Only 33 studies addressed topics at the public health or the livestock–wildlife interface.
evidence_quote: In total, only 33 studies addressed topics at the public health or the livestock–wildlife interface (Figure 4a).

measure_name: Forest edge
what_it_represents: Forest fragmentation and the edge between natural forest and human-modified habitat, treated as interface habitat associated with potential human exposure.
measurement_method: Gridded landscape predictor included in boosted regression tree models of cutaneous and visceral leishmaniasis occurrence.
metric_or_unit: Forest edge; edge density metrics (unit not reported).
role_in_analysis: Candidate landscape predictor in models of disease distribution.
quantitative_result: The edge landscape metrics did not rank amongst the ten most important predictors for either disease form.
evidence_quote: The edge landscape metrics did not rank amongst the ten most important predictors for either disease form.
section: Results — Environmental predictors of the recent past distribution of leishmaniases

measure_name: Crop FoodPerennial edge and crop energy edge
what_it_represents: Fragmentation/edge of cropland, representing the interface between cropland and other habitats.
measurement_method: Landscape predictors listed for modelling leishmaniasis distribution.
metric_or_unit: Crop FoodPerennial edge and crop energy edge (unit not reported).
role_in_analysis: Candidate landscape predictors in the boosted regression tree analysis.
quantitative_result: The edge landscape metrics did not rank amongst the ten most important predictors for either disease form.
evidence_quote: Landscape cover and fragmentation of cropland linked to perennial food crops FoodPerennial cover (crop FoodPerennial cover and crop FoodPerennial edge)
section: Table 1. Potential environmental predictors of leishmaniasis distribution.

measure_name: Host category
what_it_represents: The host-domain status of CC398 isolates, including livestock and wildlife.
measurement_method: Host species were assigned to Human, Livestock, and Wildlife categories.
metric_or_unit: Number of genomes per category (Human n = 7; Livestock n = 22; Wildlife n = 14).
role_in_analysis: Used as the discrete trait for ancestral trait mapping and evaluation of host transitions.
quantitative_result: The most likely between-category transmission was from livestock to wildlife (PP = 0.99).
evidence_quote: The CC398 dataset is composed of 43 S. aureus genomes collected in the Iberian Peninsula from 2008 to 2022. Host species were assigned to three categories: Human (n = 7), Livestock (n = 22), and Wildlife (n = 14).
section: 3.4. Phylodynamic inference suggests expansion of livestock S. aureus CC398 strains towards wildlife in Iberian Peninsula

measure_name: Livestock-to-wildlife host transition posterior probability
what_it_represents: The inferred probability of transmission from livestock to wildlife among host categories.
measurement_method: Discrete ancestral trait mapping (DATM) under an asymmetric model.
metric_or_unit: Posterior probability (PP).
role_in_analysis: Estimated and compared the likely transmission directions between host categories.
quantitative_result: Transmission from livestock to wildlife had PP = 0.99.
evidence_quote: Concerning transmission events between different host categories, the more likely were from livestock to wildlife (Posterior probability [PP] = 0.99) and from livestock to human (PP = 0.89) (Fig. 5B).
section: 3.4. Phylodynamic inference suggests expansion of livestock S. aureus CC398 strains towards wildlife in Iberian Peninsula

measure_name: Domestic-interface (DI) use
what_it_represents: Coyote use of an area of plausible interaction among coyotes, people, and dogs around human settlements.
measurement_method: GPS locations within a 500 m buffer from the edge of a human settlement were counted for each coyote and divided by that individual's total observations.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of space used in DI; percentage of tracked days with at least one visit to a human settlement.
role_in_analysis: Operationalised coyote exposure to the domestic interface and described individual use of that interface.
quantitative_result: 24.1% (95% CI 3.3–44.9) of tracked days contained at least one visit to a human settlement; the male coyote from MV used 16% of his space within the DI and contacted it on 55% of observed days.
evidence_quote: Given the number of days each coyote was tracked with a GPS collar, 24.1% (95% CI 3.3–44.9) of tracked days contained at least one visit to a human settlement. The male coyote from MV was particularly prone to domestic contact, with 16% of his space use within the DI, and contacting that interface on 55% of the days we observed him.

measure_name: Camera sightings of dogs (dog events)
what_it_represents: Dog occurrence at camera-trap sites in relation to coyote relative abundance.
measurement_method: Independent camera images were defined as occurring at least 30 min apart; dog sightings were included as a predictor in quasi-Poisson generalized linear mixed models of coyote events per site.
metric_or_unit: Dog sightings; independent records per trap day; number of dog events.
role_in_analysis: Predictor of coyote relative abundance in GLMMs.
quantitative_result: Dogs comprised 0.049 dog sightings (23 independent records/trap day), and numbers of dog events were not significant predictors of coyote events.
evidence_quote: The GLMM showed that neither numbers of dog events nor human structures (minimum distance to the nearest human settlement, distances to the nearest paved and dirt road) were significant predictors of coyote events.

measure_name: MAP ‘Bison type’ genotype in Nilgai and domestic small ruminants
what_it_represents: Shared MAP genotype across free-ranging Nilgai and CIRG goats and sheep, used to represent inter-species transmission.
measurement_method: IS1311 PCR-REA genotyping of MAP colonies.
metric_or_unit: Categorical genotype (‘Bison type’).
role_in_analysis: Compared across Nilgai and goats/sheep to establish inter-species transmission.
quantitative_result: All the cultures from Nilgai were characterized as MAP and genotyped as ‘Bison type’.
evidence_quote: All the cultures from Nilgai were characterized as MAP and genotyped as ‘Bison type’.

measure_name: Difference in IS900 insertion-sequence nucleotides between goat and Nilgai MAP isolates
what_it_represents: Genetic comparison of MAP isolates of goat (S5) and Nilgai (B42) origin.
measurement_method: Sequencing of IS900 PCR products.
metric_or_unit: 2 (1%) base-pair difference at the 11th and 12th positions.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare MAP from domestic goats and Nilgai in the assessment of sharing/inter-species transmission.
quantitative_result: There was difference of 2 (1%) base pairs at the 11th and 12th position between goat and Nilgai origin IS900 sequences.
evidence_quote: There was difference of 2 (1%) base pairs at the 11th and 12th position (Genbank accession number EU130943) between insertion sequence of (IS900) goat (S5) and Nilgai (B42) origin.

measure_name: Monthly distribution of anthrax cases from all 3 health sectors
what_it_represents: Temporal co-occurrence of anthrax outbreaks across human, livestock, and wildlife sectors in northern Tanzania.
measurement_method: Retrospective review of human, livestock, and wildlife outbreak records; cases were cross-tabulated across species and seasons.
metric_or_unit: Monthly outbreak peaks in March and September through November.
role_in_analysis: Used to describe and interpret the temporal relationship between anthrax occurrence in humans and animals.
quantitative_result: Peaks of outbreaks occurred in humans, livestock and wildlife during March and September through November each year in the last decade.
evidence_quote: Our data demonstrated a seasonal pattern of anthrax outbreaks in northern Tanzania with peaks of outbreaks in humans, livestock and wildlife during March (start of long rain season) and September through November (end of dry season) each year in the last decade.

measure_name: Contact risk between buffalo and cattle
what_it_represents: Modelled risk of contact between buffalo in Kruger National Park and cattle in adjacent communal lands.
measurement_method: Landscape resistance maps for cattle and buffalo resource utilisation were used to model dispersal.
role_in_analysis: Compared by season and spatially located relative to the Sabi River, fence condition, and villages.
quantitative_result: Contact risk was significantly higher in the dry season and concentrated along the Sabi River at weaker fence sections.
evidence_quote: Landscape resistance maps for cattle and buffalo resource utilisation were used to model dispersal of these animals within these two areas. Contact risk between buffalo and cattle was significantly higher in the dry season and was concentrated along the Sabi River at the weaker parts of the fence.

measure_name: Shared habitat and contacts between cattle and buffalo
what_it_represents: Spatial overlap and contacts between cattle from Pezvi and buffalo from Kruger National Park near the Limpopo River.
measurement_method: Satellite data from collared individual cattle and buffalo.
metric_or_unit: 16.9% of habitat shared; most contacts occurring less than 500 m from the riverbed.
role_in_analysis: Used to describe cross-species spatial overlap/contact and relate buffalo contact to FMD antibody incidence in cattle.
quantitative_result: The species shared 16.9% of habitat, and FMD antibody incidence in cattle was higher at sites with high buffalo contact.
evidence_quote: Satellite data from collared individual cattle from Pezvi and buffalo from Kruger National Park showed that the two species shared 16.9% of habitat with most contacts occurring less than 500 m from the riverbed. These contacts increased during the dry season suggesting that contact is driven by resource availability (Miguel et al., 2013). Incidence of FMD antibodies in cattle was higher in sites with high buffalo contact suggesting spread of the infection from buffalo to cattle (Miguel et al., 2013).

measure_name: Number of viruses shared between host species
what_it_represents: Potential virus sharing among wild mammal species, domestic dog, and humans.
measurement_method: The list of mammal species extracted from IUCN, with domestic dog and human added, was linked to a published dataset of virus species from mammals and represented in bipartite and unipartite networks.
metric_or_unit: 57 viruses shared between 43 host species
role_in_analysis: Network-based predictive analysis of potential virus sharing and transmission among hosts.
quantitative_result: A total of 57 viruses were found to be shared between 43 host species, including the domestic dog and the human species.
evidence_quote: A total of 57 viruses were found to be shared between 43 host species (see S1 and S2 Tables), including the domestic dog and the human species (Fig 3A), with the human species hosting the highest number of viruses followed by the domestic dog, the Indochinese rhesus macaque (Macaca mulatta), and several bat species.

measure_name: Host centrality in the network of virus sharing
what_it_represents: The relative importance of each host, including domestic dog and wild-host groups, in virus sharing across the host network.
measurement_method: Eigenvalue centrality (EC) was calculated using the ‘evcent’ function from the ‘igraph’ package.
metric_or_unit: Eigenvalue centrality (EC)
role_in_analysis: Used to identify hosts that are central in the network of virus sharing and have greater potential for virus transmission.
quantitative_result: Primates had the highest centrality because of humans, followed by carnivores due to domestic dog, then deer, rodents, and bats.
evidence_quote: In terms of host centrality in the network of virus sharing, the primates showed the highest centrality because of the human species, followed by carnivores due to the domestic dog, the deer species (Cetartiodactylida), the rodents, and the bats (Fig 6).

measure_name: Freshwater runoff category
what_it_represents: A terrestrial-to-marine exposure setting for sea otters, categorized as high versus low or medium freshwater runoff.
measurement_method: Otters sampled near areas of high freshwater runoff were compared with otters sampled in areas with low or medium freshwater runoff in an epidemiologic study.
metric_or_unit: 2.9 times more likely to be exposed to T. gondii
role_in_analysis: Comparison of T. gondii exposure between otters sampled in different freshwater-runoff settings.
quantitative_result: Otters sampled near high freshwater runoff were 2.9 times more likely to be exposed to T. gondii.
evidence_quote: An epidemiologic study based on live and dead otter samples from 1998 to 2001 showed that otters sampled near areas of high freshwater runoff, such as Elkhorn Slough in Monterey Bay were 2.9 times more likely to be exposed to T. gondii than otters sampled in areas with low or medium freshwater runoff (Miller et al., 2002b).
section: 3. Parasite biology indicates a land–sea connection

measure_name: Geographic coastal area
what_it_represents: Spatial variation in sea otter T. gondii exposure across coastal areas, including areas characterized as having freshwater runoff near urban centres.
measurement_method: Multivariate logistic regression evaluated geographic differences in live and dead otters, adjusted by age and live/dead status.
metric_or_unit: Odds of exposure relative to the Big Sur coast; 95% Confidence Interval (CI)
role_in_analysis: Spatial exposure-risk analysis.
quantitative_result: Otters from the Elkhorn Slough area were six times as likely and otters from San Simeon to Morro Bay were five times as likely to have been exposed to T. gondii than otters from the Big Sur coast.
evidence_quote: Specifically, otters from the Elkhorn Slough area were six times as likely (95% Confidence Interval (CI): 1.9–20.0) and otters from San Simeon to Morro Bay were five times as likely (95% CI: 1.9–16.2) to have been exposed to T. gondii than otters from the more remote and rocky Big Sur coast.
section: 4. Updated analysis of T. gondii exposure of live and dead otters

measure_name: Level 1 co-occurrence transmission-risk map (T01A)
what_it_represents: Potential virus transmission between domestic poultry and wild waterfowl when both groups are predicted present in a grid cell.
measurement_method: A binary overlay model using predicted presence or absence of poultry and waterfowl at 1 km resolution.
metric_or_unit: T01A value of 0 or 1.
role_in_analysis: Used to map locations where poultry and wild waterfowl co-occur and therefore may come in contact.
quantitative_result: Dense concentrations of positive risk grid cells were present across much of southeastern China during both seasons.
evidence_quote: A T 01A value of 0 indicates no transmission risk (i.e., no co-occurrence) between domestic and wild species because both are not present within a cell. A transmission risk value of 1 indicates the potential for virus transmission between wild and domestic populations.

measure_name: Level 1 poultry-type/waterfowl co-occurrence measure (T01B)
what_it_represents: Co-occurrence of wild waterfowl with one or both types of domestic poultry, with output categories representing decreasing transmission threat.
measurement_method: Predicted binary presence of terrestrial poultry, aquatic poultry, and waterfowl was combined as T01B = (Pt01 + Pa01) × W01.
metric_or_unit: Model output 2, 1, or 0.
role_in_analysis: Used to compare combinations of poultry groups occurring with wild waterfowl in mapped transmission-risk assessments.
quantitative_result: Localized regions existed in the west where only one poultry type (usually chickens) was present in combination with wild waterfowl.
evidence_quote: Parameter values are 1 or 0 (present or absent), and model output is 2, 1, or 0 represented in decreasing threat of transmission risk for the three output values (both types of poultry are present along with waterfowl; one type of poultry is present along with waterfowl; or either poultry or waterfowl are not present in the grid cell):

measure_name: Uni-directional poultry–waterfowl transmission risk (TP to W and TW to P)
what_it_represents: Predicted transmission risk from poultry to wild waterfowl and from wild waterfowl to poultry, incorporating domestic-poultry density, effective wild-waterfowl population, viral shedding, uptake, and biosecurity terms.
measurement_method: Level 2 deterministic equations and Level 3 Monte-Carlo simulations at 1 km and 30 km resolutions.
metric_or_unit: Predicted number of cases per day; also displayed as 0 risk and four quantiles from low to highest risk.
role_in_analysis: Used to estimate and map directional H5N1 transmission risk between domestic and wild bird populations.
quantitative_result: The mean level of risk was greater for the poultry to waterfowl models (Eq. 3) by approximately two orders of magnitude.
evidence_quote: Model output is a measure of the transmission risk between poultry and waterfowl in units of predicted number of cases.
section: TRANSMISSION RISK EQUATIONS — Level 2 and 3 models

measure_name: species (dog/raccoon)
what_it_represents: Comparison of ESC-R E. coli occurrence between the wild raccoon and domestic dog host populations.
measurement_method: Sample prevalence was calculated for each species and compared using Fisher’s exact test.
metric_or_unit: Sample prevalence (%), odds ratio, 95% CI, and P value.
role_in_analysis: Predictor variable in the contingency-table analysis of ESC-R E. coli presence/absence.
quantitative_result: Raccoons had 56.9% sample prevalence and dogs had 16.5%; the odds of recovery were higher for raccoons (OR = 3.44, P < 0.0001).
evidence_quote: With a sample prevalence of 56.9% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 50.1% to 63.4%) and 16.5% (95% CI = 11.7% to 22.7%) for raccoons and dogs, respectively (Fig. 2A), there was a significantly higher odds of recovering at least one ESC-R E. coli isolate from raccoons than from dogs (Fisher’s exact test; odds ratio [OR] = 3.44, 95% CI = 2.16 to 5.63; P , 0.0001).

measure_name: private/public site (dog presence)
what_it_represents: The raccoon-dog interface, represented by whether raccoons were sampled at sites inaccessible or accessible to domestic dogs.
measurement_method: Raccoon fecal ESC-R E. coli presence was analyzed using a binomial GLMM, with private/public site and its interaction with urban-suburban context.
metric_or_unit: Odds ratio, 95% CI, and P value.
role_in_analysis: Predictor variable for ESC-R E. coli presence in raccoons.
quantitative_result: Dog presence was associated with higher odds of isolating ESC-R E. coli (OR = 5.36, 95% CI = 1.26–22.83; P = 0.02), modified by urban context (OR = 0.07, P = 0.03).
evidence_quote:
dog presence (yes) 5.36 (1.26–22.83) 0.02
urban context (urban) 􏰀 dog presence (yes) 0.07 (0.01–0.79) 0.03

measure_name: host type (public park raccoon, private park raccoon, dog)
what_it_represents: Three wild-domestic/shared-setting categories used to assess phylogenetic clustering of ESC-R E. coli isolates.
measurement_method: A univariable PERMANOVA assessed the influence of host type on pairwise SNP distance.
metric_or_unit: PERMANOVA F statistic and P value; pairwise SNP distance.
role_in_analysis: Predictor variable in analysis of phylogenetic similarity across public-park raccoons, private-park raccoons, and dogs.
quantitative_result: There was no significant difference in phylogenetic distance among these host types (F2, 151 = 0.43, P = 0.95).
evidence_quote: There was no significant difference in the phylogenetic distance of ESC-R E. coli isolates recovered from raccoons sampled at public parks and raccoons sampled at private parks or from those recovered from domestic dogs (PERMANOVA: F2, 151 = 0.43, P = 0.95).

measure_name: Host-specific viral positivity
what_it_represents: The occurrence of Carnivore protoparvovirus 1-positive samples across domestic dogs and wild carnivore species.
measurement_method: Fecal samples and intestines were screened using molecular testing for canine parvovirus and feline panleukopenia virus.
metric_or_unit: Positive/tested samples and percentage of positivity.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of infection occurrence among domestic dogs and wildlife species.
quantitative_result: Dogs: 290/343 (84.5%); Eurasian badgers: 4/55 (7.2%); golden jackals: 3/12 (25%); grey wolves: 1/5 (20%).
evidence_quote: Overall, we screened n = 387 fecal samples and intestines from dogs and different wildlife species, achieving a total of n = 298 positive samples among dogs (n = 290/343, 84.5%), Eurasian badgers (n = 4/55, 7.2%), golden jackals (n = 3/12, 25%), and grey wolves (n = 1/5, 20%).

measure_name: Phylogenetic host association of viral strains
what_it_represents: The genetic relationship of strains obtained from wildlife and illegally imported dogs, used to assess potential cross-species relationship and spillover.
measurement_method: Maximum likelihood phylogenetic analyses of complete genomes and VP2 gene sequences.
metric_or_unit: Phylogenetic clustering and maximum nucleotide identity.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of wildlife-derived and dog-derived viral sequences.
quantitative_result: The grey-wolf CPV-2c sequence showed a maximum nucleotide identity with dog strains of 99.9% across the whole genome and VP2 region.
evidence_quote: This sequence was antigenically classified as CPV-2c and phylogenetically closely related with Asian-origin CPV-2c circulating in dogs, showing a maximum nucleotide identity with dog strains of 99.9% across the whole genome and in the VP2 region (Figures 1 and 2).

measure_name: Wild bird species densities at multiple spatial scales
what_it_represents: The spatial distribution and density of wild bird species in relation to HPAI outbreak risk on poultry farms.
measurement_method: Winter bird counts were used to construct maps of estimated numbers of wild birds per species per square; densities were included at four spatial scales, including raw unsmoothed rasters.
metric_or_unit: Densities of 58 bird species; four spatial scales.
role_in_analysis: Predictor features in conditional logistic regressions and machine-learning classifiers of HPAI outbreak risk on poultry farms.
quantitative_result: Seventeen waterbird and two raptor species were most strongly associated with the HPAI outbreak risks.
evidence_quote: We showed that a model using wild bird species’ densities can accurately predict HPAI risk areas for poultry farms in the Netherlands. Seventeen waterbird and two raptor species were most strongly associated with the HPAI outbreak risks.

measure_name: Host species (dog vs. fox) in ectoparasite occurrence and abundance models
what_it_represents: The wild-domestic host comparison between Andean foxes and free-ranging rural dogs.
measurement_method: Tick and flea occurrence and abundance were compared by carnivore species using generalized linear mixed models.
metric_or_unit: GLMM fixed-effect estimate ± SE, z-value, and P-value; occurrence and abundance.
role_in_analysis: Fixed effect used to test host association and differences in ectoparasite occurrence and abundance between foxes and dogs.
quantitative_result: The abundance and occurrence of R. sanguineus s.s. and Ctenocephalides spp. were significantly higher in dogs than in foxes, whereas A. tigrinum and Pulex sp. were higher in foxes.
evidence_quote: The abundance and occurrence of R. sanguineus s.s. and Ctenocephalides spp. were significantly higher in dogs than in foxes, and both C. canis and C. felis felis were more abundant in dogs than in foxes (Table 3, Fig. 2). In contrast, higher abundance and occurrence of A. trigrinum and Pulex sp. was found in foxes than in dogs.

measure_name: Shared nucleotide sequence types (ntSTs) between foxes and dogs
what_it_represents: Molecular evidence of ectoparasite sharing and potential interspecific transmission between wild foxes and domestic dogs.
measurement_method: Ectoparasites found to be shared between hosts were molecularly characterized; sequences were assigned ntSTs and genetic structure among hosts was assessed using Snn.
metric_or_unit: Number of ntSTs shared; Snn and P-value.
role_in_analysis: Used to evaluate genetic sharing and genetic structure of ectoparasites among dog and fox hosts.
quantitative_result: R. sanguineus ntSTs were shared between foxes and dogs, with no genetic structure observed among the two host species (Snn = 0.70; P = 0.74).
evidence_quote: The R. sanguineus ntSTs were shared between foxes and dogs, with no genetic structure observed among the two host species (Snn = 0.70; P = 0.74) (Fig. 4).

measure_name: Host–parasite sharing network edges
what_it_represents: Parasite sharing between host species, including wild and domestic herbivores.
measurement_method: A bipartite species-level network was built and associations were retained when mean relative read abundance for a parasite mOTU in a host species was at least 2%.
metric_or_unit: Mean RRA ≥ 2% per host species; number of host species infected by each parasite mOTU.
role_in_analysis: Operationalised parasite-sharing links and host breadth in the host–parasite network.
quantitative_result: 47% of mOTUs infected just one species and only 25% infected greater than 3.
evidence_quote: In our network of host–parasite connections (filtered to mean RRA greater than 2% at the species level), parasite–host breadth was highly aggregated (right-skewed) and followed a lognormal distribution (electronic supplementary material, table S6), indicating many host specialists and few generalists, as predicted. Host breadth varied among parasite families (1–10, median 2), but 47% of mOTUs infected just one species and only 25% infected greater than 3 (electronic supplementary material, figure S7).
section: Results (c) Parasite host specificity and parasite-sharing patterns

measure_name: Shared mOTUs and host-network centrality
what_it_represents: The extent of parasite overlap between host species and the relative centrality of each host in the parasite-sharing network.
measurement_method: The bipartite network was projected to a weighted unipartite host-species network; edge weights were calculated using the sum product of RRA values for shared mOTUs, and degree, closeness, eigenvector, and betweenness centrality were calculated.
metric_or_unit: Number of other hosts sharing parasites; normalized centrality metrics.
role_in_analysis: Compared host roles and identified domestic and wild species connected by shared parasites.
quantitative_result: Cattle shared parasites with 8 other hosts, whereas elephant and warthog each shared just one mOTU with another species.
evidence_quote: Notably, cattle shared parasites with 8 other hosts, whereas elephant and warthog each shared just one mOTU with another species (figure 3a,b; electronic supplementary material, Appendix IV).
section: Results (c) Parasite host specificity and parasite-sharing patterns

measure_name: Proximity to nearest Ramsar wetland
what_it_represents: Proximity of poultry-outbreak or control locations to strongly protected waterfowl habitat, representing restrictions on contact between poultry and wildfowl.
measurement_method: Calculated to the edge of the nearest contemporary Ramsar site along a normalized scale of 100.
metric_or_unit: Normalized proximity scale of 0–100; one unit approximately 17.6 km.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory risk factor in multivariate logistic regression models of H5N1 poultry outbreaks.
quantitative_result: A unit increase in proximity was associated with a 3.2% reduction in the odds of an H5N1 outbreak.
evidence_quote: We found that a unit increase in proximity (* 17.6 km) to the nearest Ramsar site (i.e., along a scale of 0–100, with 0 being the farthest distance recorded in the dataset; see Methods) was associated with a 3.2% reduction in the odds of an H5N1outbreak.

measure_name: Proximity to nearest unprotected large water body
what_it_represents: Proximity to unprotected habitat attractive to wildfowl, representing greater potential exposure of poultry populations to wildfowl habitat.
measurement_method: Calculated to the nearest unprotected waterbody larger than 1 sq. km along a normalized scale of 100.
metric_or_unit: Normalized proximity scale of 0–100; one unit approximately 1.5 km.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory risk factor in multivariate logistic regression models of H5N1 poultry outbreaks.
quantitative_result: A unit increase in proximity was associated with a 7.7% increase in the odds of an H5N1 outbreak.
evidence_quote: By contrast, a unit increase in proximity (* 1.5 km) to the nearest unprotected waterbody was associated with a 7.7% increase in the odds of an H5N1outbreak.

measure_name: Rice paddy area
what_it_represents: Amount of rice paddy cover around outbreak/control locations; rice paddies are described as a common habitat for domesticated fowl and as human-dominated, poultry-abundant habitat.
measurement_method: Area covered by rice paddy was estimated within 10-km radius buffer zones around outbreaks, with 20-km and 50-km alternatives also tested.
metric_or_unit: Percent land cover within a 10-km radius buffer zone; table reports km2.
role_in_analysis: Explanatory risk factor in multivariate logistic regression models of H5N1 poultry outbreaks.
quantitative_result: Within a 10-km radius buffer zone, a 1% increase in rice paddy land cover was associated with up to a 1.6% increase in the odds of an outbreak.
evidence_quote: Within a 10-km radius buffer zone, an increase of 1% in rice paddy land cover was associated with up to a 1.6% increase in the odds of an outbreak.

measure_name: Serological prevalence of antibodies against F. hepatica by host species
what_it_represents: Comparison of F. hepatica antibody prevalence among domestic cattle and sheep and wild Pyrenean chamois and European mouflon in the multi-host system.
measurement_method: Serum samples were tested for antibodies against F. hepatica.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%) and 95% confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Host-species prevalence was compared for statistically significant differences.
quantitative_result: Total serological prevalence was 57.7% in cattle, 42.6% in sheep, 9.1% in Pyrenean chamois, and 19.4% in European mouflon; prevalences with different superscripts were significantly different (p < .05).

measure_name: Interface type / area of origin
what_it_represents: Cattle exposure setting in relation to wildlife: unrestricted contact at a porous interface, fencing-restricted contact at a non-porous interface, or absence of livestock-wildlife interaction at a non-interface site.
measurement_method: Study sites were selected and classified as porous, non-porous, and non-interface; cattle seropositivity was compared across these categories and area of origin was included as a predictor in multivariable logistic regression.
metric_or_unit: Brucellosis seroprevalence (%) and odds ratio (OR) for Brucella seropositivity.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of cattle seroprevalence by interface category and predictor variable in multivariable logistic regression.
quantitative_result: The porous interface had 19.5% seroprevalence versus 13.0% in the non-interface area; cows from the porous-interface area had OR = 1.9 for Brucella seropositivity compared with cows from the non-interface area.
evidence_quote: The porous interface recorded a significantly (p = 0.03) higher seroprevalence (19.5%; 95% CI: 16.1–23.4%) compared to the non-interface area (13.0%; 95% CI: 9.2–19.9%).

measure_name: Area of origin (porous-interface Malipati versus non-interface Chomupani)
what_it_represents: Comparison of cattle from an area with unrestricted livestock-wildlife contact against cattle from an area classified as having no livestock/wildlife interactions.
measurement_method: Multivariable logistic regression used area of origin of cows as a categorical predictor of Brucella seropositive status.
metric_or_unit: Odds ratio (OR), 95% confidence interval, and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Independent predictor in the final multivariable logistic regression model.
quantitative_result: Cows from Malipati, the porous-interface area, had approximately twice the odds of Brucella seropositivity as cows from Chomupani, a non-interface area (OR = 1.9, p = 0.007).
evidence_quote: The odds of being Brucella seropositive for cows from Malipati, the porous interface area, were approximately twice (OR = 1.9, 1.2 < OR < 3.0, p = 0.007) compared to those from Chomupani, a non-interface area.

measure_name: Percentage of nucleotide (nt) and amino acid (AA) identity
what_it_represents: Genetic similarity between the aMPV-B strain detected in a Northern shoveler and selected Italian aMPV-B strains from poultry.
measurement_method: Comparison of overlapping partial G gene sequences; nucleotide and amino-acid identity was computed using BioEdit software v7.2.
metric_or_unit: Percentage nt and AA identity; number of different nt and AA residues.
role_in_analysis: Used with phylogenetic analysis to assess the relationship of the wild-bird strain to strains circulating in Italian chickens and turkeys.
quantitative_result: A 100% nt and AA identity was detected with Italian strains detected in 2016 and 2019.
evidence_quote: A 100% nt and AA identity was detected with Italian strains detected in 2016 and 2019 (Table 2).

measure_name: Study village as a livestock-wildlife interaction/distance category
what_it_represents: Village-level differences in livestock-wildlife interaction and overlap, based on distance to Maasai Mara National Reserve.
measurement_method: Three villages were purposively selected based on expected interaction differences related to their distance from the reserve; Mara Rianta was described as having high wildlife-livestock interactions, whereas Lemek and Endoinyo Narasha had less overlap.
metric_or_unit: Village-specific cattle seroprevalence (%) and odds ratios (ORs).
role_in_analysis: Comparison of Brucella seropositivity between village categories representing differing livestock-wildlife interaction settings.
quantitative_result: Mara Rianta had 22.7% seroprevalence and an OR of 7.03 versus Endoinyo Narasha, which had 4.0% seroprevalence.
evidence_quote: Three villages (Lemek, Mara Rianta and Endoinyo Narasha) were selected purposively to represent areas with expected differences in livestock-wildlife interaction based on the distance to the national reserve.

measure_name: Grazing in reserve
what_it_represents: Cattle grazing inside the national reserve, an exposure setting associated with interaction with wildlife.
measurement_method: Farmer questionnaire; the questionnaire asked whether cattle were let to graze inside the national reserve.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of farms reporting grazing in the reserve.
role_in_analysis: Included as one component of the calculated risk score that was compared between seropositive and negative farms.
quantitative_result: Grazing in the reserve was reported by 60% overall, including 100% of farms in Mara Rianta; the average risk score was 7.4 in seropositive farms and 7.1 in negative farms, but the difference was not significant.
evidence_quote: A risk score was calculated adding all risk practices; whether cattle are let to graze inside the national reserve; whether cattle mix with other herds while grazing; whether cattle mix with other herds at watering points; whether cattle share trek route with other herds; whether herds share water point on trek; whether farmer has bought livestock from other farms; whether working personnel visit other livestock holdings; and whether vehicles have access to farm.

measure_name: Cattle density in the county
what_it_represents: The density of a domestic cattle population in the county of sampled roe deer.
measurement_method: Calculated from county information on land used for animal husbandry and reported livestock units.
metric_or_unit: Livestock units (LUs) per square kilometer.
role_in_analysis: Predictor tested by Spearman’s correlation and logistic regression against detection of Staphylococcaceae with reduced susceptibility to cefoxitin in roe deer nasal swabs.
quantitative_result: The logistic-regression association in roe deer was confirmed (OR, 1.01; P < 0.05).
evidence_quote: According to logistic regression analyses, only the significant association between the detection of Staphylococcaceae with a non-wild-type phenotype for cefoxitin in samples of roe deer and the density of cattle in the county (odds ratio [OR], 1.01; P < 0.05), as well as between the detection of these bacteria in nasal swabs of wild boar and the density of poultry in the county (OR, 1.28; P = 0.03) were confirmed.

measure_name: Poultry density in the county
what_it_represents: The density of a domestic poultry population in the county of sampled wild boar.
measurement_method: Calculated from county information on land used for animal husbandry and reported livestock units.
metric_or_unit: Livestock units (LUs) per square kilometer.
role_in_analysis: Predictor tested by Spearman’s correlation and logistic regression against detection of Staphylococcaceae with reduced susceptibility to cefoxitin in wild boar nasal swabs.
quantitative_result: The logistic-regression association in wild boar was confirmed (OR, 1.28; P = 0.03).
evidence_quote: According to logistic regression analyses, only the significant association between the detection of Staphylococcaceae with a non-wild-type phenotype for cefoxitin in samples of roe deer and the density of cattle in the county (odds ratio [OR], 1.01; P < 0.05), as well as between the detection of these bacteria in nasal swabs of wild boar and the density of poultry in the county (OR, 1.28; P = 0.03) were confirmed.
