measure_name: Seroprevalence of FCoV, FPLV, FHV and FCV in wild and domestic carnivores
what_it_represents: Antibody exposure to feline-related viruses in wild carnivores and domestic cats at the domestic animal–wildlife interface.
measurement_method: Commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test kits were used on blood samples.
metric_or_unit: Percentage seropositive, with pathogen-specific positive titre cut-offs.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of pathogen seroprevalence between wild carnivore species and domestic cats.
quantitative_result: All domestic cats and one flat-headed cat tested positive for FCV, while only two domestic cats (7.4%) were infected with FHV.
evidence_quote: Blood samples, collected from wild carnivores (n = 21) and domestic cats (n = 27), were tested for antibodies against feline coronavirus (FCoV), feline panleukopenia virus (FPLV), feline herpesvirus (FHV) and feline calicivirus (FCV), using commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test kits.

measure_name: Hemoplasma infection prevalence by host species
what_it_represents: Comparison of hemoplasma infection between co-occurring wild guignas and rural domestic cats.
measurement_method: Blood/spleen samples from guignas and domestic cats were assessed for hemoplasma infection by direct sequencing of the 16S RNA gene; prevalence differences between species were tested with a Mann-Whitney U test.
metric_or_unit: Percent positive, with 95% confidence intervals; Mann-Whitney U test p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether infection prevalence differed across the wild and domestic host domains.
quantitative_result: 24 guignas (23.53%) and 40 domestic cats (15.27%) were positive; prevalence did not differ significantly (p = 0.28, U = 10690).
evidence_quote: Across the study area, 24 guignas (23.53%; 95% CI = 15.16–31.90%) and 40 domestic cats (15.27%; 95% CI = 10.8–19.65%) were positive for hemoplasma. There was no statistically significant difference observed in prevalence rate between the two species (p = 0.28, U = 10690).

measure_name: Shared nucleotide sequence types (ntSTs) between host species
what_it_represents: Genetic sharing of hemoplasma sequence types between guignas and domestic cats, used as evidence of cross-species transmission.
measurement_method: A nucleotide sequence type network was generated from 16S rRNA gene sequences; host-species genetic structure was assessed using Phist and Snn statistics.
metric_or_unit: Number of shared ntSTs; Phist and Snn test statistics and p-values.
role_in_analysis: Evaluated cross-species transmission and genetic structure between wild and domestic hosts.
quantitative_result: Two shared ntSTs were observed, one for Mhf and one for Mycoplasma sp.; CMhm showed significant host-species genetic structure.
evidence_quote: On the other hand, two cases of shared ntSTs between both host species were observed (1 for Mhf, 1 for Mycoplasma sp.) and no genetic structure of Mhf sequences between guignas and domestic cats was found (Phist = 0.19, p = 0.39; Snn = 0.58, p = 0.43).

measure_name: Landscape category associated with guigna infection
what_it_represents: Human-dominated fragmented landscapes versus pristine continuous forest habitats, representing hypothesized opportunities for domestic cat-guigna encounters.
measurement_method: Land use was quantified within circular buffers surrounding guigna sample locations and included as an independent variable in multivariate logistic regression with hemoplasma infection as the binary response variable.
metric_or_unit: Categorical land use: fragmented landscape or continuous forest; infection prevalence.
role_in_analysis: Tested the prediction that human-dominated landscapes, rather than pristine forest, would be associated with guigna hemoplasma infection.
quantitative_result: Guignas from continuous forest had significantly higher prevalence of total hemoplasmas, CMhm, and Mhf than guignas from fragmented landscapes.
evidence_quote: We also found a significantly higher prevalence of total hemoplasma species and specifically of CMhm and Mhf (Table S1, Fig. S2) in guignas from continuous forest compared with fragmented landscapes.

measure_name: Number of buffalo that escaped from the Kruger National Park to the Nkomazi area
what_it_represents: The number of buffalo moving out of the Kruger National Park into the adjacent cattle area following fence damage, representing opportunity for buffalo-cattle contact.
measurement_method: Observed and displayed by year/quarter as strayed, destroyed and post mortem buffalo.
metric_or_unit: Number of buffalo; year/quarter.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of observations in 2000-2001 following fence damage with observations from 1996-1999.
quantitative_result: Increased numbers of buffalo escaped to the Nkomazi area in 2000 and 2001 after the fence was damaged.
evidence_quote: Observed increased numbers of buffalo that escaped from the Kruger National Park to the Nkomazi area in 2000 and 2001 after damage to the park game fence, compared with similar observations between 1996 and 1999

measure_name: Number of small domestic swine farms per state
what_it_represents: A state-level domestic-swine farming condition considered relevant to feral-domestic swine contact.
measurement_method: The authors tested the number of small domestic swine farms in a multivariable model; farms with 1,000 or fewer domestic swine were classified as small.
metric_or_unit: Number of farms per state; small farms were defined as farms with 1,000 or fewer domestic swine.
role_in_analysis: Potential risk factor in manual forward variable selection and a multivariable model of IAV exposure/seroprevalence in feral swine.
quantitative_result: There were more IAV-seropositive samples from states with more small domestic swine farms.
evidence_quote: We considered farms with 1,000 or fewer domestic swine to be small farms. Small farms were of interest due to lower biosecurity and increased chance for contact with feral swine.
section: RESULTS — Factors associated with IAV seroprevalance in feral swine

measure_name: Feral swine serum-sample cross-reactivity to swine and avian IAVs
what_it_represents: Serological evidence of feral-swine exposure to IAVs associated with domestic swine and avian hosts.
measurement_method: Hemagglutination inhibition assays of 294 ELISA-positive feral swine serum samples against reference IAVs.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of 294 tested serum samples.
role_in_analysis: Quantitative comparison of feral swine antibody cross-reactivity against swine- versus avian-origin IAVs.
quantitative_result: Only 16 (5.4%) cross-reacted to one of the four avian IAVs, whereas 271 of 294 tested HI positive against swine and human IAV.
evidence_quote: Although 271 of the 294 feral swine serum samples tested HI positive against swine and human IAV, only 16 (5.4%) cross-reacted to one of the four avian IAVs included in the reference panel
section: RESULTS — Distinction between swine and avian IAVs

measure_name: Tick infestation by host group
what_it_represents: The occurrence of tick infestation in domestic free-roaming dogs compared with wild carnivores.
measurement_method: Ticks were collected after visual examination of each free-roaming dog and wild carnivore.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of hosts with ticks: 12 (60%) free-roaming dogs and six (9.2%) wild carnivores.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of tick-host associations across domestic and wild carnivore host groups.
quantitative_result: Ticks were collected from 60% of free-roaming dogs and 9.2% of wild carnivores.
evidence_quote: We collected 45 ticks belonging to two families (Ixodidae and Argasidae) from 12 (60%) free roaming dogs and six (9.2%) wild carnivores.

measure_name: Tick-species association with host group
what_it_represents: The distribution of brown dog ticks and sylvatic ticks between domestic dogs and wild carnivores.
measurement_method: Collected ticks were identified using morphological keys, with DNA sequencing confirmation for Ixodes kingi and Rh. sanguineus s.l. specimens.
metric_or_unit: Presence/absence of tick types on each host group.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive assessment of host associations at the domestic-wild carnivore interface.
quantitative_result: The authors did not find brown dog ticks on wild carnivores or sylvatic ticks on dogs.
evidence_quote: Despite the premise that domestic and wild carnivores could play bidirectional roles as alternate hosts for ectoparasites (Dobler and Pfeffer, 2011) and high densities and free-roaming activity of domestic dogs at JBR (Almuna, 2016), we did not find brown dog ticks on wild carnivores or sylvatic ticks on dogs.

measure_name: Leptospiral infection prevalence by wild/domestic carnivore group
what_it_represents: Comparison of Leptospira infection prevalence between wild carnivores and domestic carnivores, and between wild carnivores and free-roaming domestic cats.
measurement_method: Urine and kidney samples were analyzed by PCR using pathogenic leptospires-specific primers.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence (%) and Fisher´s p-value
role_in_analysis: Comparison of prevalence across wild and domestic carnivore groups.
quantitative_result: Wild versus domestic carnivores: 7.8% versus 9.7% (Fisher´s p= 1.0); wild carnivores versus free-roaming cats: 7.8% versus 7.4% (Fisher´s p= 1.0).
evidence_quote:
No differences were found
either between wild and domestic carnivores (7.8%
vs 9.7%; Fisher´s p= 1.0) or between wild carnivores
and free-roaming cats (7.8% vs 7.4%; Fisher´s p= 1.0).

measure_name: Wild versus domestic bird host status
what_it_represents: A categorical host-domain trait used to reconstruct transmission between wild and domestic birds.
measurement_method: Sequences were categorized by wild or domestic host status and analyzed using a discrete trait diffusion model.
metric_or_unit: Inferred transitions between wild and domestic birds.
role_in_analysis: Transmission inference between wild and domestic birds, including estimation of repeated introductions into domestic birds.
quantitative_result: The final 1:3 dataset resolved 106 domestic-sequence clusters, each inferred as a unique introduction from wild to domestic birds; only 4 introductions were inferred from domestic to wild birds.
evidence_quote: The phylogeny of the final dataset (using a 1:3 ratio of domestic to wild sequences) shows 106 clusters of domestic sequences (Figure 5A, Figure S14-15, Table S11) each inferred as a unique introduction of H5N1 from wild birds into domestic birds. Among these domestic-only clusters, we calculate that lineages persisted for ~4.5 months on average (95% HPD: 2.7, 5.63). In contrast, we infer limited transmission from domestic birds back to wild birds (Figure 5B, Table S11), with only 4 inferred introductions from domestic birds to wild birds (Table S11).

measure_name: Domestic-to-wild sequence ratio (titration analysis)
what_it_represents: Alternative sampling compositions of domestic and wild bird sequences used to assess the effect of sampling on inferred cross-domain transmission.
measurement_method: The authors generated five datasets by progressively adding wild bird sequences to an equal domestic/wild dataset.
metric_or_unit: Domestic:wild sequence ratios of 1:1, 1:1.5, 1:2, 1:2.5, and 1:3.
role_in_analysis: Sensitivity analysis for transmission inference between wild and domestic birds.
quantitative_result: As wild sequences were added, the analysis inferred more transitions from wild to domestic birds and less transmission between domestic birds.
evidence_quote: As wild sequences were progressively added into the tree, most domestic-only clusters became smaller, broken up by wild sequences that interspersed within these clades (Figure S12A-E). The “breaking up” of these domestic clusters results in inference of more transitions from wild to domestic birds, and less transmission between domestic birds (Figure 5B-C, Figure S13).

measure_name: Wild-to-domestic introductions into agricultural birds
what_it_represents: The estimated number of independent viral introductions from wild birds into domestic birds.
measurement_method: Discrete trait diffusion and ancestral-state reconstruction applied across titration analyses of domestic and wild bird sequence datasets.
metric_or_unit: Number of independent introductions, reported as 46 to 113.
role_in_analysis: Quantifies the contribution of wild-bird spillover to agricultural outbreaks.
quantitative_result: The authors inferred no fewer than 46 and as many as 113 independent introductions into domestic birds.
evidence_quote: While the exact number of inferred introductions vary across analyses (Table S11, S12), we infer no fewer than 46, and as many as 113 independent introductions into domestic birds.

measure_name: association strength
what_it_represents: The extent to which each pair of host species aggregated with other species, representing interspecific proximity/contact.
measurement_method: Calculated as the percentage of observations in which two species were observed within 50 m of each other, relative to all observations of those species.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of observations; values reported as >7.5%, maximum 14.2%, and 3.2%.
role_in_analysis: Covariate in MR-QAP matrix regression predicting parasite sharing between pairs of host species.
quantitative_result: The number of parasite taxa shared by two host species was positively correlated with association strength (ˇ = 3.39, p = 0.03).
evidence_quote: Our analysis revealed that the number of parasite taxa shared by two host species was positively correlated with the association strength between the hosts (ˇ = 3.39, p = 0.03, Fig. 4a and b).

measure_name: Jaccard index for parasite sharing
what_it_represents: The extent to which each pair of host species shared parasite taxa, representing potential transmission between wild and domestic ungulates.
measurement_method: Calculated as the number of shared parasite taxa divided by the total number of taxa found in both host species combined.
metric_or_unit: Jaccard index (proportion of parasite taxa shared).
role_in_analysis: Outcome variable in MR-QAP matrix regression, assessed in relation to association strength and shared dietary niche.
quantitative_result: Species pairs observed associating in >7.5% of observations shared nearly half their parasite taxa on average.
evidence_quote: We measured the extent to which each pair of host species shared parasite taxa using the Jaccard index. The Jaccard index is deﬁned as the number of shared parasite taxa divided by the total number of taxa found in both host species combined.

measure_name: PPRV seropositivity in wildlife inhabiting areas near domestic livestock, pastures, and water sources
what_it_represents: PPRV antibody positivity in wildlife sampled in a setting characterized by proximity to domestic livestock and pasture and water-source use.
measurement_method: Detection of antibodies in blood samples by H c-ELISA.
metric_or_unit: 63% seropositivity
role_in_analysis: Evidence of PPRV infection in wildlife in the context of possible spillover from domestic animals.
quantitative_result: 63% seropositivity for PPRV was found.
evidence_quote: We tested wildlife inhabiting areas near domestic livestock, pastures, and water sources in the Ngorongoro district in the Serengeti ecosystem of northern Tanzania and found 63% seropositivity for peste des petits ruminants virus.

measure_name: Presence–absence vectors Yd(wr, pd) / association probability Ψd(wr, pd)
what_it_represents: Whether a wildlife species shares a parasite species recorded in a focal human or domestic host species.
measurement_method: The authors constructed vectors across combinations of wildlife species, zoogeographical regions, and parasite species recorded in each focal species; absence of a record was set to 0, and the resulting data were modelled with logistic hierarchical regressions.
metric_or_unit: Binary presence–absence; probability of association.
role_in_analysis: Outcome used to analyse drivers of parasite sharing between focal domestic species and wildlife.
quantitative_result: Of the 1,345 mammalian wildlife species in the database, 41% (n = 553 spp.) were infected with helminth parasite species also found in humans.
evidence_quote: Of the 1,345 mammalian wildlife species in our host–parasite data-base, 41% (n = 553 spp.) were infected with helminth parasite spe-cies (Nematoda, Cestoda and Trematoda) also found in humans.

measure_name: Association risk
what_it_represents: The relative risk that a wildlife species will share parasites with each focal host species.
measurement_method: Calculated by entering wildlife species’ ecological traits into equations from fitted models using posterior modes of parameter estimates.
metric_or_unit: Relative risk; a value of “1” indicates a wildlife species is likely to share all parasite species known from a particular focal species.
role_in_analysis: Model-based prediction projected geographically for wildlife species and local wildlife assemblages.
quantitative_result: Wild mammals occurring in the Nearctic and Palaearctic regions were predicted to show high association risk for sharing parasites with humans.
evidence_quote: We computed the relative risk that a wildlife species will share parasites with each of the focal host species for all 5,289 terrestrial mammal species in the IUCN database by entering species’ ecologi-cal traits into equations from the fitted models above (using poste-rior modes of parameter estimates).

measure_name: Simple badger-mediated edge (B-edge)
what_it_represents: Two cattle farms neighboring the same badger sett/home range, representing a potential badger-mediated contact between farms.
measurement_method: A B-edge was assigned when both farms were neighbors of a given sett; farm-setts were neighbors when a farm pasture intersected the badger home range.
metric_or_unit: Binary edge-type variable (presence/absence); odds ratio and attributable risk fraction.
role_in_analysis: Included as a binary explanatory variable in a logistic regression of whether an edge from an infected farm ended at a farm infected by the same molecular type.
evidence_quote: - A simple badger-mediated edge (denoted B-edge below) between farms i and j represented the fact that both farms were neighbors of a given sett;

measure_name: Second level badger-mediated edge (D-edge)
what_it_represents: Two cattle farms each neighboring distinct but neighboring badger home ranges, representing potential contact mediated through neighboring badger social groups.
measurement_method: A D-edge was assigned when farm i neighbored sett k1, farm j neighbored sett k2, and setts k1 and k2 were neighbors.
metric_or_unit: Binary edge-type variable (presence/absence); odds ratio and attributable risk fraction.
role_in_analysis: Included as a binary explanatory variable in a logistic regression of whether an edge from an infected farm ended at a farm infected by the same molecular type.
evidence_quote: - A second level badger-mediated edge (denoted D-edge below) between farms i and j represented the fact that (i) farm i was neighbor of a sett k1 , (ii) farm j was neighbor of a sett k2 , and (iii) the setts k1 and k2 were themselves neighbors.

measure_name: Badger-sett infection status for B- and/or D-edges
what_it_represents: Whether badger setts supporting badger-mediated edges were infected, in relation to infection by the same molecular type in the linked cattle farms.
measurement_method: Setts were classified infected when at least one trapped badger had an identified molecular type; uninfected when at least two trapped badgers tested negative and no occupant badger was infected. A Fisher exact test assessed association with the status of B- and/or D-edges.
metric_or_unit: Number and percentage of case/control edges supported by positive badger setts; Fisher exact test and odds ratio.
role_in_analysis: Tested the association between infection status of badger setts and case status of badger-mediated edges connecting infected cattle farms.
quantitative_result: Among 44 case edges, 38 (86%) were supported by positive badger setts, versus 102 of 220 control edges (46%); Fisher exact test p < 0.0001 and OR 7.3 [95% CI: (2.9–21.9)].
evidence_quote: Among them, 44 were case edges (i.e., the destination farm had also been found infected by the same molecular type) of which 38 (86%) were supported by positive badger setts; and 220 were control edges of which 102 were supported by positive badger setts (46%). These differences were significant (Fisher exact test: p < 0.0001) with an associated OR of 7.3 [95% CI: (2.9–21.9)].

measure_name: Farmer-observed elk and deer use of cattle summer pastures and winter feeding areas (cervid-cattle comingling)
what_it_represents: Cervid use of cattle settings and direct feeding with cattle before and after barrier-fence construction.
measurement_method: Farmer observations recorded through interviews, including observations concerning 294 cattle summer pastures and 51 cattle winter feeding areas.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of respondents observing use or change in use; before-versus-after barrier-fence periods.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive before-and-after comparison of cervid use of cattle pasture and winter feeding areas and reported comingling.
quantitative_result: Use of cattle winter feeding areas by deer was observed by 26% of respondents during the 5 years prior to the barrier fence, but this increased to 38% of respondents after receiving a barrier fence.
evidence_quote: Elk use of cattle winter feeding areas was observed by 10% of respondents before and 12% after barrier fence construction, with two farmers observing that elk comingling with cattle stopped after the fence was constructed.

measure_name: Relationship between the number of farms with bTB reactive cattle and the number of bTB positive deer
what_it_represents: Regional association between bTB-positive wild deer and farms reporting bTB-reactive domestic cattle.
measurement_method: Spearman test of regional data from 17 sampled areas; farms with infected cattle were located using UK TB Advisory Service maps and deer bTB status was determined by serology.
metric_or_unit: Spearman correlation coefficient (r), P value, and number of regions (n).
role_in_analysis: Tests the relationship between bTB occurrence in deer and cattle farms across regions.
quantitative_result: Significant positive correlation (r = 0.643, P < 0.02, n = 17).
evidence_quote: The relationship between the number of farms with bTB reactive cattle and the number of deer with bTB showed a significant positive correlation (r = 0.643, P < 0.02, n = 17).
section: Results — Deer density and farms with reactors

measure_name: Relationship between deer density and the number of farms with bTB reactive cattle
what_it_represents: Regional association between density of wild red deer and the number of cattle farms with bTB reactors.
measurement_method: Spearman test of annual deer-count density data and numbers of farms with bTB-reactive cattle across 17 regions.
metric_or_unit: Spearman correlation coefficient (r) and number of regions (n).
role_in_analysis: Tests whether regional deer density is associated with bTB-reactive cattle farms.
quantitative_result: Weak positive trend (r = 0.181, n = 17).
evidence_quote: A weak positive trend was seen in the relationship between deer density and the number of farms with bTB reactive cattle (r = 0.181, n = 17).
section: Results — Deer density and farms with reactors

measure_name: Water availability
what_it_represents: Geographic variation in water availability associated with risk of transmission among wildlife, livestock, and people.
measurement_method: Identification of geographic areas with varying water availability using information on bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis in livestock and wildlife.
role_in_analysis: Used to identify areas where transmission risk may be high and in detailed models assessing effects on disease status.
evidence_quote: The HALI project has now identified bovine tuberculosis and brucellosis in livestock and wildlife in the Ruaha ecosystem and is using this information to identify geographic areas with varying water availability, in which the risk of transmission among wildlife, livestock, and people may be high.

measure_name: Shared water sources with livestock or wildlife
what_it_represents: Pastoral households' perceived health risk from sharing water sources with livestock or wildlife.
measurement_method: Survey findings from participating pastoral households.
metric_or_unit: 75% of households
role_in_analysis: Used to illustrate the need for targeted community education about zoonotic disease risk.
quantitative_result: 75% of households did not consider sharing water sources with livestock or wildlife to be a health risk.
evidence_quote: Furthermore, when the HALI project began working in this region, 75% of households did not consider sharing water sources with livestock or wildlife to be a health risk, illustrating the need for effective community education.

measure_name: Direct and indirect contacts among wildlife, humans, and domestic animals
what_it_represents: The annual contacts resulting from wildlife handling and wildlife trade across wildlife, human, and domestic-animal domains.
measurement_method: The article states that figures were compiled by the Wildlife Conservation Society from a variety of sources.
metric_or_unit: At least a billion contacts annually
role_in_analysis: Descriptive estimate used to characterize the scale of contact; not used in a statistical comparison or model.
quantitative_result: At least a billion direct and indirect contacts occur annually.
evidence_quote: All considered, at least a billion direct and indirect contacts among wildlife, humans, and domestic animals result from the handling of wildlife and the wildlife trade annually.

measure_name: Host population / host type
what_it_represents: Wild and domestic animal populations as discrete host populations for avian influenza and FMDV circulation analyses.
measurement_method: Viral sequences were assigned by host; host was included as information in phylogenetic/network analyses.
metric_or_unit: Number of sequences per host; discrete host populations.
role_in_analysis: Used to estimate circulation and transmission patterns among host populations.
quantitative_result: The thesis reports that wild Anseriformes accounted for most virus circulation in Europe, whereas domestic Anseriformes accounted for virus movements in Asia.
evidence_quote:
I also determined that while wild Anseriformes are
responsible for most of the of the virus circulation in Europe, domestic Anseriformes
birds are responsible for the virus movements in Asia.

measure_name: Estimated transmission rates between potential hosts
what_it_represents: FMDV transmission among the three host populations: antelopes, cattle, and buffalo.
measurement_method: Phylogeographic analysis estimating transmission rates between sampled hosts.
metric_or_unit: Estimated transmission rates.
role_in_analysis: Tests and characterises host-to-host FMDV circulation for SAT1 and SAT2.
quantitative_result: Antelopes were found to appear to act as an intermediate host between buffalo and cattle for both serotypes.
evidence_quote:
Thirdly, using advanced Bayesian structured coalescent model
approximations, I studied the role played by antelopes in the transmission of FMDV
SAT1 and SAT2 in Africa. I found that for both serotypes, antelopes seem to act as
an intermediate host between buffalo and cattle.

measure_name: Salmonella serovar prevalence in wild boar and cattle before and after management
what_it_represents: Occurrence and prevalence patterns of shared Salmonella serovars in sympatric wild boar and cattle across periods before and after cattle removal and wild-boar population management.
measurement_method: Fresh faecal samples from wild boar and cattle were cultured for Salmonella; isolates were serologically typed, and prevalence was compared between Be and Af using Fisher’s exact tests.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence at CI 95%; Fisher’s exact test odds ratio and P-value.
role_in_analysis: Used to assess changes in Salmonella prevalence following host-population management and to identify concordant patterns in cattle and wild boar.
quantitative_result: Serovar Meleagridis prevalence in wild boar decreased from 36 (22.9–51) before management to 2 (0.25–7.2) after management (odds ratio 26.3 (5.8–245), P <0.001); in cattle it decreased from 75 (19–99) to no detected after-management isolates (P <0.01).
evidence_quote: The number of isolates and the prevalence obtained for each serovar in both wild boar and cattle Be and Af are shown in Table 1.

measure_name: PFGE DNA similarity of Salmonella isolates across wild boar and cattle
what_it_represents: Molecular similarity of shared Salmonella serovars isolated from wild boar and cattle, used to support epidemiological connection and bacterial exchange between the host domains.
measurement_method: Meleagridis and Anatum isolates were analysed by pulsed field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) with xbaI; DNA patterns were analysed using BioNumerics 6.5 software.
metric_or_unit: Percentage DNA similarity.
role_in_analysis: Used to confirm shared strain patterns across wild boar and cattle and infer epidemiological connections.
quantitative_result: All but one Meleagridis isolate from wild boar, cattle and red fox had a common PFGE DNA pattern with 100% similarity; Anatum isolates from wild boars and cattle after management also had an identical 100% pattern.
evidence_quote: All the serovar Meleagridis isolated from wild boar, cattle and the red fox, as well as both Be and Af, gave a common DNA pattern (100% similarity) of PFGE, except one (90% similarity; Fig. 1). Serovar Anatum also had an identical DNA pattern (100%) in isolates from wild boars and cattle Af, although one isolate from cattle Be was less similar (90.4%; Fig. 2).

measure_name: Wildlife–livestock interface publication count and percentage
what_it_represents: The frequency of publications for taxonomic wildlife–livestock group pairings.
measurement_method: Publications were analyzed by interfaces; only publications mentioning one disease were included for analysis of wildlife–livestock interfaces.
metric_or_unit: Publications (%)
role_in_analysis: Identification and comparison of the top three wildlife–livestock interfaces.
quantitative_result: Birds–poultry: 2,378 (17.9%); Artiodactyls–cattle: 1,570 (11.8%); Carnivorans–cattle: 1,324 (10%).
evidence_quote: Table 2. Top three wildlife–livestock interfaces including the five predominant diseases

measure_name: Long-term publication trends at top wildlife–livestock interfaces
what_it_represents: Rates of publication on diseases at the bird–poultry, artiodactyls–cattle, and carnivorans–cattle interfaces over time.
measurement_method: Piecewise models were fitted after a standard Poisson regression model to estimate long-term publication-rate trends and changepoints.
metric_or_unit: Annual growth-rate parameters (β1 and β2), changepoint year, and P value for slope change.
role_in_analysis: Testing whether publication-rate slopes changed over time for the top three interfaces.
quantitative_result: The bird–poultry and artiodactyls–cattle interfaces had significant slope changes (P <0.001), whereas carnivorans–cattle did not (P = 0.121).
evidence_quote: For each of the top three wildlife–livestock interfaces, piecewise models were fitted to estimate long-term trends in publication rates (1912–2013).

measure_name: Wildlife and domestic reservoir status of important zoonoses
what_it_represents: Whether each identified important zoonosis had a wildlife reservoir, a domestic animal reservoir, or both.
measurement_method: Information extracted from three standard textbooks and entered into an Excel database; reservoir type was recorded for each disease.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of 292 important zoonoses.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive characterization of zoonoses with wildlife and domestic animal reservoirs, including zoonoses involving both reservoir types.
quantitative_result: 82% had a wildlife reservoir, 74% had a domestic animal reservoir and 60% had both a wildlife and a domestic animal reservoir.
evidence_quote: We identified 292 important zoonoses from the literature: 82% of these had a wildlife reservoir, 74% had a domestic animal reservoir and 60% had both a wildlife and a domestic animal reservoir.
section: 3. Importance of zoonoses and the livestock‐wildlife interface — Summary of main messages

measure_name: contact rate between wild and domestic avian compartments
what_it_represents: Epidemiological interaction between wild birds and domestic avian compartments, including intensive poultry, backyard and farmed ostrich compartments.
measurement_method: Estimated using host community data.
role_in_analysis: Used to assign a risk to the interaction.
quantitative_result: The approach highlighted species or seasons at risk for domestic compartments.
evidence_quote:
With the

estimation of epidemiological interaction using host community data, I estimated the contact

rate between wild and domestic avian compartments (intensive poultry, backyard and farmed

ostrich compartments) and assigned a risk to this interaction based on dynamic and non-

measure_name: Domestic risk (DR)
what_it_represents: Epidemiological interaction between waterfowl and each of three domestic compartments during peak risk periods.
role_in_analysis: Used to rank families participating in the epidemiological interaction.
quantitative_result: The table identifies the most important families participating in the interaction during peak risk periods.
evidence_quote:
Most important families participating to the epidemiological interaction defined as domestic
risk (DR) between the waterfowl and each of the 3 domestic compartments during peak risk
period.

measure_name: CDV seroprevalence in dogs and foxes
what_it_represents: Comparison of evidence of CDV infection between domestic dogs and wild canids.
measurement_method: Serum samples were analysed using the microneutralisation test for CDV; dog and fox seropositivity was compared using a chi-square test.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%; positive/sampled) and chi-square statistic.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether CDV seropositivity differed between domestic dogs and wild foxes.
quantitative_result: CDV seroprevalence was 51 % (135/267) in dogs and 42 % (14/33) in wild canids; the difference was not significant (χ2 =1.67, d.f.=1, p=0.19).
evidence_quote: CDV seroprevalence in dogs was 51 % (135/267). Of 33 foxes that were trapped and blood-sampled, 30 were chilla foxes and only three were culpeo foxes; therefore, infection prevalence data was pooled for all wild canids sampled. CDV seroprevalence in wild canids was 42 % (14/33). When comparing the overall CDV seropositivity of dogs and foxes, no significant differences were found (χ2 =1.67, d.f.=1, p=0.19) (Table 1).

measure_name: CPV seroprevalence in dogs and foxes
what_it_represents: Comparison of evidence of CPV infection between domestic dogs and wild canids.
measurement_method: Serum samples were analysed using the haemagglutination inhibition test (HAI) for CPV; dog and fox seropositivity was compared using a chi-square test.
metric_or_unit: Seroprevalence (%; positive/sampled) and chi-square statistic.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether CPV seropositivity differed between domestic dogs and wild foxes.
quantitative_result: CPV seroprevalence was 76 % (203/267) in dogs and 49 % (16/33) in foxes; dog prevalence was significantly higher (χ2 =11.1, d.f.=1, p<0.001).
evidence_quote: CPV seroprevalence in dogs (76 %, 203/267) was significantly higher than CPV seroprevalence in foxes (49 %, 16/33) (χ2 =11.1, d.f.=1, p<0.001).

measure_name: Host distribution of identified H8N4 viruses
what_it_represents: The occurrence of H8N4 viruses in wild versus domestic avian hosts, representing the wild-domestic host relationship and reservoir distribution.
measurement_method: Hosts were summarized using virus isolation information from available sequence data.
metric_or_unit: Number of viruses (n) and percentage of identified H8N4 viruses.
role_in_analysis: Categorization of global H8Nx sequence information to assess prevalence in different bird hosts.
quantitative_result: 77.9% of the 235 identified H8N4 viruses were detected from wild ducks; 25 were identified from domestic ducks and four from chickens.
evidence_quote: Importantly, 77.9% of the 235 identified H8N4 viruses were detected from wild ducks, including mallards (Anas playtyrhynchos) (n=102), pintails (Anas acuta) (n=39), and shovelers (Anas clypeata) (n=16). A total of 25 H8N4 viruses were identified from domestic ducks, while only four viruses were detected from chickens (Fig. 1-C).
section: 3.1. Subtype combinations of H8Nx viruses and their spatial and temporal distribution in birds

measure_name: Replication and transmission of a wild bird-isolated H8N4 virus in domestic ducks and chickens
what_it_represents: Susceptibility, viral shedding, and transmission of a virus isolated from a wild bird in domestic waterfowl and chickens.
measurement_method: SPF ducks and chickens were inoculated with 10^6 EID50 virus; viral titers were determined by titration in eggs, and inoculated and contact birds were sampled by oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs.
metric_or_unit: Viral titers (log10 EID50 mL−1), days post-inoculation/contact, and HI antibody titers (log2).
role_in_analysis: Experimental comparison of infection and transmission in domestic duck and chicken hosts.
quantitative_result: Viral titers in inoculated and contact ducks ranged from 0.75 to 5.25 log10EID50 mL−1, whereas chickens had a viral titer of 0.75 log10EID50 mL−1 at 5 and 9 dpi.
evidence_quote: The transmission study results indicated that the H8N4 virus were detected in oropharyngeal and cloacal swabs of both inoculated and contact ducks, with viral titers ranging from 0.75 to 5.25 log 10EID 50 mL –1. The viral shedding period of the H8N4 virus in the inoculated and contact ducks extended to 11 dpi (Fig. 6-B).
section: 3.6. Differences in the replication and transmission of the wild bird-isolated H8N4 virus in ducks and chickens

measure_name: Domestic dog and crab-eating fox CDV sequences in phylogenetic analysis
what_it_represents: The wild-domestic relationship represented by CDV sequences from domestic dogs and wild crab-eating foxes from the Aburrá Valley.
measurement_method: Amplification and phylogenetic analysis of the Fsp coding region from rt-PCR samples.
metric_or_unit: 405 bp; eight domestic dog sequences and one crab-eating fox sequence.
role_in_analysis: Used to assess phylogenetic clustering of the domestic dog/Cerdocyon thous CDV interface within a CDV lineage.
quantitative_result: The domestic Dog/Cerdocyon thous CDV interface clustered within the South America/North America-4 lineage.
evidence_quote: For phylogenetic analysis, 405 bp of the Fsp coding region was evaluated and amplified from all the rt-PCR samples. Due to poor sequence quality, only eight domestic dog and one crab-eating fox CDV sequences were included in the analysis.

measure_name: AIV positivity in wild birds, duck flocks, and duck-area environment
what_it_represents: Comparison of AIV detection across the three interface compartments: wild birds, domestic ducks, and their environment.
measurement_method: Real-time RT-PCR positivity at flock and environmental-area levels, compared using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Positive flocks or areas out of sampled flocks or areas; chi-square statistic and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tests whether AIV positivity differed between domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
quantitative_result: Duck swabs were positive for 5 of 12 flocks and environmental samples for 6 of 16 areas; ducks and environment had statistically similar positivity, while both had higher positivity than wild-bird taxa.
evidence_quote: For AIV, duck swabs were positive for 5 flocks out of 12 and environmental samples for 6 areas out of 16, with 2 flocks showing positive results in their swabs conjointly with the environment of their area (Table 1). Overall, ducks and the environment presented statistically simi- lar rates of AIV positivity according to chi-square tests ­(X2 = 0, p = 1). However, both ducks and the environment presented much higher viral positive rates than did any other wild bird taxa ­(X2 = 419.9, p < 1e-10) (Figure 5).
section: Comparison of avian pathogens in the three compartments

measure_name: Coronavirus positivity in wild birds, duck flocks, and duck-area environment
what_it_represents: Comparison of coronavirus detection across domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
measurement_method: Real-time RT-PCR positivity at flock and environmental-area levels, compared using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Positive flocks or areas out of sampled flocks or areas; chi-square statistic and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tests whether coronavirus positivity differed between domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
quantitative_result: Two of five duck flocks and three of 16 environmental areas were positive; ducks and environment had similar positivity and both exceeded wild birds, in which no positives were detected.
evidence_quote: For coronaviruses, duck swabs were positive for 2 flocks out of 5 and environmental samples for 3 areas out of 16, but no duck flock was positive conjointly with envi- ronmental samples from their area (Table 1). Overall, the rates of coronavirus positivity in ducks and the environ- ment were statistically similar according to chi-square tests ­(X2 = 0.1, p = 0.7). As no wild bird was detected as positive by real-time RT‒PCR, both ducks and the environment presented significantly higher positive rates than did the wild bird taxa (­X2 = 530.2, p < 1e-10) (Figure 5).
section: Comparison of avian pathogens in the three compartments

measure_name: Chlamydia sp. positivity in wild birds, duck flocks, and duck-area environment
what_it_represents: Comparison of Chlamydia sp. detection across domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
measurement_method: Real-time PCR positivity at flock and environmental-area levels, compared using chi-square tests.
metric_or_unit: Positive flocks or areas out of sampled flocks or areas; chi-square statistic and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Tests whether Chlamydia sp. positivity differed between domestic ducks, their environment, and wild birds.
quantitative_result: Two of five duck flocks and seven of 16 environmental areas were positive; ducks and environment had similar positivity, while both had higher positivity than wild-bird taxa.
evidence_quote: For Chlamydia sp., duck swabs were positive for 2 flocks out of 5 and environmental samples for 7 areas out of 16, with one duck flock showing positive results in swabs conjoint with environmental samples of their area (Table 1). Overall, ducks and the environment presented statistically simi- lar rates of Chlamydia sp. bacterial posi- tivity according to chi-square tests (­X2 = 0, p = 1). How- ever, both ducks and the environment presented much higher bacterial positive rates than any other wild bird taxa did ­(X2 = 421.6, p < 1e-10) (Figure 5).
section: Comparison of avian pathogens in the three compartments

measure_name: D. renale cases in domestic dogs and maned wolves
what_it_represents: Occurrence of D. renale across domestic and wild canids in the same Brazilian Cerrado microregion.
measurement_method: A survey of animals with diocthymosis was conducted at the southwest of the state of Goiás for 2020-2024.
metric_or_unit: Number of recorded cases, reported by host type and municipality.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive reporting of parasite circulation in domestic and wild animals.
quantitative_result: 12 cases were recorded: nine in domestic dogs and three in maned wolves.
evidence_quote: Over the last five years, 12 cases of D. renale have been recorded in domestic and wild canids dogs, nine in domestic dogs (nSanta Rita do Araguaia=1; nMineiros=1; nSerranópolis=2; nJataí=5) and three cases in maned wolves (Chrysocyon brachyurus) (nMineiros=1; nSerranópolis=1; nJataí=1).

measure_name: Wild bird species’ favorability distributions
what_it_represents: The predicted spatial distribution of wild bird species, including species observed near poultry farms, as an exposure representing their potential contribution to HPAI spillover into poultry.
measurement_method: Species distribution models were built using a BART approach; predicted probability maps were transformed into favorability maps.
metric_or_unit: Favorability (0 to 1 in response curves)
role_in_analysis: Used as explanatory variables in univariable and final multivariable ensemble models of HPAI outbreak occurrence in poultry.
quantitative_result: Cluster 3 showed the highest average importance (Imp = 28%) and a strong positive association with emergence of new outbreaks.
evidence_quote: Cluster 3 (including most of the Pelecaniformes, the common pheasant, the black-winged stilt, and the common moorhen—Gallinula chloropus) showed the highest average importance (Imp = 28%) and a strong positive association with the emergence of new outbreaks.

measure_name: Cluster 4 wild-bird group favorability
what_it_represents: The spatial favorability of a group containing species typically considered HPAI reservoirs, specifically Anseriformes and Charadriiformes.
measurement_method: Species were grouped by cluster analysis based on highly related favorability distributions; a representative species from each cluster was used in the multivariable model.
metric_or_unit: Average importance (Imp = 17%)
role_in_analysis: Predictor group in the final multivariable outbreak-probability model.
quantitative_result: Cluster 4 had a moderate association with emergence of new outbreaks and average importance of 17%.
evidence_quote: A moderate association was also observed for Cluster 4, which accounts for the species typically considered reservoirs of the disease (i.e., Anseriformes and Charadriiformes), although its average importance is lower than Cluster 3 (Imp = 17%).

measure_name: Interface Density—ID(x,y)
what_it_represents: Density of interfaces between wild-boar-associated vegetated areas and streets/roads or urban areas, representing the probability of interaction with ASF vectors.
measurement_method: Interfaces were mapped as vector lines from intersections of vegetated areas with streets/roads or urban areas; line lengths were summed within municipality boundaries.
metric_or_unit: km ha−1
role_in_analysis: Used as V(x,y), the vulnerability component of the livestock ASF risk model; also contributes to environmental risk ER(x,y).
quantitative_result: Higher ID values were close to the north part of the AOI, with a small concentration of high ID value in the center.
evidence_quote: Moreover, the interfaces between vegetated areas and streets/roads or urban areas were mapped as vector lines. The interface density (i.e., km ha−1 ) for each municipality was computed summing line lengths within municipality boundaries.

measure_name: Total ASF risk—R(x,y)
what_it_represents: The probability that ASF negatively affects livestock pigs, combining likelihood of infected vectors, vulnerability represented by interface density, and livestock-pig impact.
measurement_method: Computed as R(x, y) = L(x, y)·V(x, y)·I(x, y), with V(x,y) identified as interface density and I(x,y) calculated as livestock pig density per municipality.
metric_or_unit: Normalized range [0;1]
role_in_analysis: Spatial risk-model outcome linking the environmental/interface component to livestock pigs.
quantitative_result: Most municipalities have a risk close to 0 because I(x,y) is low and few or zero pigs are present.
evidence_quote: where R(x,y) is the total risk, i.e., the probability that ASF negatively affects livestock pigs; L(x,y) is the likelihood, i.e., the probability to find infected vector; V(x,y) is the vulnerability, i.e., the probability to interact with a vector; and I(x,y) is the impact, i.e., the probability that a negative event affects targets (for ASF, the livestock animals).

measure_name: Animal population category (domestic versus synanthropic animals)
what_it_represents: Comparison of prioritized disease occurrence between domestic and synanthropic animal populations, representing pathogen distribution across animal domains relevant to spillover risk to wildlife.
measurement_method: qPCR and ELISA testing of sampled domestic and synanthropic animals, with disease-status comparisons using chi-square and Fisher’s exact tests.
metric_or_unit: Disease prevalence and p-value
role_in_analysis: Used to compare disease occurrence between domestic and synanthropic animals.
quantitative_result: Hemorrhagic septicemia showed a significantly higher prevalence in domestic animals (p < 0.01), whereas enterotoxemia was more prevalent in synanthropic animals.
evidence_quote: Hemorrhagic septicemia showed a significantly higher prevalence in domestic animals (p < 0.01), whereas enterotoxemia was more prevalent in synanthropic animals.

measure_name: Species
what_it_represents: Influenza A positivity and H5N1 isolates across bird species sampled in live bird markets, including domestic poultry and wild-bird species.
measurement_method: Realtime RT-PCR testing of samples, with H5N1 isolates identified by complete genome sequencing.
metric_or_unit: Total tested and positive influenza A samples, N (%); H5N1 isolates, N (%).
role_in_analysis: Epizootic variable analyzed for differences in influenza A positivity between categories using a Chi-square test.
quantitative_result: Influenza A positivity differed by species (p <0.0001); chicken samples were 162 (23.54) positive and duck samples were 36 (34.61) positive.
section: Results, 3.1. H5N1 Virus in Live Bird Markets

measure_name: Wolf range location
what_it_represents: A spatial category representing cattle farms within versus outside the range of wolves, used to assess whether wolf-associated setting was related to cattle N. caninum infection.
measurement_method: Farm sites were classified as northern farms inside or southern farms outside known wolf range; cattle seroprevalence was compared between northern and southern counties using a chi-square goodness-of-fit test.
metric_or_unit: Cumulative cattle seroprevalence (%); odds ratio and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of N. caninum infection in cattle across wolf-range categories.
quantitative_result: Northern county animals had cumulative seroprevalence of 21.3% and southern county animals had cumulative seroprevalence of 20.4%; no statistically significant difference was noted (OR = 1.06, p-value = 0.8).
evidence_quote: Using the chi-square test for goodness of fit, no statistically significant difference was noted between the number of infected cattle in northern counties versus southern counties (OR = 1.06, p-value = 0.8).

measure_name: Wildlife contact with cattle
what_it_represents: Producer-reported contact between cattle and wildlife species, representing direct wild-domestic interaction on farms.
measurement_method: Producer survey responses.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of respondents reporting contact; percentages listing wildlife species.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive quantitative representation of wildlife-cattle contact in the surveyed producer population.
quantitative_result: 69% indicated wildlife other than rodents and small birds had contact with cattle; deer were listed by 75%, birds by 50%, coyotes by 48%, and wolves by 40% of respondents living in wolf range or the fringe.
evidence_quote: Overall, 69% indicated that wildlife other than rodents and small birds had contact with cattle. The most frequently listed species were deer (75%), birds (50%), and coyotes (48%). Wolves were noted by 40% of respondents who lived either in wolf range or the fringe.

measure_name: Dog and wild-canid access on farms
what_it_represents: Farm risk categories for domestic dogs and wild canids accessing cattle housing and/or feed storage areas, representing opportunities for domestic and wild canid interaction with livestock settings.
measurement_method: On-farm risk assessment scored farms as low, moderate, or high risk based on access to cattle housing and/or feed storage areas.
metric_or_unit: Number of farms (of 10) in risk categories.
role_in_analysis: On-farm quantitative risk assessment used to characterize exposure pathways for N. caninum to cattle.
quantitative_result: Six of 10 farms scored high risk for dogs on premises, and eight of 10 farms scored high risk for wild canids on farm property.
evidence_quote: Six of 10 farms scored high risk for dogs on premises (dogs have free or occasional access to cattle housing and/or feed storage areas) and three of 10 farms scored moderate risk for dogs on premises (dogs located on premises but have no access to cattle housing and/or feed storage areas).

measure_name: Contact with wildlife
what_it_represents: Whether domestic small ruminants had contact with wildlife.
measurement_method: Recorded as a yes/no factor and evaluated in univariable regression for association with CHRV3 serological status.
metric_or_unit: Frequency (N) and seroprevalence (%) by yes/no category; p value.
role_in_analysis: Independent variable in univariable analysis of factors associated with domestic small-ruminant CHRV3 positivity.
quantitative_result: Seroprevalence was 7,58 % in both groups; p = 0.998.
evidence_quote:
Contact with wildlife Yes 356 7,58 % 0.998
No 66 7,58 %

measure_name: Flock management - seasonal grazing
what_it_represents: Flocks declared to graze in open pastoral systems in hilly and mountainous areas depending on the season; the authors interpret this grazing practice as improving interaction between wild and domestic ruminants.
measurement_method: Recorded as a yes/no flock-management factor and included in multinomial logistic regression for CHRV3 seropositivity.
metric_or_unit: Odds ratio and 95 % CI; p value.
role_in_analysis: Significant factor retained in the final multivariable logistic regression model.
quantitative_result: Flocks not grazing seasonally had OR 0.115 (95 % CI 0.043–0.307; p < 0.001) relative to seasonally grazing flocks.
evidence_quote: Finally, flocks that do not graze seasonally are less likely to have positive antibody titers than those that do seasonal grazing (p-value < 0.001) (Table 8).
section: Factors influencing positivity against CHRV3 virus in domestic small ruminants

measure_name: Shared / Pshared
what_it_represents: The number and proportion of a host's nematode parasite species shared across the wild-domestic host boundary.
measurement_method: Known host–parasite associations from databases and domestic-animal veterinary checklists were used to identify parasites reported in wild and domestic ungulates.
metric_or_unit: Number of shared parasite species and proportion of total parasite species shared.
role_in_analysis: Used to quantify parasite-species overlap between wild and domestic ungulates and to calculate liability.
quantitative_result: For goats, 29 parasite species were shared with wild ungulates and Pshared was 0.73.
evidence_quote: Shared (number of parasites shared with domestic ungulates); Pshared (proportion of total shared with domestic ungulates);

measure_name: L, the liability index
what_it_represents: A comparative index of host liability to parasite transmission across the wild-domestic boundary, based on specialized versus generalized parasite fauna.
measurement_method: A simple index was defined to compare host species according to parasite specialization versus generalization across the wild-domestic boundary.
metric_or_unit: Liability index (L).
role_in_analysis: Compared wild and domestic host species for cross-boundary parasite sharing.
quantitative_result: Goats had a liability index of 0.70, while horses had a liability index of −0.014.
evidence_quote: We define a simple index of liability to compare host species by the extent to which their parasite fauna is specialized versus generalized, i.e. crossing the wild–domestic boundary.

measure_name: Host-associated CDV H gene phylogenetic relationship
what_it_represents: The genetic relationship of marmoset-derived CDV variants to dog-derived CDV sequences, used to assess a probable domestic-dog origin and spillover into wildlife.
measurement_method: Maximum likelihood phylogenetic analysis based on CDV H gene sequences.
metric_or_unit: Phylogenetic clustering; H gene sequence relationship.
role_in_analysis: Comparison of host-associated viral sequences to infer probable domestic dog origin and subsequent spillover into local wildlife.
quantitative_result: The marmoset-and-fox clade was most closely related to dog-derived sequences from Mato Grosso and Rondônia.
evidence_quote: This combined clade was, in turn, most closely related to dog-derived sequences from nearby states of Mato Grosso and Rondônia (GenBank: MT119972-77) (Figure 5).

measure_name: H gene pairwise distance
what_it_represents: Genetic distance of the marmoset CDV variants relative to representative CDV lineages, including the fox-derived virus.
measurement_method: Pairwise distance matrix generated from H gene sequences.
metric_or_unit: Percent H gene sequence distance.
role_in_analysis: Used to determine whether the variants met the threshold for a distinct lineage.
quantitative_result: The variants were below the 5% threshold and were included in the Europe 1/South America 1 lineage.
evidence_quote: CDV strains differing by less than 5% in H gene sequences from known lineages are not considered distinct lineages [27]. Pairwise distance analysis showed that these variants fall below this threshold, supporting their inclusion in ES1 (Table 2).

measure_name: Tick-borne pathogen prevalence across host species
what_it_represents: Prevalence of tick-borne pathogens in different domestic and wildlife host species.
measurement_method: Heatmap synthesis of prevalence data from the reviewed studies.
metric_or_unit: Prevalence percentages
role_in_analysis: Descriptive comparison of pathogen prevalence across host species.
quantitative_result: Cattle exhibited several pathogens reaching prevalence values above 50%, while some impala infections exceeded 25% prevalence.
evidence_quote: Cattle (Bos taurus Linnaeus, 1758) were the most frequently sampled host species and exhibited the broadest range of pathogens.

measure_name: Tick–host and pathogen–host interaction network
what_it_represents: Connections among tick species, pathogens, and domestic and wildlife host species, including potential wildlife-to-livestock bridging.
measurement_method: Network graph constructed from the review dataset.
metric_or_unit: 13 tick–pathogen interactions, 22 pathogen–host interactions, and 15 tick–host interactions
role_in_analysis: Network analysis of overlap and potential transmission routes between hosts and vectors.
quantitative_result: R. appendiculatus was linked to domestic hosts and wildlife and was interpreted as a bridge vector between wildlife and livestock.
evidence_quote: The network captures a total of 13 tick–pathogen interactions, 22 pathogen–host interactions, and 15 tick–host interactions, indicating multiple points of overlap and potential transmission routes within the system.

measure_name: Wild or domestic carnivore
what_it_represents: Host categorization as wild carnivore or domestic carnivore.
measurement_method: Records were grouped into domestic and wild hosts.
metric_or_unit: Wild carnivore; domestic carnivore
role_in_analysis: Used to evaluate host samples and genotypes in the spatial analysis and to assess whether genetic-lineage detection was related to wild or domestic host.
quantitative_result: Belonging to Caniformia, animals were categorized as domestic, with only dogs (C. lupus familiaris) as species (42.67%) or wild (57.33%) (Table 2; Figure 2A).
evidence_quote: These data were evaluated by species suborder (Caniformia/Feliformia) and grouped into domestic and wild hosts.

measure_name: Distance to protected areas (Distance to PAs)
what_it_represents: A proxy of the wildlife/livestock interface and potential contact with wild hosts for FMDV.
measurement_method: The Euclidean distance between each animal’s homestead and the nearest boundary of the protected system was estimated via QGIS, which relies on GPS positions recorded in the field. Farms were classified as close to or far from protected areas using a 2 km threshold.
metric_or_unit: Distance in km; close (< 2 km) versus far (> 2 km).
role_in_analysis: Explanatory risk-factor variable in generalized linear mixed models of the pooled antibody-detection outcome; its interaction with species was tested.
quantitative_result: For cattle in Hwange SES, serological prevalence estimations were twice as high for cattle living less than 2 km away from a protected area than for cattle living more than 2 km away from a protected area.
evidence_quote: This variable was used as a proxy of the wildlife/livestock interface and potential contact with wild hosts for FMDV.
section: Materials and methods — Factors considered likely to generate variation in serological status

measure_name: Distance to protected areas by species
what_it_represents: Whether the relationship of FMDV serological prevalence to the wildlife/livestock interface proxy differed between cattle and goats.
measurement_method: Interaction between species and farm distance category to protected areas in the generalized mixed model.
metric_or_unit: Species × distance-to-PAs interaction; p = 0.005.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether serological prevalence varied according to distance to protected areas differently across cattle and goats.
quantitative_result: Distance to the protected area influenced serological prevalence but differently depending on the species (p = 0.005 for the interaction between distance to protected areas and species; Table 3).
evidence_quote: Distance to the protected area influenced serological prevalence but differently depending on the species (p = 0.005 for the interaction between distance to protected areas and species; Table 3).
section: Results — Variation in serological prevalence according to SES and spatial characteristics

measure_name: Total L. infantum exposure by zone across humans, dogs, and vectors
what_it_represents: The joint circulation of L. infantum among human, domestic dog, and vector domains in each urban zone.
measurement_method: Positivity was determined by IFAT and/or qPCR, and spatial clustering used a Bernoulli model.
metric_or_unit: Percent positive individuals and vectors by zone; relative risk (RR) and p-value.
role_in_analysis: Compared total exposure across Z1-Z3 and identified a high-exposure spatial cluster.
quantitative_result: Total exposure was 48.2% (67/139) in Z1, 22.2% (16/72) in Z3, and 12.2% (9/74) in Z2; the Z1 cluster had RR: 2.1 (p < 0.001).
evidence_quote: Spatial analysis showed that the distribution of exposure to L. infantum among humans, dogs, and sandflies in the urban zones (Z1-Z3) was heterogeneous. Total L. infantum exposure was significantly higher in Z1 (48.2%; 67/139) compared to Z3 (22.2%; 16/72) and Z2 (12.2%; 9/74) (p < 0.001). Furthermore, a significant spatial cluster was detected in Z1 (37.684858 N, 4.480886 W) for exposure to L. infantum in humans, dogs, and vectors (RR: 2.1; p < 0.001) (Figure 2).
section: Spatial clustering in hosts and sandflies

measure_name: L. infantum exposure in dogs and wild lagomorphs
what_it_represents: Infection/exposure patterns in domestic dogs and wild lagomorph reservoirs.
measurement_method: IFAT and/or qPCR testing of sampled hosts.
metric_or_unit: Percentage positive and number positive/number tested.
role_in_analysis: Reported comparative host-domain exposure supporting the reservoir role of wild lagomorphs in relation to dogs and human leishmaniosis.
quantitative_result: Total exposure was 73.2% (30/41) in dogs and 100% (41/41) in wild lagomorphs.
evidence_quote: Total exposure to L. infantum of individual analyzed (% positive IFAT and/or qPCR) 6.2% (9/145; 95%CI: 2.3–10.1) 73.2% (30/41; 95%CI: 59.6–86.7) 100% (41/41; 95%CI: 94.1–100)

measure_name: Host lifestyle
what_it_represents: The comparison of mammals classified as farmed versus wild, representing their differing host lifestyle and setting.
measurement_method: Samples were classified by origin: environments with frequent human interaction and antibiotic exposure, such as farms, versus designated wildlife reserves and similar environments.
metric_or_unit: 783 farmed mammals and 190 wild mammals
role_in_analysis: Grouping variable for comparisons of viral, microbial, and antibiotic-resistance patterns between farmed and wild mammals.
quantitative_result: 17 viruses were identified in both farmed and wild mammals.
evidence_quote: We identified 17 viruses in both farmed and wild mammals, including Getah virus (GETV, Alphavirus getah), RVA, canine coronavirus (CCoV, Alphacoronavirus suis), PIV5, and RbCoV HKU14 (Figure 2E).
section: RESULTS — Virome characterization in non-traditional asymptomatic mammals

measure_name: Bacterial strain-sharing events across host lifestyles
what_it_represents: The occurrence of highly similar bacterial strains shared between farmed and wild mammal lifestyles.
measurement_method: The inStrain workflow defined shared strains among known species-level genome bins using population ANI and genome-comparison thresholds.
metric_or_unit: Percentage of strain-sharing events; 7.0% across lifestyles
role_in_analysis: Quantitative characterization of potential bacterial sharing across lifestyles.
quantitative_result: Strain-sharing events across mammalian lifestyles accounted for 7.0% of the identified events.
evidence_quote: After analyzing 96,643 strain pairs, 2,558 met these criteria for strain-sharing events. In addition, we observed that bacterial strain-sharing events occurred across geographical regions (i.e., Chinese provinces) (50.1%), mammalian orders (11.1%), and lifestyles (7.0%) (Figure 3D).
section: Bacteria, fungi, and parasites in non-traditional mammals

measure_name: ARG abundance by host lifestyle
what_it_represents: The abundance of antibiotic resistance genes in farmed compared with wild mammals.
measurement_method: The resistome was characterized by mapping open reading frames against the ResFinder database; ARG abundance was compared between lifestyle groups.
metric_or_unit: Median ARG abundance; p < 0.001
role_in_analysis: Statistical comparison of resistome burden between farmed and wild mammal groups.
quantitative_result: Farmed mammals had significantly higher median ARG abundance than wild mammals across all 13 antibiotic classes.
evidence_quote: Farmed mammals exhibited a significantly higher median ARG abundance compared with wild mammals when considering the aggregate of all 13 antibiotic classes (p < 0.001; see STAR Methods section for details) (Figure S5B).
section: Putative ARGs in farmed and wild mammals

measure_name: Transmission rate from cell to herds
what_it_represents: Transmission from wild boar cells to domestic pig herds.
measurement_method: Estimated by approximate Bayesian computation in the multihost spatio-temporal model.
role_in_analysis: One of the estimated transmission-rate parameters for routes between domestic and wildlife hosts.
quantitative_result: The beta that governed the rate of transmission from cells to herds (β2) appeared to have a relatively wide 95% credible interval.
evidence_quote: β : Transmission rate from cell to herds Estimated 0.2363 (0.0074, 0.5752)

measure_name: Transmission rate from herd to cell
what_it_represents: Transmission from domestic pig herds to wild boar cells.
measurement_method: Estimated by approximate Bayesian computation in the multihost spatio-temporal model.
role_in_analysis: One of the estimated transmission-rate parameters for routes between domestic and wildlife hosts.
quantitative_result: The transmission rate from herds to cells (β3 = 0.1631 (95% CI 0.0100, 0.3828)) was similar to that of cells to cells (β4 = 0.1315 ((0.0051, 0.3724)), though the betas for both the between-herd transmission rate (β1) and the transmission rate from the effect of the international border (β5) were 10-fold lower than others.
evidence_quote: β : Transmission rate from herd to cell Estimated 0.1631 (0.0100, 0.3828)

measure_name: Degree of interaction with human environments
what_it_represents: The domestic–wildlife interface involving domestic dogs and captive, synanthropic, and elusive species.
measurement_method: Extracted as a host ecological and behavioural variable; Table 1 records contact with human environments as Yes or No.
metric_or_unit: Categorical: Yes, No.
role_in_analysis: Used descriptively to compare vaccine-related CDV isolates and sequences in domestic–wild interface habitats by genotype.
quantitative_result: America-1 genotypes had 21 cases and Rockborn-like had 7 cases in species living in habitats at the domestic–wild interface.
evidence_quote: Finally, the presence of vaccine-related CDV isolates and sequences is particularly notable in species living in habitats at the domestic–wild interface, being high in America-1 genotypes (21 cases) and also relevant in Rockborn-like (7 cases), reinforcing the hypothesis of favoured transmission in areas of interspecific contact between wild hosts and domestic hosts (dogs) or wild hosts in captivity (Figure 3E).
section: 3.2. Descriptive Epidemiology of CD Due to Strains of Vaccine Origin

measure_name: Host functional group and potential transmission connections
what_it_represents: Transmission relationships among domestic dogs, captive carnivores, synanthropic mesocarnivores, and wild non-synanthropic carnivores.
measurement_method: Potential connections were generated from temporally compatible genotype records, filtered using plausibility criteria, and classified into seven epidemiological plausibility levels; connection frequencies between origin and destination functional groups were analysed.
metric_or_unit: Number of connections; ordinal potentiality scale from 1 (highest plausibility) to 7 (lowest).
role_in_analysis: Used in statistical tests of whether dispersion plausibility differed by origin and destination host functional group and in directional/spatial analyses.
quantitative_result: For America-1 connections, potentiality differed significantly by host functional group at origin (H = 18.04, p = 0.00043) and destination (H = 100.93, p < 0.001).
evidence_quote: A Kruskal–Wallis H-test (Table S4, Supplementary File S4) revealed significant differences in the level of potentiality according to the host functional group in America-1 connections, both when acting as origin (H = 18.04, p = 0.00043) and destination (H = 100.93, p < 0.001).

measure_name: Spatial association between B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs
what_it_represents: Spatial concordance between infection prevalence in the wild-boar and domestic-pig populations, based on prevalence estimates transferred between sampling locations of the two host populations.
measurement_method: Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) interpolation was conducted separately for wild boar and pig farm datasets; interpolated prevalence values from one host population were assigned to sampling points of the other host population, followed by correlation/regression analysis.
metric_or_unit: B. suis prevalence values; regression correlation with p-value < 0.05.
role_in_analysis: Used to investigate potential spatial associations and potential epidemiological links or shared environmental risk factors between wild boar and domestic pigs.
quantitative_result: A regression analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation (p-value < 0.05) between the spatial distributions of B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs.
evidence_quote: A regression analysis revealed a statistically significant positive correlation (p-value < 0.05) between the spatial distributions of B. suis prevalence in wild boar and domestic pigs (Fig. 8).

measure_name: Genome-wide nucleotide identity of the wild-boar PCV3 strain relative to domestic-pig PCV3 sequences
what_it_represents: Genetic homology between PCV3 detected in a wild boar and PCV3 sequences identified in domestic pigs.
measurement_method: Genetic analysis of complete PCV3 genome sequences; sequences were aligned using the ClustalW algorithm and analyzed phylogenetically.
metric_or_unit: Percent nucleotide similarity / genome-wide identity
role_in_analysis: Cross-host genomic comparison used to interpret a potential epidemiological connection and potential viral transmission between wild boars and domestic pigs.
quantitative_result: The wild-boar strain had 98.9 to 99.1% similarity with domestic-pig PCV3 sequences from China and up to 99.1% genome-wide identity with a sequence from domestic pigs in Nanjing.
evidence_quote: Further genetic analysis showed that PCV3/CN/Nanjing/WB/2021 exhibited 98.9% nucleotide similarity with PCV3 genomes retrieved from wild boars in Brazil (MT075517, MT075518, and MT075519) and 98.9 to 99.1% similarity with PCV3 sequences identified in domestic pigs in China (MK580468, MF069116, and MH491016).
section: Results, 3.4. Sequence Analysis of PCV3 in Wild Boar Samples

measure_name: bi-weekly estimates of relative abundance of waterfowl species
what_it_represents: Waterfowl abundance in the landscape associated with poultry-operation spillover risk.
measurement_method: Data were available weekly; the authors used the natural log of abundance averaged for each two-week period and summed values for all species within each group.
metric_or_unit: Relative abundance; z-standardized continuous covariate in the model.
role_in_analysis: Environmental covariate selected for the final Renv model of relative HPAI spillover risk.
quantitative_result: Increased waterfowl abundance was associated with increased spillover risk (β = 0.422, 0.337–0.507 95 % C.I.).
evidence_quote: The final Renv model indicated increasing risk with decreasing temperatures (β = − 1.242, − 1.372 to − 1.112 95 % C.I.), increased precipitation (β = 0.642, 0.553–0.731 95 % C.I.), and increased waterfowl abundance (β = 0.422, 0.337–0.507 95 % C.I.).

measure_name: whether wild birds had access to the litter before use
what_it_represents: A binary farm-level condition of wild-bird access to fresh litter before its use at the poultry farm.
measurement_method: Case-control questionnaire covariate included in the top-performing model.
metric_or_unit: Binary covariate; regression coefficient β with 95 % confidence interval.
role_in_analysis: Biosecurity covariate in the top-performing model describing relative spillover risk.
evidence_quote: The top performing model describing relative spillover risk included binary covariates describing whether farms used fresh litter (i. e., bedding) (Fig. 3A; ΔWAIC = 0; β = − 1.041, − 1.635 to − 0.447 95 % C.I.), whether fresh litter was heat treated before delivery onto the farm (β = − 3.158, − 3.7172 to − 2.600 95 % C.I.), and whether wild birds had access to the litter before use (β = − 0.089, − 0.627–0.806 95 % C.I.).

measure_name: Relative transmission risk (RR)
what_it_represents: Relative risk of an avian influenza spillover event between wild birds and domestic poultry operations.
measurement_method: Calculated as the estimated number of infected waterfowl at a given time and place multiplied by the number of poultry operations in that location weighted by their risk of a spillover event occurring.
metric_or_unit: Relative transmission risk; modeled at ~2.96 km² and county spatial scales.
role_in_analysis: Primary modeled outcome, mapped weekly and validated against wild-bird spillover events into poultry flocks.
quantitative_result: For all poultry at the county level, the full model had AUC 0.84 and Spearman’s correlation coefficient (Rho) 0.58.
evidence_quote:
The risk of such a spillover event can be modeled as the relative transmission risk (RR) between wild birds and domestic poultry operations using the following equations:
RR = W × P (1)

measure_name: Estimated number of infected waterfowl (W)
what_it_represents: The wild-waterfowl component of spillover risk at a given time and place.
measurement_method: Derived from relative abundance of waterfowl by species (Was) and the percentage predicted positive with AIVs (Wps).
metric_or_unit: Relative abundance multiplied by predicted percentage positive with AIVs.
role_in_analysis: Component of relative transmission risk; separately assessed in model validation.
quantitative_result: The validation model containing only the number of infected waterfowl had AUC 0.81 and Rho 0.54 for all poultry.
evidence_quote: where W is the estimated number of infected waterfowl present at a given time and place and P is the number of poultry operations in that location weighted by their risk of a spillover event occurring.

measure_name: Number and risk-weighted type of poultry operations (P)
what_it_represents: The domestic-poultry component of spillover risk, incorporating operation count and relative risk by poultry operation type.
measurement_method: Pnt is the number of poultry operations of type t, multiplied by Prt, the relative risk associated with each operation type.
metric_or_unit: Number of operations weighted by relative risk.
role_in_analysis: Component of relative transmission risk; poultry relative risk and count of poultry facilities were separately evaluated in validation.
quantitative_result: For all poultry, poultry relative risk had AUC 0.63 and Rho 0.21, while count of poultry facilities had AUC 0.51 and Rho 0.01.
evidence_quote: where Was is the relative abundance of waterfowl of species s, Wps is the percentage of those waterfowl predicted to be positive with AIVs, Pnt is the number of poultry operations of a given type t, and Prt is the relative risk associated with each operation type (See Fig. 1 for graphical depiction of model components).

measure_name: Proportion of retrieved publications dealing with diseases shared with livestock
what_it_represents: The frequency of literature on diseases shared between cervid hosts and livestock.
measurement_method: Retrieved-paper review summarized in Figure 58.1.
metric_or_unit: Proportion of retrieved papers (n = 125); almost two-thirds of publications.
role_in_analysis: Descriptive analysis of the epidemiological literature concerning deer at the interface with domestic animals.

measure_name: Proportion of GPS points intersecting cattle-occupied polygons
what_it_represents: Potential cattle–deer interactions and spatial overlap between the collared mule deer and cattle pastures.
measurement_method: The deer's GPS locations were intersected with static polygons representing cattle-occupied pastures over the last 50 days of the deer's life.
metric_or_unit: Proportion of GPS points; percentage.
role_in_analysis: Used to identify times and locations of potential cattle–deer interactions and infer a potential spillover pathway.
quantitative_result: Approximately 16.5% of GPS points intersected occupied cattle pastures; during peak overlap, the deer spent an average of 29% of the day within cattle pastures.
evidence_quote: Approximately 16.5% of GPS points recorded during the 50 days prior to mortality intersected with occupied cattle pastures (83.5% were recorded outside; Figure 3A). Peak deer–pas- ture overlap occurred between 3 and 6 weeks prior to death (Figure 3B), during which the deer spent an average of 29% of the day within cattle pastures.

measure_name: Spatiotemporal overlap of wild-duck utilization distributions (UDs) and HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks
what_it_represents: The wild duck–infected poultry transmission interface, represented by poultry outbreaks occurring within tracked duck home-range utilization distributions relative to outbreaks outside those distributions.
measurement_method: Satellite telemetry data were used to generate 14-day, three-dimensional UDs; poultry outbreak data were compared inside versus outside each UD, within a minimum convex polygon (MCP), using 1-sample exact binomial tests.
metric_or_unit: Number and proportion of poultry outbreaks inside versus outside UDs by 14-day period; percentage of UDs significantly associated with poultry outbreaks.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether poultry outbreaks overlapped duck UDs more than expected from the relative UD area within the MCP, and compared overlap by season and species.
quantitative_result: During the spring migration, a larger proportion of the utilization distributions of both Common Teal (23.1%) and Common Shelduck (27.3%) significantly overlapped with H5N1-infected poultry.
evidence_quote: During the spring migration, a larger proportion of the utilization distributions of both Common Teal (23.1%) and Common Shelduck (27.3%) significantly overlapped with H5N1-infected poultry (Supplementary Table S6).
